The anterior pituitary (pars distalis) synthesizes and secretes six trophic/peptide hormones: growth hormone (GH), prolactin (PRL), thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), luteinizing hormone (LH), and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH). In contrast, oxytocin and vasopressin (ADH) are synthesized by the neurosecretory cells of the hypothalamus and transported axonally to the posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis) for storage and release.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, oxytocin is not secreted by the anterior pituitary; it is released from the posterior pituitary.

चरण 1: सैद्धांतिक सिद्धांत
पीयूष ग्रंथि को शारीरिक रूप से एडिनोहाइपोफाइसिस (जिसमें पार्स डिस्टैलिस, जिसे सामान्यतः अग्र पीयूष ग्रंथि कहा जाता है, और पार्स इंटरमीडिया शामिल हैं) तथा न्यूरोहाइपोफाइसिस (पश्च पीयूष ग्रंथि) में विभाजित किया जाता है।

चरण 2: हार्मोन उत्पत्ति का मूल्यांकन
अग्र पीयूष ग्रंथि (पार्स डिस्टैलिस) छह हार्मोनों का संश्लेषण और स्राव करती है: वृद्धि हार्मोन (GH), प्रोलैक्टिन (PRL), थायरॉइड-प्रेरक हार्मोन (TSH), एड्रीनोकॉर्टिकोट्रॉपिक हार्मोन (ACTH), ल्यूटिनाइजिंग हार्मोन (LH), और पुटिका-प्रेरक हार्मोन (FSH)। इसके विपरीत, ऑक्सीटोसिन और वैसोप्रेसिन (ADH) का संश्लेषण हाइपोथैलेमस की तंत्रिकास्रावी कोशिकाओं द्वारा होता है और इन्हें संग्रहण तथा विमोचन के लिए पश्च पीयूष ग्रंथि (न्यूरोहाइपोफाइसिस) में भेजा जाता है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अतः ऑक्सीटोसिन अग्र पीयूष ग्रंथि द्वारा स्रावित नहीं होता है; यह पश्च पीयूष ग्रंथि से मुक्त होता है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICALCOORDINATIONANDINTEGRATION_MCQ_Q03 - Hormones responsible for stress response before interview

questiontext.text:
3. Mary is about to face an interview. But during the first five minutes before the interview she experiences sweating, increased rate of heart beat, respiration etc. Which of the following hormones are responsible for her restlessness?

3. मैरी एक साक्षात्कार का सामना करने वाली है। लेकिन साक्षात्कार से पहले के शुरुआती पाँच मिनटों के दौरान उसे पसीना आना, हृदय गति बढ़ना, श्वसन दर बढ़ना आदि का अनुभव होता है। उसकी इस बेचैनी के लिए निम्नलिखित में से कौन-से हार्मोन उत्तरदायी हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
During acute stress or emergency situations, the sympathetic nervous system stimulates the adrenal medulla to rapidly release catecholamines into the bloodstream.

Step 2: Application to the Given Situation
The adrenal medulla secretes two hormones called adrenaline (epinephrine) and noradrenaline (norepinephrine), commonly known as emergency hormones or hormones of fight or flight. They increase alertness, pupilary dilation, piloerection, sweating, heart beat, strength of heart contraction, and the rate of respiration.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The physiological symptoms experienced by Mary—sweating, increased heart rate, and increased respiration—are caused by adrenaline and noradrenaline.

चरण 1: सैद्धांतिक सिद्धांत
तीव्र तनाव या आपातकालीन स्थितियों के दौरान, अनुकंपी तंत्रिका तंत्र अधिवृक्क मध्यांश (एड्रीनल मेडुला) को रक्तप्रवाह में तेजी से कैटेकोलामीन मुक्त करने के लिए प्रेरित करता है।

चरण 2: दी गई स्थिति पर अनुप्रयोग
अधिवृक्क मध्यांश एड्रीनलीन (एपिनेफ्रीन) और नॉरएड्रीनलीन (नॉरएपिनेफ्रीन) नामक दो हार्मोनों का स्राव करता है, जिन्हें सामान्यतः आपातकालीन हार्मोन या 'लड़ो या भागो' के हार्मोन कहा जाता है। ये सतर्कता, पुतली का फैलना, रोंगटे खड़े होना, पसीना आना, हृदय गति, हृदय संकुचन की शक्ति और श्वसन दर को बढ़ाते हैं।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
मैरी द्वारा अनुभव किए गए शारीरिक लक्षण—पसीना आना, हृदय गति बढ़ना और श्वसन दर बढ़ना—एड्रीनलीन और नॉरएड्रीनलीन के कारण होते हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICALCOORDINATIONANDINTEGRATION_MCQ_Q04 - Steroid responsible for water and electrolyte balance

questiontext.text:
4. The steroid responsible for balance of water and electrolytes in our body is

4. हमारे शरीर में जल और विद्युत-अपघट्यों (इलेक्ट्रोलाइट्स) के संतुलन के लिए उत्तरदायी स्टेरॉयड है

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Corticoids secreted by the adrenal cortex that regulate the balance of water and electrolytes in the body are called mineralocorticoids.

Step 2: Evaluation
Aldosterone is the main mineralocorticoid in the human body. It acts mainly at the renal tubules and stimulates the reabsorption of \(\text{Na}^+\) and water, as well as the excretion of \(\text{K}^+\) and phosphate ions, thereby maintaining electrolytes, body fluid volume, osmotic pressure, and blood pressure. Insulin and melatonin are non-steroid hormones, while testosterone is an androgen responsible for male sexual development.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The steroid hormone responsible for water and electrolyte balance is aldosterone.

चरण 1: सैद्धांतिक सिद्धांत
अधिवृक्क वल्कुट (एड्रीनल कॉर्टेक्स) द्वारा स्रावित वे कॉर्टिकॉइड्स जो शरीर में जल और विद्युत-अपघट्यों के संतुलन को नियंत्रित करते हैं, मिनरलोकॉर्टिकॉइड्स कहलाते हैं।

चरण 2: मूल्यांकन
एल्डोस्टेरोन मानव शरीर में मुख्य मिनरलोकॉर्टिकॉइड है। यह मुख्य रूप से वृक्क नलिकाओं पर कार्य करता है और \(\text{Na}^+\) तथा जल के पुनःअवशोषण एवं \(\text{K}^+\) तथा फॉस्फेट आयनों के उत्सर्जन को प्रेरित करता है, जिससे विद्युत-अपघट्य, शरीर के द्रव का आयतन, परासरणी दाब और रक्तदाब बना रहता है। इंसुलिन और मेलाटोनिन गैर-स्टेरॉयड हार्मोन हैं, जबकि टेस्टोस्टेरोन एक एंड्रोजन है जो नर लैंगिक विकास के लिए उत्तरदायी है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
जल और विद्युत-अपघट्यों के संतुलन के लिए उत्तरदायी स्टेरॉयड हार्मोन एल्डोस्टेरोन है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICALCOORDINATIONANDINTEGRATION_MCQ_Q05 - Role of thymosin in immune system

questiontext.text:
5. Thymosin is responsible for

5. थायमोसिन किसके लिए उत्तरदायी है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The thymus gland plays a major role in the development of the immune system by secreting peptide hormones called thymosins.

Step 2: Evaluation
Thymosins play a major role in the differentiation of T-lymphocytes, which provide cell-mediated immunity. In addition, thymosins also promote production of antibodies to provide humoral immunity. Blood sugar level is regulated primarily by insulin and glucagon, blood calcium level by parathyroid hormone and thyrocalcitonin, and RBC production by erythropoietin.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thymosin is responsible for the differentiation of T lymphocytes.

चरण 1: सैद्धांतिक सिद्धांत
थाइमस ग्रंथि थायमोसिन नामक पेप्टाइड हार्मोनों का स्राव करके प्रतिरक्षा तंत्र के विकास में प्रमुख भूमिका निभाती है।

चरण 2: मूल्यांकन
थायमोसिन T-लिम्फोसाइट्स के विभेदन में प्रमुख भूमिका निभाते हैं, जो कोशिका-माध्यित प्रतिरक्षा प्रदान करते हैं। इसके अतिरिक्त, थायमोसिन तरल (ह्यूमरल) प्रतिरक्षा प्रदान करने के लिए प्रतिरक्षियों (एंटीबॉडी) के उत्पादन को भी बढ़ावा देते हैं। रक्त शर्करा का स्तर मुख्य रूप से इंसुलिन और ग्लूकागॉन द्वारा, रक्त कैल्शियम का स्तर पैराथायरॉइड हार्मोन और थायरोकैल्सिटोनिन द्वारा, तथा RBC उत्पादन एरिथ्रोपोइटिन द्वारा नियंत्रित होता है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
थायमोसिन T लिम्फोसाइट्स के विभेदन के लिए उत्तरदायी है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICALCOORDINATIONANDINTEGRATION_MCQ_Q06 - Second messenger in protein hormone action

questiontext.text:
6. In the mechanism of action of a protein hormone, one of the second messengers is

6. प्रोटीन हार्मोन की क्रियाविधि में, द्वितीयक संदेशवाहकों (सेकंड मैसेंजर) में से एक है

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Protein/peptide hormones are water-soluble and cannot cross the lipid bilayer of the target cell plasma membrane. Therefore, they bind to membrane-bound receptors.

Step 2: Mechanism
Binding of a protein hormone to its membrane-bound receptor normally triggers the generation of intracellular second messengers such as cyclic AMP (cAMP), inositol triphosphate (\(\text{IP}_3\)), or \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\), which in turn regulate cellular metabolism. Insulin, \(\text{T}_3\), and gastrin are hormones (primary messengers), not second messengers.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Cyclic AMP is one of the second messengers in the mechanism of action of a protein hormone.

चरण 1: सैद्धांतिक सिद्धांत
प्रोटीन/पेप्टाइड हार्मोन जल-विलेय होते हैं और लक्ष्य कोशिका की प्लाज्मा झिल्ली के लिपिड द्विस्तर को पार नहीं कर सकते। इसलिए, वे झिल्ली-बद्ध ग्राहियों (रिसेप्टर्स) से जुड़ते हैं।

चरण 2: क्रियाविधि
प्रोटीन हार्मोन का अपने झिल्ली-बद्ध ग्राही से जुड़ना सामान्यतः कोशिका के भीतर द्वितीयक संदेशवाहकों जैसे चक्रीय AMP (cAMP), इनोसिटॉल ट्राइफॉस्फेट (\(\text{IP}_3\)), या \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) के निर्माण को प्रेरित करता है, जो आगे कोशिकीय उपापचय को नियंत्रित करते हैं। इंसुलिन, \(\text{T}_3\) और गैस्ट्रिन हार्मोन (प्राथमिक संदेशवाहक) हैं, न कि द्वितीयक संदेशवाहक।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
प्रोटीन हार्मोन की क्रियाविधि में चक्रीय AMP एक द्वितीयक संदेशवाहक है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICALCOORDINATIONANDINTEGRATION_MCQ_Q07 - Hormones produced by Leydig cells

questiontext.text:
7. Leydig cells produce a group of hormones called

7. लीडिग कोशिकाएँ किस हार्मोन समूह का उत्पादन करती हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The testis consists of seminiferous tubules and stromal or interstitial tissue.

Step 2: Evaluation
The Leydig cells (or interstitial cells), which are present in the intertubular spaces of the testis, produce a group of male sex hormones called androgens, mainly testosterone. Estrogens are produced mainly by ovarian follicles, aldosterone by the adrenal cortex, and gonadotropins (LH and FSH) by the anterior pituitary.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Leydig cells produce a group of hormones called androgens.

चरण 1: सैद्धांतिक सिद्धांत
वृषण में शुक्रजनक नलिकाएँ और भरण या अंतराली ऊतक होते हैं।

चरण 2: मूल्यांकन
वृषण के अंतरानलिकीय अवकाशों में उपस्थित लीडिग कोशिकाएँ (या अंतराली कोशिकाएँ) एंड्रोजन नामक नर लिंग हार्मोनों के समूह का उत्पादन करती हैं, जिनमें मुख्य रूप से टेस्टोस्टेरोन शामिल है। एस्ट्रोजन मुख्य रूप से अंडाशयी पुटिकाओं द्वारा, एल्डोस्टेरोन अधिवृक्क वल्कुट द्वारा और गोनैडोट्रॉपिन (LH और FSH) अग्र पीयूष ग्रंथि द्वारा उत्पादित होते हैं।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
लीडिग कोशिकाएँ एंड्रोजन नामक हार्मोन समूह का उत्पादन करती हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICALCOORDINATIONANDINTEGRATION_MCQ_Q08 - Hormone secreted by corpus luteum

questiontext.text:
8. Corpus luteum secretes a hormone called

8. कॉर्पस ल्यूटियम किस हार्मोन का स्राव करता है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
After ovulation, the ruptured Graafian follicle in the ovary transforms into a temporary endocrine structure called the corpus luteum.

Step 2: Evaluation
The corpus luteum secretes mainly progesterone, which supports pregnancy and acts on the mammary glands to stimulate the formation of alveoli and milk secretion. Prolactin is secreted by the anterior pituitary, aldosterone by the adrenal cortex, and testosterone by the Leydig cells of the testis.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Corpus luteum secretes the hormone progesterone.

चरण 1: सैद्धांतिक सिद्धांत
अंडोत्सर्ग (ओव्यूलेशन) के बाद, अंडाशय में फटी हुई ग्राफी पुटिका कॉर्पस ल्यूटियम नामक एक अस्थायी अंतःस्रावी संरचना में बदल जाती है।

चरण 2: मूल्यांकन
कॉर्पस ल्यूटियम मुख्य रूप से प्रोजेस्टेरोन का स्राव करता है, जो गर्भावस्था को बनाए रखता है और स्तन ग्रंथियों पर कार्य करके कूपिकाओं (एल्विओलाई) के निर्माण तथा दुग्ध स्राव को प्रेरित करता है। प्रोलैक्टिन अग्र पीयूष ग्रंथि द्वारा, एल्डोस्टेरोन अधिवृक्क वल्कुट द्वारा और टेस्टोस्टेरोन वृषण की लीडिग कोशिकाओं द्वारा स्रावित होता है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
कॉर्पस ल्यूटियम प्रोजेस्टेरोन नामक हार्मोन का स्राव करता है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICALCOORDINATIONANDINTEGRATION_MCQ_Q09 - Endocrine gland secreting cortisol

questiontext.text:
9. Cortisol is secreted by

9. कॉर्टिसोल किसके द्वारा स्रावित होता है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The adrenal gland is composed of two types of tissues: the centrally located adrenal medulla and the outer adrenal cortex.

Step 2: Evaluation
The adrenal cortex secretes many hormones, commonly called corticoids. Corticoids involved in carbohydrate metabolism are called glucocorticoids, and in our body, cortisol is the main glucocorticoid (secreted primarily by the zona fasciculata of the adrenal cortex). Pancreas secretes insulin and glucagon, thyroid secretes thyroxine and calcitonin, and thymus secretes thymosins.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Cortisol is secreted by the adrenal gland.

चरण 1: सैद्धांतिक सिद्धांत
अधिवृक्क (एड्रीनल) ग्रंथि दो प्रकार के ऊतकों से बनी होती है: केंद्र में स्थित अधिवृक्क मध्यांश (एड्रीनल मेडुला) और बाहरी अधिवृक्क वल्कुट (एड्रीनल कॉर्टेक्स)।

चरण 2: मूल्यांकन
अधिवृक्क वल्कुट कई हार्मोनों का स्राव करता है, जिन्हें सामान्यतः कॉर्टिकॉइड्स कहा जाता है। कार्बोहाइड्रेट उपापचय में शामिल कॉर्टिकॉइड्स को ग्लूकोकॉर्टिकॉइड्स कहते हैं, और हमारे शरीर में कॉर्टिसोल मुख्य ग्लूकोकॉर्टिकॉइड है (जो मुख्यतः अधिवृक्क वल्कुट के जोना फैसिकुलाटा द्वारा स्रावित होता है)। अग्न्याशय इंसुलिन और ग्लूकागॉन का, थायरॉइड थायरॉक्सिन और कैल्सिटोनिन का, तथा थाइमस थायमोसिन का स्राव करता है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
कॉर्टिसोल अधिवृक्क (एड्रीनल) ग्रंथि द्वारा स्रावित होता है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICALCOORDINATIONANDINTEGRATION_MCQ_Q10 - Hormone regulating normal sleep-wake cycle

questiontext.text:
10. A hormone responsible for normal sleep-wake cycle is

10. सामान्य सोने-जागने के चक्र के लिए उत्तरदायी हार्मोन है

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The pineal gland, located on the dorsal side of the forebrain, regulates the 24-hour (diurnal) rhythm of our body.

Step 2: Evaluation
The pineal gland secretes the hormone melatonin, which plays a very important role in the regulation of a 24-hour diurnal rhythm of our body, such as maintaining the normal rhythms of the sleep-wake cycle and body temperature. Epinephrine is involved in emergency responses, gastrin stimulates gastric juice secretion, and insulin regulates blood glucose levels.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Melatonin is the hormone responsible for maintaining the normal sleep-wake cycle.

चरण 1: सैद्धांतिक सिद्धांत
अग्रमस्तिष्क के पृष्ठीय भाग पर स्थित पीनियल ग्रंथि हमारे शरीर की 24 घंटे की (दैनिक) लय को नियंत्रित करती है।

चरण 2: मूल्यांकन
पीनियल ग्रंथि मेलाटोनिन हार्मोन का स्राव करती है, जो हमारे शरीर की 24 घंटे की दैनिक लय को नियंत्रित करने में बहुत महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाता है, जैसे सोने-जागने के चक्र की सामान्य लय और शरीर के तापमान को बनाए रखना। एपिनेफ्रीन आपातकालीन अनुक्रियाओं में शामिल होता है, गैस्ट्रिन जठर रस के स्राव को प्रेरित करता है, और इंसुलिन रक्त शर्करा के स्तर को नियंत्रित करता है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
सामान्य सोने-जागने के चक्र को बनाए रखने के लिए उत्तरदायी हार्मोन मेलाटोनिन है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICALCOORDINATIONANDINTEGRATION_MCQ_Q11 - Location of receptors for protein hormones

questiontext.text:
11. Hormones are called chemical signals that stimulate specific target tissues. Their action depends on the presence of receptors on the respective target tissues. Which of the following is the correct location of the receptors in the case of protein hormones?

11. हार्मोनों को रासायनिक संकेत कहा जाता है जो विशिष्ट लक्ष्य ऊतकों को प्रेरित करते हैं। उनकी क्रिया संबंधित लक्ष्य ऊतकों पर ग्राहियों (रिसेप्टर्स) की उपस्थिति पर निर्भर करती है। प्रोटीन हार्मोनों के मामले में ग्राहियों का सही स्थान निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Hormones produce their effects on target tissues by binding to specific proteins called hormone receptors located in the target tissues only.

Step 2: Evaluation
Protein, peptide, and polypeptide hormones are water-soluble and lipid-insoluble, so they cannot pass through the lipid bilayer of the cell membrane. Consequently, their receptors are located on the cell membrane (plasma membrane) of the target cells (membrane-bound receptors). In contrast, steroid hormones and iodothyronines are lipid-soluble and bind to intracellular receptors (mostly nuclear receptors).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
In the case of protein hormones, the receptors are located on the plasma membrane.

चरण 1: सैद्धांतिक सिद्धांत
हार्मोन केवल लक्ष्य ऊतकों में स्थित हार्मोन ग्राही (रिसेप्टर) नामक विशिष्ट प्रोटीनों से जुड़कर लक्ष्य ऊतकों पर अपना प्रभाव उत्पन्न करते हैं।

चरण 2: मूल्यांकन
प्रोटीन, पेप्टाइड और पॉलीपेप्टाइड हार्मोन जल-विलेय और लिपिड-अविलेय होते हैं, इसलिए वे कोशिका झिल्ली के लिपिड द्विस्तर को पार नहीं कर सकते। परिणामस्वरूप, उनके ग्राही लक्ष्य कोशिकाओं की कोशिका झिल्ली (प्लाज्मा झिल्ली) पर स्थित होते हैं (झिल्ली-बद्ध ग्राही)। इसके विपरीत, स्टेरॉयड हार्मोन और आयोडोथायरोनिन लिपिड-विलेय होते हैं और अंतःकोशिकीय ग्राहियों (मुख्यतः नाभिकीय ग्राहियों) से जुड़ते हैं।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
प्रोटीन हार्मोनों के मामले में, ग्राही प्लाज्मा झिल्ली पर स्थित होते हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICALCOORDINATIONANDINTEGRATION_MCQ_Q12 - Match hormones with their physiological functions

questiontext.text:
12. Choose the correct option among the following options

Column IColumn II
A. Epinephrinei. Stimulates muscle growth
B. Testosteroneii. Decrease in blood pressure
C. Glucagoniii. Breakdown of liver glycogen content
D. Atrial natriuretic factoriv. Increases heart beat

12. निम्नलिखित विकल्पों में से सही विकल्प चुनिए

स्तंभ Iस्तंभ II
A. एपिनेफ्रीनi. पेशीय वृद्धि को प्रेरित करता है
B. टेस्टोस्टेरोनii. रक्तदाब में कमी
C. ग्लूकागॉनiii. यकृत ग्लाइकोजन की मात्रा का विघटन
D. अलिंद नैट्रियूरेटिक कारक (ANF)iv. हृदय की धड़कन बढ़ाता है

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Different hormones exert specific physiological actions on target organs to maintain homeostasis and regulate metabolism, cardiovascular function, and growth.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Hormone and Function
Epinephrine increases heart beat, the strength of heart contraction, and the rate of respiration during emergency situations. Testosterone produces anabolic (synthetic) effects on protein and carbohydrate metabolism and stimulates muscle growth. Glucagon acts mainly on the liver cells (hepatocytes) and stimulates glycogenolysis (breakdown of liver glycogen content), resulting in increased blood sugar. Atrial natriuretic factor (ANF) is secreted by the atrial wall of the heart when blood pressure increases; it causes dilation of blood vessels and decreases blood pressure.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct match is Epinephrine with Increases heart beat, Testosterone with Stimulates muscle growth, Glucagon with Breakdown of liver glycogen content, and Atrial natriuretic factor with Decrease in blood pressure (A-iv, B-i, C-iii, D-ii).

चरण 1: सैद्धांतिक सिद्धांत
विभिन्न हार्मोन समस्थापन बनाए रखने तथा उपापचय, हृदय-संवहनी कार्य और वृद्धि को नियंत्रित करने के लिए लक्ष्य अंगों पर विशिष्ट शारीरिक क्रियाएँ करते हैं।

चरण 2: प्रत्येक हार्मोन और उसके कार्य का मूल्यांकन
एपिनेफ्रीन आपातकालीन स्थितियों के दौरान हृदय की धड़कन, हृदय संकुचन की शक्ति और श्वसन दर को बढ़ाता है। टेस्टोस्टेरोन प्रोटीन और कार्बोहाइड्रेट उपापचय पर उपचयी (एनाबॉलिक) प्रभाव डालता है और पेशीय वृद्धि को प्रेरित करता है। ग्लूकागॉन मुख्य रूप से यकृत कोशिकाओं (हेपेटोसाइट्स) पर कार्य करता है और ग्लाइकोजेनोलिसिस (यकृत ग्लाइकोजन की मात्रा का विघटन) को प्रेरित करता है, जिससे रक्त शर्करा बढ़ती है। अलिंद नैट्रियूरेटिक कारक (ANF) रक्तदाब बढ़ने पर हृदय की अलिंद भित्ति द्वारा स्रावित होता है; यह रक्त वाहिकाओं को फैलाता है और रक्तदाब में कमी लाता है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
सही मिलान एपिनेफ्रीन का हृदय की धड़कन बढ़ाना, टेस्टोस्टेरोन का पेशीय वृद्धि को प्रेरित करना, ग्लूकागॉन का यकृत ग्लाइकोजन की मात्रा का विघटन और अलिंद नैट्रियूरेटिक कारक का रक्तदाब में कमी (A-iv, B-i, C-iii, D-ii) है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICALCOORDINATIONANDINTEGRATION_MCQ_Q13 - Factor not involved in calcium balance

questiontext.text:
13. Which of the following do not play any role in calcium balance in the human body?

13. निम्नलिखित में से कौन मानव शरीर में कैल्शियम संतुलन में कोई भूमिका नहीं निभाता है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Calcium homeostasis in the human body is tightly regulated by hormones and vitamin derivatives that control calcium absorption in the intestine, reabsorption in the kidneys, and deposition or resorption in bones.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Factor
Vitamin D increases intestinal absorption of calcium ions. Parathyroid hormone (PTH) is a hypercalcemic hormone that increases blood \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) levels by stimulating bone resorption, renal reabsorption of \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\), and \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) absorption from digested food. Thyrocalcitonin (TCT) is a hypocalcemic hormone secreted by the thyroid gland that lowers blood calcium levels by promoting calcium deposition in bones. In contrast, thymosin is secreted by the thymus gland and plays a major role in the differentiation of T-lymphocytes and immune function, having no role in calcium balance.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thymosin does not play any role in calcium balance in the human body.

चरण 1: सैद्धांतिक सिद्धांत
मानव शरीर में कैल्शियम समस्थापन को उन हार्मोनों और विटामिन व्युत्पन्नों द्वारा सख्ती से नियंत्रित किया जाता है जो आंत में कैल्शियम अवशोषण, वृक्क में पुनःअवशोषण तथा अस्थियों में निक्षेपण या अवशोषण को नियंत्रित करते हैं।

चरण 2: प्रत्येक कारक का मूल्यांकन
विटामिन D कैल्शियम आयनों के आंत्रीय अवशोषण को बढ़ाता है। पैराथायरॉइड हार्मोन (PTH) एक हाइपरकैल्सीमिक हार्मोन है जो अस्थि अवशोषण, वृक्क में \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) के पुनःअवशोषण और पचे हुए भोजन से \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) अवशोषण को प्रेरित करके रक्त \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) स्तर को बढ़ाता है। थायरोकैल्सिटोनिन (TCT) थायरॉइड ग्रंथि द्वारा स्रावित एक हाइपोकैल्सीमिक हार्मोन है जो अस्थियों में कैल्शियम निक्षेपण को बढ़ावा देकर रक्त कैल्शियम स्तर को कम करता है। इसके विपरीत, थायमोसिन थाइमस ग्रंथि द्वारा स्रावित होता है और T-लिम्फोसाइट्स के विभेदन तथा प्रतिरक्षा कार्य में प्रमुख भूमिका निभाता है; इसकी कैल्शियम संतुलन में कोई भूमिका नहीं होती है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
थायमोसिन मानव शरीर में कैल्शियम संतुलन में कोई भूमिका नहीं निभाता है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICALCOORDINATIONANDINTEGRATION_MCQ_Q14 - Mammalian organ lacking cortex and medulla

questiontext.text:
14. Which of the following organs in mammals does not consist of a central 'medullary' region surrounded by a cortical region?

14. स्तनधारियों में निम्नलिखित में से किस अंग में वल्कुट (कॉर्टिकल) क्षेत्र से घिरा हुआ केंद्रीय 'मध्यांश' (मेडुलरी) क्षेत्र नहीं होता है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Several mammalian organs are structurally organized into an outer cortex and an inner medulla.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Organ
The ovary has an outer ovarian cortex and an inner medulla. The adrenal gland consists of an outer adrenal cortex and a central adrenal medulla. The kidney is internally divided into an outer renal cortex and an inner renal medulla. In contrast, the liver is organized into hepatic lobules containing hepatic cells arranged in the form of cords, and it does not possess a central medullary region surrounded by a cortical region.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The liver does not consist of a central medullary region surrounded by a cortical region.

चरण 1: सैद्धांतिक सिद्धांत
कई स्तनधारी अंग संरचनात्मक रूप से एक बाहरी वल्कुट (कॉर्टेक्स) और एक आंतरिक मध्यांश (मेडुला) में व्यवस्थित होते हैं।

चरण 2: प्रत्येक अंग का मूल्यांकन
अंडाशय में एक बाहरी अंडाशयी वल्कुट और एक आंतरिक मध्यांश होता है। अधिवृक्क ग्रंथि में एक बाहरी अधिवृक्क वल्कुट और एक केंद्रीय अधिवृक्क मध्यांश होता है। वृक्क आंतरिक रूप से एक बाहरी वृक्क वल्कुट और एक आंतरिक वृक्क मध्यांश में विभाजित होता है। इसके विपरीत, यकृत यकृतीय पालिकाओं (हेपेटिक लोब्यूल्स) में व्यवस्थित होता है जिनमें यकृत कोशिकाएँ रज्जुओं के रूप में व्यवस्थित होती हैं, और इसमें वल्कुट क्षेत्र से घिरा कोई केंद्रीय मध्यांश क्षेत्र नहीं होता है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
यकृत में वल्कुट क्षेत्र से घिरा केंद्रीय मध्यांश क्षेत्र नहीं होता है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICALCOORDINATIONANDINTEGRATION_MCQ_Q15 - Condition not linked to thyroid hormone deficiency

questiontext.text:
15. Which of the following conditions is not linked to deficiency of thyroid hormones?

15. निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी स्थिति थायरॉइड हार्मोनों की कमी से जुड़ी नहीं है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Disorders of the thyroid gland are broadly classified into hypothyroidism (deficiency of thyroid hormones) and hyperthyroidism (excessive secretion of thyroid hormones).

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Condition
Deficiency of iodine in the diet results in hypothyroidism and enlargement of the thyroid gland, commonly called simple goitre. Hypothyroidism during pregnancy causes defective development and maturation of the growing baby, leading to stunted growth (cretinism), mental retardation, and low intelligence quotient. Myxedema is a condition caused by severe hypothyroidism in adults. In contrast, exophthalmia (exophthalmic goitre or Graves' disease) is a form of hyperthyroidism characterized by enlargement of the thyroid gland, protrusion of the eyeballs, increased basal metabolic rate, and weight loss.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Exophthalmia is linked to hyperthyroidism (excess thyroid hormones) rather than deficiency of thyroid hormones.

चरण 1: सैद्धांतिक सिद्धांत
थायरॉइड ग्रंथि के विकारों को मुख्य रूप से हाइपोथायरॉइडिज़्म (थायरॉइड हार्मोनों की कमी) और हाइपरथायरॉइडिज़्म (थायरॉइड हार्मोनों का अत्यधिक स्राव) में वर्गीकृत किया जाता है।

चरण 2: प्रत्येक स्थिति का मूल्यांकन
आहार में आयोडीन की कमी से हाइपोथायरॉइडिज़्म और थायरॉइड ग्रंथि का बढ़ना होता है, जिसे सामान्यतः सरल गलगंड (गॉयटर) कहा जाता है। गर्भावस्था के दौरान हाइपोथायरॉइडिज़्म से गर्भस्थ शिशु का दोषपूर्ण विकास और परिपक्वता होती है, जिससे अवरुद्ध वृद्धि (क्रेटिनिज़्म), मानसिक मंदता और कम बुद्धिलब्धि होती है। मिक्सीडिमा वयस्कों में गंभीर हाइपोथायरॉइडिज़्म के कारण होने वाली स्थिति है। इसके विपरीत, एक्सॉफ्थैल्मिया (एक्सॉफ्थैल्मिक गॉयटर या ग्रेव्स रोग) हाइपरथायरॉइडिज़्म का एक रूप है जिसकी विशेषता थायरॉइड ग्रंथि का बढ़ना, नेत्रगोलक का बाहर की ओर उभरना, बढ़ी हुई आधारी उपापचय दर और वजन घटना है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
एक्सॉफ्थैल्मिया थायरॉइड हार्मोनों की कमी के बजाय हाइपरथायरॉइडिज़्म (थायरॉइड हार्मोनों की अधिकता) से जुड़ा है।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q01 - Accuracy and precision of mass measurements

questiontext.text:
1. Two students performed the same experiment separately and each one of them recorded two readings of mass which are given below. Correct reading of mass is 3.0 g. On the basis of given data, mark the correct option out of the following statements.

Student Readings
(i) (ii)
A 3.01 2.99
B 3.05 2.95

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Precision refers to the closeness of various measurements for the same quantity to one another. Accuracy refers to the agreement of a particular value (or the average of measurements) to the true value of the result.

Step 2: Evaluation
The true mass is \(3.0\text{ g}\). For student A, the readings are \(3.01\text{ g}\) and \(2.99\text{ g}\). Their average is \(\frac{3.01 + 2.99}{2} = 3.00\text{ g}\), which matches the true value, and the difference between the two readings is only \(0.02\text{ g}\). For student B, the readings are \(3.05\text{ g}\) and \(2.95\text{ g}\). Their average is \(\frac{3.05 + 2.95}{2} = 3.00\text{ g}\), which matches the true value, but the difference between the two readings is \(0.10\text{ g}\).

Step 3: Application
Since the readings of student A are both very close to each other and their average equals the true value, the results of student A are both precise and accurate. For student B, the average equals the true value (accurate), but the individual readings are spread apart (not precise).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Results of student A are both precise and accurate.

answer.text: Results of both the students are neither accurate nor precise.
Results of student A are both precise and accurate.
Results of student B are neither precise nor accurate.
Results of student B are both precise and accurate.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q02 - Conversion of Fahrenheit temperature to Celsius scale

questiontext.text: 2. A measured temperature on Fahrenheit scale is 200 °F. What will this reading be on Celsius scale?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Temperature on the Fahrenheit scale, \(T_{\text{F}} = 200\ ^\circ\text{F}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Standard temperature conversion relation between Fahrenheit and Celsius scales applies.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The relation between Fahrenheit and Celsius scales is:
\[T_{\text{F}} = \frac{9}{5}T_{\text{C}} + 32\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Rearranging the formula for \(T_{\text{C}}\):
\[T_{\text{C}} = \frac{5}{9}(T_{\text{F}} - 32)\]
Substituting \(T_{\text{F}} = 200\):
\[T_{\text{C}} = \frac{5}{9}(200 - 32) = \frac{5}{9} \times 168 = \frac{840}{9} = 93.33\ ^\circ\text{C} \approx 93.3\ ^\circ\text{C}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Since \(212\ ^\circ\text{F} = 100\ ^\circ\text{C}\), a value slightly below \(212\ ^\circ\text{F}\) should be slightly below \(100\ ^\circ\text{C}\). Thus, \(93.3\ ^\circ\text{C}\) is physically reasonable. The reading on the Celsius scale is \(93.3\ ^\circ\text{C}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q03 - Molarity of sodium chloride aqueous solution

questiontext.text: 3. What will be the molarity of a solution, which contains 5.85 g of NaCl(s) per 500 mL?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) = \(5.85\text{ g}\)
Volume of solution = \(500\text{ mL}\)
Molar mass of \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) = \(23 + 35.5 = 58.5\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Volume is converted to litres using \(1\text{ L} = 1000\text{ mL}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Number of moles of solute} = \frac{\text{Mass of solute}}{\text{Molar mass of solute}}\]
\[\text{Molarity } (M) = \frac{\text{Number of moles of solute}}{\text{Volume of solution in litres}}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Moles of \(\mathrm{NaCl} = \frac{5.85\text{ g}}{58.5\text{ g mol}^{-1}} = 0.1\text{ mol}\)
Volume of solution in litres \(= \frac{500\text{ mL}}{1000\text{ mL L}^{-1}} = 0.5\text{ L}\)
\[M = \frac{0.1\text{ mol}}{0.5\text{ L}} = 0.2\text{ mol L}^{-1}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Units simplify to \(\text{mol L}^{-1}\), which is the standard unit for molarity. Therefore, the molarity of the solution is \(0.2\text{ mol L}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q04 - Molarity of a solution after dilution

questiontext.text: 4. If 500 mL of a 5M solution is diluted to 1500 mL, what will be the molarity of the solution obtained?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial molarity, \(M_1 = 5\text{ M}\)
Initial volume, \(V_1 = 500\text{ mL}\)
Final volume after dilution, \(V_2 = 1500\text{ mL}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Upon dilution by adding solvent, the total number of moles of solute remains conserved.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Dilution equation:
\[M_1 V_1 = M_2 V_2\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the given values:
\[5\text{ M} \times 500\text{ mL} = M_2 \times 1500\text{ mL}\]
\[M_2 = \frac{5 \times 500}{1500} = \frac{5}{3} = 1.666\ldots\text{ M} \approx 1.66\text{ M}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The volume increases by a factor of 3, so the molarity decreases by a factor of 3 (\(5 / 3 \approx 1.66\text{ M}\)). Thus, the final molarity is \(1.66\text{ M}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q05 - Greatest number of atoms among given samples

questiontext.text: 5. The number of atoms present in one mole of an element is equal to Avogadro number. Which of the following element contains the greatest number of atoms?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Four samples are given: \(4\text{ g He}\), \(46\text{ g Na}\), \(0.40\text{ g Ca}\), and \(12\text{ g He}\).
Atomic masses: \(\mathrm{He} = 4\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\mathrm{Na} = 23\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\mathrm{Ca} = 40\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
One mole of atoms of any element contains Avogadro's number (\(N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23}\)) of atoms, so the sample with the largest number of moles contains the greatest number of atoms.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Number of moles } (n) = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Molar mass}}\]
\[\text{Number of atoms} = n \times N_A\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
For \(4\text{ g He}\): \(n = \frac{4}{4} = 1\text{ mol}\) (Number of atoms \(= N_A\))
For \(46\text{ g Na}\): \(n = \frac{46}{23} = 2\text{ mol}\) (Number of atoms \(= 2N_A\))
For \(0.40\text{ g Ca}\): \(n = \frac{0.40}{40} = 0.01\text{ mol}\) (Number of atoms \(= 0.01N_A\))
For \(12\text{ g He}\): \(n = \frac{12}{4} = 3\text{ mol}\) (Number of atoms \(= 3N_A\))

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Comparing the number of moles, \(3\text{ mol}\) is the largest. Therefore, \(12\text{ g He}\) contains the greatest number of atoms.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q06 - Molarity of glucose in blood

questiontext.text: 6. If the concentration of glucose (\(\mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{12}\mathrm{O}_{6}\)) in blood is \(0.9\text{ g L}^{-1}\), what will be the molarity of glucose in blood?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Concentration of glucose in blood \(= 0.9\text{ g L}^{-1}\)
Molecular formula of glucose \(= \mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Standard atomic masses are \(\mathrm{C} = 12\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\mathrm{H} = 1\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), and \(\mathrm{O} = 16\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Molarity} = \frac{\text{Concentration in g L}^{-1}}{\text{Molar mass in g mol}^{-1}}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Molar mass of \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6} = 6(12) + 12(1) + 6(16) = 72 + 12 + 96 = 180\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)
\[\text{Molarity} = \frac{0.9\text{ g L}^{-1}}{180\text{ g mol}^{-1}} = 0.005\text{ mol L}^{-1} = 0.005\text{ M}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Units simplify to \(\text{mol L}^{-1}\) (M). Thus, the molarity of glucose in blood is \(0.005\text{ M}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q07 - Molality of HCl gas in water

questiontext.text: 7. What will be the molality of the solution containing 18.25 g of HCl gas in 500 g of water?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of solute (\(\mathrm{HCl}\)) \(= 18.25\text{ g}\)
Mass of solvent (water) \(= 500\text{ g}\)
Molar mass of \(\mathrm{HCl} = 1 + 35.5 = 36.5\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Mass of solvent is converted from grams to kilograms using \(1\text{ kg} = 1000\text{ g}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Molality } (m) = \frac{\text{Moles of solute}}{\text{Mass of solvent in kg}}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Moles of \(\mathrm{HCl} = \frac{18.25\text{ g}}{36.5\text{ g mol}^{-1}} = 0.5\text{ mol}\)
Mass of water in kg \(= \frac{500\text{ g}}{1000\text{ g kg}^{-1}} = 0.5\text{ kg}\)
\[m = \frac{0.5\text{ mol}}{0.5\text{ kg}} = 1\text{ mol kg}^{-1} = 1\text{ m}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Molality is denoted by lowercase \(m\) (whereas \(M\) denotes molarity). Hence, the molality of the solution is \(1\text{ m}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q08 - Number of sulphuric acid molecules in solution

questiontext.text: 8. One mole of any substance contains \(6.022 \times 10^{23}\) atoms/molecules. Number of molecules of \(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}\) present in 100 mL of \(0.02\text{ M}\) \(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}\) solution is ______.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Volume of \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) solution, \(V = 100\text{ mL}\)
Molarity of \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) solution, \(M = 0.02\text{ M} = 0.02\text{ mol L}^{-1}\)
Avogadro's number, \(N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23}\text{ mol}^{-1}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Convert volume from millilitres to litres: \(100\text{ mL} = 0.1\text{ L}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Number of moles} = \text{Molarity} \times \text{Volume in litres}\]
\[\text{Number of molecules} = \text{Number of moles} \times N_A\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Moles of \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4} = 0.02\text{ mol L}^{-1} \times 0.1\text{ L} = 0.002\text{ mol} = 2 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol}\)
Number of molecules \(= 2 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol} \times 6.022 \times 10^{23}\text{ mol}^{-1} = 12.044 \times 10^{20}\text{ molecules}\)

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The exponent is \(10^{-3} \times 10^{23} = 10^{20}\), and \(2 \times 6.022 = 12.044\). Therefore, the number of molecules is \(12.044 \times 10^{20}\) molecules.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q09 - Mass percent of carbon in carbon dioxide

questiontext.text: 9. What is the mass percent of carbon in carbon dioxide?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Compound: Carbon dioxide (\(\mathrm{CO_2}\))
Atomic mass of carbon (\(\mathrm{C}\)) \(= 12\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)
Atomic mass of oxygen (\(\mathrm{O}\)) \(= 16\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
One mole of \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) contains 1 mole of \(\mathrm{C}\) atoms and 2 moles of \(\mathrm{O}\) atoms.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Mass percent of an element} = \frac{\text{Mass of that element in 1 mole of compound}}{\text{Molar mass of the compound}} \times 100\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Molar mass of \(\mathrm{CO_2} = 12 + 2(16) = 12 + 32 = 44\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)
\[\text{Mass percent of carbon} = \frac{12}{44} \times 100 = \frac{3}{11} \times 100 = 27.27\%\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Since \(\frac{12}{44} \approx 0.2727\), the percentage is \(27.27\%\). Therefore, the mass percent of carbon in carbon dioxide is \(27.27\%\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q10 - Molecular formula from empirical formula and mass

questiontext.text: 10. The empirical formula and molecular mass of a compound are CH₂O and 180 g respectively. What will be the molecular formula of the compound?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Empirical formula \(= \mathrm{CH_2O}\)
Molecular mass \(= 180\text{ g}\)
Atomic masses: \(\mathrm{C} = 12\), \(\mathrm{H} = 1\), \(\mathrm{O} = 16\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The molecular formula is an integral multiple \(n\) of the empirical formula.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[n = \frac{\text{Molecular mass}}{\text{Empirical formula mass}}\]
\[\text{Molecular formula} = (\text{Empirical formula})_n\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Empirical formula mass of \(\mathrm{CH_2O} = 12 + 2(1) + 16 = 30\text{ g}\)
\[n = \frac{180}{30} = 6\]
\[\text{Molecular formula} = (\mathrm{CH_2O})_6 = \mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The molecular mass of \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\) is \(6(12) + 12(1) + 6(16) = 180\text{ g}\), which matches the given value. Thus, the molecular formula is \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q11 - Mass calculation using significant figures rules

questiontext.text: 11. If the density of a solution is \(3.12\text{ g mL}^{-1}\), the mass of \(1.5\text{ mL}\) solution in significant figures is ______.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Density of solution \(= 3.12\text{ g mL}^{-1}\) (3 significant figures)
Volume of solution \(= 1.5\text{ mL}\) (2 significant figures)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
In multiplication or division, the final result should be reported with no more significant figures than the measurement with the fewest significant figures.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Mass} = \text{Density} \times \text{Volume}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[\text{Mass} = 3.12\text{ g mL}^{-1} \times 1.5\text{ mL} = 4.68\text{ g}\]
Since \(1.5\text{ mL}\) has only 2 significant figures, \(4.68\text{ g}\) must be rounded to 2 significant figures. As the digit to be dropped (8) is greater than 5, the preceding digit (6) is increased by 1, giving \(4.7\text{ g}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The value \(4.7\text{ g}\) has 2 significant figures and correct units. Therefore, the mass in significant figures is \(4.7\text{ g}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q12 - Characteristic properties of a chemical compound

questiontext.text: 12. Which of the following statements about a compound is incorrect?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A compound is a pure substance formed when two or more atoms of different elements combine chemically in a fixed ratio by mass. Its constituent elements can only be separated by chemical or electrochemical methods, not physical methods.

Step 2: Evaluation
When elements combine chemically to form a compound, a new substance is formed whose physical and chemical properties are completely different from those of its constituent elements. For example, hydrogen and oxygen are gases at room temperature, whereas their compound, water, is a liquid.

Step 3: Application
Statements stating that a molecule of a compound has atoms of different elements, cannot be separated by physical methods, and has a fixed ratio of atoms are all true. The statement claiming that a compound retains the physical properties of its constituent elements is false.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The incorrect statement is that a compound retains the physical properties of its constituent elements.

answer.text: A molecule of a compound has atoms of different elements.
A compound cannot be separated into its constituent elements by physical methods of separation.
A compound retains the physical properties of its constituent elements.
The ratio of atoms of different elements in a compound is fixed.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q13 - Law of conservation of mass in iron oxidation

questiontext.text:
13. Which of the following statements is correct about the reaction given below:

\[4\text{Fe(s)} + 3\text{O}_2\text{(g)} \longrightarrow 2\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3\text{(g)}\]

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
According to the law of conservation of mass, matter can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction; therefore, the total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products in a balanced chemical equation.

Step 2: Evaluation
The given equation \(4\text{Fe(s)} + 3\text{O}_2\text{(g)} \longrightarrow 2\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3\text{(g)}\) is balanced: there are 4 atoms of \(\mathrm{Fe}\) and 6 atoms of \(\mathrm{O}\) on both the reactant and product sides. Hence, the total mass of iron and oxygen in the reactants equals the total mass of iron and oxygen in the product.

Step 3: Application
The law of multiple proportions applies when two elements form more than one compound, not to mass conservation in a single reaction. Furthermore, adding one reactant in excess does not increase or decrease the amount of product formed once the other reactant acts as the limiting reagent.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Total mass of iron and oxygen in reactants = total mass of iron and oxygen in product therefore it follows law of conservation of mass.

answer.text: Total mass of iron and oxygen in reactants = total mass of iron and oxygen in product therefore it follows law of conservation of mass.
Total mass of reactants = total mass of product; therefore, law of multiple proportions is followed.
Amount of \(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}\) can be increased by taking any one of the reactants (iron or oxygen) in excess.
Amount of \(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}\) produced will decrease if the amount of any one of the reactants (iron or oxygen) is taken in excess.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q14 - Reaction violating law of conservation of mass

questiontext.text: 14. Which of the following reactions is not correct according to the law of conservation of mass.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
For a chemical reaction to obey the law of conservation of mass, the number of atoms of each element on the reactant side must equal the number of atoms of that element on the product side (i.e., the equation must be balanced).

Step 2: Evaluation
Checking the atom balance for each reaction:
- \(2\text{Mg(s)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)} \longrightarrow 2\text{MgO(s)}\): 2 Mg and 2 O on both sides (balanced).
- \(\text{C}_3\text{H}_8\text{(g)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)} \longrightarrow \text{CO}_2\text{(g)} + \text{H}_2\text{O(g)}\): Reactants have 3 C, 8 H, 2 O; products have 1 C, 2 H, 3 O (unbalanced).
- \(\text{P}_4\text{(s)} + 5\text{O}_2\text{(g)} \longrightarrow \text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}\text{(s)}\): 4 P and 10 O on both sides (balanced).
- \(\text{CH}_4\text{(g)} + 2\text{O}_2\text{(g)} \longrightarrow \text{CO}_2\text{(g)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O(g)}\): 1 C, 4 H, and 4 O on both sides (balanced).

Step 3: Application
Because \(\text{C}_3\text{H}_8\text{(g)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)} \longrightarrow \text{CO}_2\text{(g)} + \text{H}_2\text{O(g)}\) is unbalanced, the total mass of reactants does not equal the total mass of products.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The reaction \(\text{C}_3\text{H}_8\text{(g)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)} \longrightarrow \text{CO}_2\text{(g)} + \text{H}_2\text{O(g)}\) is not correct according to the law of conservation of mass.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q15 - Statement illustrating law of multiple proportions

questiontext.text: 15. Which of the following statements indicates that law of multiple proportion is being followed.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The law of multiple proportions (proposed by Dalton) states that if two elements can combine to form more than one compound, the masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other element are in the ratio of small whole numbers.

Step 2: Evaluation
- Carbon dioxide from any source having a fixed ratio illustrates the law of definite proportions.
- Carbon forming two oxides, \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) and \(\mathrm{CO}\), where the masses of oxygen (\(32\text{ g}\) and \(16\text{ g}\)) combining with a fixed mass of carbon (\(12\text{ g}\)) are in the simple whole-number ratio \(2:1\), directly illustrates the law of multiple proportions.
- Conservation of magnesium mass illustrates the law of conservation of mass.
- Combining \(200\text{ mL}\) of hydrogen with \(100\text{ mL}\) of oxygen to give \(200\text{ mL}\) of water vapour illustrates Gay Lussac's law of gaseous volumes.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The statement that carbon forms two oxides namely \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) and \(\mathrm{CO}\), where masses of oxygen which combine with fixed mass of carbon are in the simple ratio \(2:1\), indicates that the law of multiple proportions is being followed.

answer.text: Sample of carbon dioxide taken from any source will always have carbon and oxygen in the ratio 1:2.
Carbon forms two oxides namely \(\mathrm{CO}_{2}\) and \(\mathrm{CO}\), where masses of oxygen which combine with fixed mass of carbon are in the simple ratio 2:1.
When magnesium burns in oxygen, the amount of magnesium taken for the reaction is equal to the amount of magnesium in magnesium oxide formed.
At constant temperature and pressure \(200\text{ mL}\) of hydrogen will combine with \(100\text{ mL}\) oxygen to produce \(200\text{ mL}\) of water vapour.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQII_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q16 - Properties of one mole of oxygen gas

questiontext.text: 16. One mole of oxygen gas at STP is equal to

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Oxygen gas exists as diatomic molecules (\(\mathrm{O_2}\)). One mole of any molecular substance contains Avogadro's number (\(6.022 \times 10^{23}\)) of molecules and has a mass equal to its molar mass in grams.

Step 2: Evaluation
For one mole of \(\mathrm{O_2}\) gas:
- Number of molecules \(= 6.022 \times 10^{23}\) molecules of \(\mathrm{O_2}\).
- Number of atoms \(= 2 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 1.2044 \times 10^{24}\) atoms of oxygen.
- Molar mass of \(\mathrm{O_2} = 2 \times 16 = 32\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), so 1 mole weighs \(32\text{ g}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
One mole of oxygen gas at STP is equal to \(6.022 \times 10^{23}\) molecules of oxygen and \(32\text{ g}\) of oxygen.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQII_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q17 - Mass and molarity of sodium sulphate formed

questiontext.text:
17. Sulphuric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide as follows :

\[\mathrm{H_2SO_4} + 2\mathrm{NaOH} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Na_2SO_4} + 2\mathrm{H_2O}\]

When 1L of 0.1M sulphuric acid solution is allowed to react with 1L of 0.1M sodium hydroxide solution, the amount of sodium sulphate formed and its molarity in the solution obtained is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Reaction: \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4 + 2NaOH \longrightarrow Na_2SO_4 + 2H_2O}\)
Volume of \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4} = 1\text{ L}\), Molarity \(= 0.1\text{ M}\)
Volume of \(\mathrm{NaOH} = 1\text{ L}\), Molarity \(= 0.1\text{ M}\)
Molar mass of \(\mathrm{Na_2SO_4} = 2(23) + 32 + 4(16) = 142\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Total volume of the resulting solution is the sum of the two volumes: \(V_{\text{total}} = 1\text{ L} + 1\text{ L} = 2\text{ L}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Moles} = \text{Molarity} \times \text{Volume in L}\]
\[\text{Mass} = \text{Moles} \times \text{Molar mass}\]
\[\text{Molarity} = \frac{\text{Moles of solute}}{\text{Total volume in L}}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Moles of \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4} = 0.1\text{ mol L}^{-1} \times 1\text{ L} = 0.1\text{ mol}\)
Moles of \(\mathrm{NaOH} = 0.1\text{ mol L}^{-1} \times 1\text{ L} = 0.1\text{ mol}\)
From stoichiometry, \(1\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) requires \(2\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{NaOH}\). Thus, \(0.1\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) would require \(0.2\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{NaOH}\), so \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) is the limiting reagent.
\(2\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) produces \(1\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{Na_2SO_4}\), so \(0.1\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) produces:
\[\text{Moles of }\mathrm{Na_2SO_4} = \frac{0.1}{2} = 0.05\text{ mol}\]
Mass of \(\mathrm{Na_2SO_4}\) formed:
\[\text{Mass} = 0.05\text{ mol} \times 142\text{ g mol}^{-1} = 7.10\text{ g}\]
Molarity of \(\mathrm{Na_2SO_4}\) in the \(2\text{ L}\) solution:
\[M = \frac{0.05\text{ mol}}{2\text{ L}} = 0.025\text{ mol L}^{-1}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The amount of \(\mathrm{Na_2SO_4}\) formed is \(7.10\text{ g}\) and its molarity in the resulting solution is \(0.025\text{ mol L}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQII_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q18 - Pairs having the same number of atoms

questiontext.text: 18. Which of the following pairs have the same number of atoms?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Molar masses: \(\mathrm{O_2} = 32\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\mathrm{H_2} = 2\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\mathrm{CO_2} = 44\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\mathrm{N_2} = 28\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\mathrm{C} = 12\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\mathrm{Na} = 23\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Total number of atoms in a sample is the product of moles of molecules (or formula units), atomicity (atoms per molecule), and Avogadro's number \(N_A\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Number of atoms} = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Molar mass}} \times \text{Atomicity} \times N_A\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
1. \(16\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{O_2}\): \(\frac{16}{32} \times 2 \times N_A = 1 N_A\) atoms; \(4\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{H_2}\): \(\frac{4}{2} \times 2 \times N_A = 4 N_A\) atoms (not equal).
2. \(16\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{O_2}\): \(1 N_A\) atoms; \(44\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{CO_2}\): \(\frac{44}{44} \times 3 \times N_A = 3 N_A\) atoms (not equal).
3. \(28\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{N_2}\): \(\frac{28}{28} \times 2 \times N_A = 2 N_A\) atoms; \(32\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{O_2}\): \(\frac{32}{32} \times 2 \times N_A = 2 N_A\) atoms (equal).
4. \(12\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{C(s)}\): \(\frac{12}{12} \times 1 \times N_A = 1 N_A\) atoms; \(23\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{Na(s)}\): \(\frac{23}{23} \times 1 \times N_A = 1 N_A\) atoms (equal).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The pairs with the same number of atoms are \(28\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{N_2}\) and \(32\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{O_2}\) (each \(2N_A\)), and \(12\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{C(s)}\) and \(23\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{Na(s)}\) (each \(1N_A\)).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQII_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q19 - Solutions having the same molar concentration

questiontext.text: 19. Which of the following solutions have the same concentration?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Molar masses: \(\mathrm{NaOH} = 23 + 16 + 1 = 40\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\mathrm{KOH} = 39 + 16 + 1 = 56\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Concentration here refers to molarity (\(\text{mol L}^{-1}\)), with volume converted from \(\text{mL}\) to \(\text{L}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Molarity} = \frac{\text{Moles of solute}}{\text{Volume of solution in L}}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
1. \(20\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) in \(200\text{ mL}\): \(\text{Moles} = \frac{20}{40} = 0.5\text{ mol}\); \(\text{Molarity} = \frac{0.5}{0.2} = 2.5\text{ M}\).
2. \(0.5\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{KCl}\) in \(200\text{ mL}\): \(\text{Molarity} = \frac{0.5}{0.2} = 2.5\text{ M}\).
3. \(40\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) in \(100\text{ mL}\): \(\text{Moles} = \frac{40}{40} = 1\text{ mol}\); \(\text{Molarity} = \frac{1}{0.1} = 10\text{ M}\).
4. \(20\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{KOH}\) in \(200\text{ mL}\): \(\text{Moles} = \frac{20}{56} \approx 0.357\text{ mol}\); \(\text{Molarity} = \frac{0.357}{0.2} \approx 1.79\text{ M}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Both \(20\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) in \(200\text{ mL}\) of solution and \(0.5\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{KCl}\) in \(200\text{ mL}\) of solution have a molarity of \(2.5\text{ M}\).

answer.text: \(20\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) in \(200\text{ mL}\) of solution
\(0.5\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{KCl}\) in \(200\text{ mL}\) of solution
\(40\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) in \(100\text{ mL}\) of solution
\(20\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{KOH}\) in \(200\text{ mL}\) of solution

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQII_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q20 - Samples with same number of molecules as oxygen

questiontext.text: 20. 16 g of oxygen has same number of molecules as in

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Reference sample: \(16\text{ g}\) of oxygen gas (\(\mathrm{O_2}\)), molar mass \(= 32\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).
Molar masses of other gases: \(\mathrm{CO} = 12 + 16 = 28\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\mathrm{N_2} = 28\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\mathrm{H_2} = 2\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Equal numbers of moles of different molecular substances contain equal numbers of molecules.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Number of moles } (n) = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Molar mass}}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Moles in \(16\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{O_2} = \frac{16}{32} = 0.5\text{ mol}\).
Comparing with the given samples:
- \(16\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{CO}\): \(n = \frac{16}{28} \approx 0.57\text{ mol}\)
- \(28\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{N_2}\): \(n = \frac{28}{28} = 1\text{ mol}\)
- \(14\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{N_2}\): \(n = \frac{14}{28} = 0.5\text{ mol}\)
- \(1.0\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{H_2}\): \(n = \frac{1.0}{2} = 0.5\text{ mol}\)

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Both \(14\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{N_2}\) and \(1.0\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{H_2}\) correspond to \(0.5\text{ mol}\), so they have the same number of molecules as \(16\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{O_2}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQII_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q21 - Unitless concentration terms in chemistry

questiontext.text: 21. Which of the following terms are unitless?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A quantity is unitless (dimensionless) if it is defined as a ratio of two quantities having the same units.

Step 2: Evaluation
- Molality is defined as moles of solute per kilogram of solvent, so its unit is \(\text{mol kg}^{-1}\).
- Molarity is defined as moles of solute per litre of solution, so its unit is \(\text{mol L}^{-1}\).
- Mole fraction is the ratio of moles of one component to the total moles of all components (\(\frac{\text{mol}}{\text{mol}}\)), making it unitless.
- Mass percent is the ratio of mass of solute to mass of solution multiplied by 100 (\(\frac{\text{g}}{\text{g}} \times 100\)), making it unitless.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Mole fraction and mass percent are unitless.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQII_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q22 - Laws unrelated to Dalton atomic theory statement

questiontext.text:
22. One of the statements of Dalton's atomic theory is given below:

"Compounds are formed when atoms of different elements combine in a fixed ratio"

Which of the following laws is not related to this statement?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The given statement of Dalton's atomic theory explains how elements combine in fixed ratios by number of atoms (and hence fixed ratios by mass) to form compounds.

Step 2: Evaluation
- Law of definite proportions states that a given compound always contains exactly the same proportion of elements by weight, which is directly explained by atoms combining in a fixed ratio.
- Law of multiple proportions deals with simple whole-number mass ratios when elements combine to form different compounds, which also follows from atoms combining in fixed whole-number ratios.
- Law of conservation of mass is explained by another postulate of Dalton's theory (atoms are indivisible and can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction), not by the fixed-ratio combination statement.
- Avogadro law relates equal volumes of all gases under the same conditions of temperature and pressure to equal numbers of molecules, which is not related to the fixed-ratio combination of atoms in compounds.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The law of conservation of mass and Avogadro law are not related to the given statement.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCHING_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MT_Q36 - Matching quantities to moles and molecules

questiontext.text: 36. Match the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Molar masses: \(\mathrm{CO_2} = 12 + 2(16) = 44\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\mathrm{O_2} = 2(16) = 32\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).
Molar volume of an ideal gas at STP \(= 22.4\text{ L mol}^{-1}\).
Avogadro's number, \(N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23}\text{ mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Number of moles is calculated from mass, number of molecules, or gas volume at STP using standard mole relationships.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[n = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Molar mass}} = \frac{\text{Number of molecules}}{N_A} = \frac{\text{Volume at STP}}{22.4\text{ L}}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
- \(88\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{CO_2}\): \(n = \frac{88}{44} = 2\text{ mol}\).
- \(6.022 \times 10^{23}\) molecules of \(\mathrm{H_2O}\): \(n = \frac{6.022 \times 10^{23}}{6.022 \times 10^{23}} = 1\text{ mol}\).
- \(5.6\text{ litres}\) of \(\mathrm{O_2}\) at STP: \(n = \frac{5.6}{22.4} = 0.25\text{ mol}\).
- \(96\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{O_2}\): \(n = \frac{96}{32} = 3\text{ mol}\).
- \(1\text{ mol}\) of any gas: contains \(6.022 \times 10^{23}\) molecules.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Each quantity is matched to its corresponding mole or molecular count: \(88\text{ g }\mathrm{CO_2} \rightarrow 2\text{ mol}\); \(6.022 \times 10^{23}\text{ molecules of }\mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow 1\text{ mol}\); \(5.6\text{ L }\mathrm{O_2}\text{ at STP} \rightarrow 0.25\text{ mol}\); \(96\text{ g }\mathrm{O_2} \rightarrow 3\text{ mol}\); \(1\text{ mol of any gas} \rightarrow 6.022 \times 10^{23}\text{ molecules}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCHING_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MT_Q37 - Matching physical quantities with their units

questiontext.text: 37. Match the following physical quantities with units

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Each physical quantity in chemistry has a characteristic unit (SI or commonly used laboratory unit) derived from its definition.

Step 2: Evaluation
- Molarity is moles of solute per litre of solution, with unit \(\text{mol L}^{-1}\).
- Mole fraction is a ratio of moles to total moles, so it is unitless.
- Mole is the SI unit for amount of substance, denoted by \(\text{mol}\).
- Molality is moles of solute per kilogram of solvent, with unit \(\text{mol kg}^{-1}\).
- Pressure is force per unit area, whose SI unit is Pascal (\(\text{N m}^{-2}\)).
- Luminous intensity has the SI base unit Candela.
- Density is mass per unit volume, commonly expressed in \(\text{g mL}^{-1}\).
- Mass has the SI base unit \(\text{kg}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are: Molarity \(\rightarrow \text{mol L}^{-1}\), Mole fraction \(\rightarrow\) Unitless, Mole \(\rightarrow \text{mol}\), Molality \(\rightarrow \text{mol kg}^{-1}\), Pressure \(\rightarrow\) Pascal, Luminous intensity \(\rightarrow\) Candela, Density \(\rightarrow \text{g mL}^{-1}\), and Mass \(\rightarrow \text{kg}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AR_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_AR_Q38 - Empirical mass and molecular mass of ethene

questiontext.text:
38. Assertion (A) : The empirical mass of ethene is half of its molecular mass.

Reason (R) : The empirical formula represents the simplest whole number ratio of various atoms present in a compound.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The molecular formula gives the exact number of different types of atoms present in a molecule, whereas the empirical formula represents the simplest whole-number ratio of those atoms.

Step 2: Evaluation
For ethene, the molecular formula is \(\mathrm{C_2H_4}\), giving a molecular mass of \(2(12) + 4(1) = 28\text{ u}\). Dividing the subscripts by 2 gives the simplest whole-number ratio, which is the empirical formula \(\mathrm{CH_2}\). Its empirical mass is \(12 + 2(1) = 14\text{ u}\), which is exactly half of \(28\text{ u}\). Therefore, the Assertion is true.

Step 3: Application
The Reason accurately defines the empirical formula as representing the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a compound, and this simplification by a factor of 2 directly explains why the empirical mass of ethene is half its molecular mass.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

answer.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AR_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_AR_Q39 - Definition of atomic mass unit and carbon-12

questiontext.text:
39. Assertion (A) : One atomic mass unit is defined as one twelfth of the mass of one carbon-12 atom.

Reason (R) : Carbon-12 isotope is the most abundant isotope of carbon and has been chosen as standard.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
One atomic mass unit (amu or u) is defined by international convention as a mass exactly equal to one-twelfth of the mass of one carbon-12 (\({}^{12}\mathrm{C}\)) atom.

Step 2: Evaluation
The Assertion is a true statement of the modern definition of the atomic mass unit. The Reason is also true: \({}^{12}\mathrm{C}\) is the most abundant isotope of carbon and was chosen as the reference standard.

Step 3: Application
However, the abundance of \({}^{12}\mathrm{C}\) does not explain why one atomic mass unit is defined specifically as *one-twelfth* of its mass (the factor of \(\frac{1}{12}\) is chosen so that the mass of a hydrogen atom is close to \(1\text{ u}\) and atomic masses of other elements remain convenient).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.

answer.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AR_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_AR_Q40 - Significant figures for trailing zeros in numbers

questiontext.text:
40. Assertion (A) : Significant figures for 0.200 is 3 where as for 200 it is 1.

Reason (R) : Zero at the end or right of a number are significant provided they are not on the right side of the decimal point.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
According to the rules for determining significant figures, trailing zeros (zeros at the end or right of a number) are significant if and only if they are on the right side of the decimal point.

Step 2: Evaluation
In \(0.200\), the leading zero is not significant, while the two trailing zeros to the right of the decimal point are significant; hence, \(0.200\) has 3 significant figures. In \(200\) (written without a decimal point), the trailing zeros are not significant; hence, \(200\) has 1 significant figure. Therefore, the Assertion is true.

Step 3: Application
The Reason states the opposite of the rule—it claims trailing zeros are significant provided they are *not* on the right side of the decimal point. Thus, the Reason is false.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
A is true but R is false.

answer.text: Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AR_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_AR_Q41 - Combustion of methane and mass of water formed

questiontext.text:
41. Assertion (A) : Combustion of 16 g of methane gives 18 g of water.

Reason (R) : In the combustion of methane, water is one of the products.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon such as methane (\(\mathrm{CH_4}\)) in oxygen produces carbon dioxide and water according to a balanced stoichiometric equation.

Step 2: Evaluation
The balanced equation for the combustion of methane is:
\[\mathrm{CH_4(g) + 2O_2(g) \longrightarrow CO_2(g) + 2H_2O(g)}\]
\(16\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{CH_4}\) corresponds to \(1\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{CH_4}\). From stoichiometry, \(1\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{CH_4}\) produces \(2\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{H_2O}\), which has a mass of \(2 \times 18\text{ g} = 36\text{ g}\), not \(18\text{ g}\). Therefore, the Assertion is false.

Step 3: Application
The Reason states that water is one of the products in the combustion of methane, which is true.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
A is false but R is true.

answer.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_Q01 - Precision and accuracy of student mass readings

questiontext.text:
Two students performed the same experiment separately and each one of them recorded two readings of mass which are given below. Correct reading of mass is \(3.0\text{ g}\). On the basis of given data, mark the correct option out of the following statements.

Student Readings
(i) (ii)
A \(3.01\) \(2.99\)
B \(3.05\) \(2.95\)

দুইজন শিক্ষার্থী পৃথকভাবে একই পরীক্ষা সম্পন্ন করে এবং প্রত্যেকে ভরের দুটি করে পাঠ লিপিবদ্ধ করে, যা নিচে দেওয়া হলো। ভরের সঠিক পাঠ হলো \(3.0\text{ g}\)। প্রদত্ত তথ্যের ভিত্তিতে নিচের বিবৃতিগুলোর মধ্য থেকে সঠিক বিকল্পটি চিহ্নিত করো।

শিক্ষার্থী পাঠ
(i) (ii)
A \(3.01\) \(2.99\)
B \(3.05\) \(2.95\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Precision refers to the closeness of various measurements for the same quantity, whereas accuracy is the agreement of a particular value (or the average of measurements) to the true value.

Step 2: Evaluation
For student A, the readings are \(3.01\text{ g}\) and \(2.99\text{ g}\). Their average is \(\frac{3.01 + 2.99}{2} = 3.00\text{ g}\), which equals the true value \(3.0\text{ g}\), and the difference between the two readings is very small (\(0.02\text{ g}\)). For student B, the readings are \(3.05\text{ g}\) and \(2.95\text{ g}\). Their average is \(\frac{3.05 + 2.95}{2} = 3.00\text{ g}\), which matches the true value, but the spread between the two readings is relatively large (\(0.10\text{ g}\)).

Step 3: Application
Since student A's measurements are both close to each other and their average matches the true value, student A's results are both precise and accurate. Student B's average matches the true value (accurate), but the individual readings deviate noticeably from each other (not precise).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the results of student A are both precise and accurate.

ধাপ ১: ধারণাগত নীতি
যথার্থতা (Precision) বলতে একই রাশির বিভিন্ন পরিমাপের পারস্পরিক নৈকট্যকে বোঝায়, আর নির্ভুলতা (Accuracy) বলতে কোনো নির্দিষ্ট মান (বা পরিমাপগুলোর গড় মান) প্রকৃত মানের কতটা কাছাকাছি তা বোঝায়।

ধাপ ২: মূল্যায়ন
শিক্ষার্থী A-এর পাঠগুলো হলো \(3.01\text{ g}\) এবং \(2.99\text{ g}\)। এদের গড় \(\frac{3.01 + 2.99}{2} = 3.00\text{ g}\), যা প্রকৃত মান \(3.0\text{ g}\)-এর সমান এবং দুটি পাঠের মধ্যকার পার্থক্য খুবই কম (\(0.02\text{ g}\))। শিক্ষার্থী B-এর পাঠগুলো হলো \(3.05\text{ g}\) এবং \(2.95\text{ g}\)। এদের গড় \(\frac{3.05 + 2.95}{2} = 3.00\text{ g}\), যা প্রকৃত মানের সমান হলেও দুটি পাঠের মধ্যকার ব্যবধান তুলনামূলকভাবে বেশি (\(0.10\text{ g}\))।

ধাপ ৩: প্রয়োগ
যেহেতু শিক্ষার্থী A-এর পরিমাপগুলো পরস্পরের খুব কাছাকাছি এবং তাদের গড় মান প্রকৃত মানের সাথে মিলে যায়, তাই শিক্ষার্থী A-এর ফলাফল যথার্থ এবং নির্ভুল উভয়ই। শিক্ষার্থী B-এর গড় মান প্রকৃত মানের সাথে মিললেও (নির্ভুল), পৃথক পাঠগুলোর মধ্যে ব্যবধান বেশি হওয়ায় তা যথার্থ নয়।

ধাপ ৪: চূড়ান্ত সিদ্ধান্ত
অতএব, শিক্ষার্থী A-এর ফলাফল যথার্থ ও নির্ভুল উভয়ই।

answer.text: Results of both the students are neither accurate nor precise.
Results of student A are both precise and accurate.
Results of student B are neither precise nor accurate.
Results of student B are both precise and accurate.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_Q02 - Conversion of Fahrenheit temperature to Celsius scale

questiontext.text:
A measured temperature on Fahrenheit scale is \(200\,^\circ\text{F}\). What will this reading be on Celsius scale?

ফারেনহাইট স্কেলে পরিমাপকৃত একটি তাপমাত্রা হলো \(200\,^\circ\text{F}\)। সেলসিয়াস স্কেলে এই পাঠ কত হবে?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Measured temperature on the Fahrenheit scale, \(T_{\text{F}} = 200\,^\circ\text{F}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Standard linear conversion between the Fahrenheit and Celsius temperature scales is used.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The relation between Fahrenheit (\(^\circ\text{F}\)) and Celsius (\(^\circ\text{C}\)) scales is: \[T_{\text{C}} = \frac{5}{9}(T_{\text{F}} - 32)\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting \(T_{\text{F}} = 200\): \[T_{\text{C}} = \frac{5}{9}(200 - 32)\] \[T_{\text{C}} = \frac{5}{9} \times 168 = \frac{840}{9} = 93.33\,^\circ\text{C}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Since \(212\,^\circ\text{F} = 100\,^\circ\text{C}\), a temperature slightly below \(212\,^\circ\text{F}\) should be slightly below \(100\,^\circ\text{C}\), confirming \(93.3\,^\circ\text{C}\) is physically reasonable. Thus, the reading on the Celsius scale is \(93.3\,^\circ\text{C}\).

ধাপ ১: প্রদত্ত তথ্য ও শর্তাবলি
ফারেনহাইট স্কেলে পরিমাপকৃত তাপমাত্রা, \(T_{\text{F}} = 200\,^\circ\text{F}\)।

ধাপ ২: অনুমান ও চিহ্ন প্রথা
ফারেনহাইট ও সেলসিয়াস তাপমাত্রা স্কেলের মধ্যে প্রচলিত রৈখিক রূপান্তর সূত্র ব্যবহার করা হয়েছে।

ধাপ ৩: প্রাসঙ্গিক সূত্র ও নীতি
ফারেনহাইট (\(^\circ\text{F}\)) ও সেলসিয়াস (\(^\circ\text{C}\)) স্কেলের মধ্যে সম্পর্ক হলো: \[T_{\text{C}} = \frac{5}{9}(T_{\text{F}} - 32)\]

ধাপ ৪: ধাপে ধাপে গণনা
\(T_{\text{F}} = 200\) বসিয়ে পাই: \[T_{\text{C}} = \frac{5}{9}(200 - 32)\] \[T_{\text{C}} = \frac{5}{9} \times 168 = \frac{840}{9} = 93.33\,^\circ\text{C}\]

ধাপ ৫: যাচাই ও চূড়ান্ত উত্তর
যেহেতু \(212\,^\circ\text{F} = 100\,^\circ\text{C}\), তাই \(212\,^\circ\text{F}\)-এর সামান্য নিচের তাপমাত্রা \(100\,^\circ\text{C}\)-এর সামান্য নিচে হবে, যা \(93.3\,^\circ\text{C}\) মানটিকে যুক্তিযুক্ত প্রমাণ করে। সুতরাং, সেলসিয়াস স্কেলে পাঠ হবে \(93.3\,^\circ\text{C}\)।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_Q03 - Molarity of NaCl solution per 500 mL

questiontext.text:
What will be the molarity of a solution, which contains \(5.85\text{ g}\) of \(\text{NaCl(s)}\) per \(500\text{ mL}\)?

প্রতি \(500\text{ mL}\)-এ \(5.85\text{ g}\) \(\text{NaCl(s)}\) ধারণকারী একটি দ্রবণের মোলারিটি কত হবে?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of solute (\(\text{NaCl}\)), \(w = 5.85\text{ g}\); Volume of solution, \(V = 500\text{ mL} = 0.5\text{ L}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Atomic masses are taken as \(\text{Na} = 23\text{ g mol}^{-1}\) and \(\text{Cl} = 35.5\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Molar mass of NaCl} = 23 + 35.5 = 58.5\text{ g mol}^{-1}\] \[\text{Number of moles } (n) = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Molar mass}}\] \[\text{Molarity } (M) = \frac{\text{Number of moles of solute}}{\text{Volume of solution in litres}}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[n = \frac{5.85\text{ g}}{58.5\text{ g mol}^{-1}} = 0.1\text{ mol}\] \[M = \frac{0.1\text{ mol}}{0.5\text{ L}} = 0.2\text{ mol L}^{-1}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The unit \(\text{mol L}^{-1}\) is consistent with molarity. Hence, the molarity of the solution is \(0.2\text{ mol L}^{-1}\).

ধাপ ১: প্রদত্ত তথ্য ও শর্তাবলি
দ্রাবের (\(\text{NaCl}\)) ভর, \(w = 5.85\text{ g}\); দ্রবণের আয়তন, \(V = 500\text{ mL} = 0.5\text{ L}\)।

ধাপ ২: অনুমান ও চিহ্ন প্রথা
পারমাণবিক ভর ধরা হয়েছে \(\text{Na} = 23\text{ g mol}^{-1}\) এবং \(\text{Cl} = 35.5\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)।

ধাপ ৩: প্রাসঙ্গিক সূত্র ও নীতি
\[\text{NaCl-এর মোলার ভর} = 23 + 35.5 = 58.5\text{ g mol}^{-1}\] \[\text{মোল সংখ্যা } (n) = \frac{\text{ভর}}{\text{মোলার ভর}}\] \[\text{মোলারিটি } (M) = \frac{\text{দ্রাবের মোল সংখ্যা}}{\text{লিটারে দ্রবণের আয়তন}}\]

ধাপ ৪: ধাপে ধাপে গণনা
\[n = \frac{5.85\text{ g}}{58.5\text{ g mol}^{-1}} = 0.1\text{ mol}\] \[M = \frac{0.1\text{ mol}}{0.5\text{ L}} = 0.2\text{ mol L}^{-1}\]

ধাপ ৫: যাচাই ও চূড়ান্ত উত্তর
একক \(\text{mol L}^{-1}\) মোলারিটির সাথে সামঞ্জস্যপূর্ণ। অতএব, দ্রবণটির মোলারিটি হলো \(0.2\text{ mol L}^{-1}\)।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_Q04 - Molarity of solution after dilution to 1500 mL

questiontext.text:
If \(500\text{ mL}\) of a \(5\text{ M}\) solution is diluted to \(1500\text{ mL}\), what will be the molarity of the solution obtained?

যদি \(5\text{ M}\) দ্রবণের \(500\text{ mL}\)-কে লঘু করে \(1500\text{ mL}\) করা হয়, তবে প্রাপ্ত দ্রবণের মোলারিটি কত হবে?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial molarity, \(M_1 = 5\text{ M}\); Initial volume, \(V_1 = 500\text{ mL}\); Final volume, \(V_2 = 1500\text{ mL}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
During dilution, the number of moles of solute remains conserved.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
By the dilution equation: \[M_1 V_1 = M_2 V_2\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the given values: \[5\text{ M} \times 500\text{ mL} = M_2 \times 1500\text{ mL}\] \[M_2 = \frac{5 \times 500}{1500} = \frac{5}{3} = 1.66\text{ M}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Since the volume increased by a factor of \(3\), the molarity decreases by a factor of \(3\), giving \(1.66\text{ M}\). Thus, the molarity of the diluted solution is \(1.66\text{ M}\).

ধাপ ১: প্রদত্ত তথ্য ও শর্তাবলি
প্রাথমিক মোলারিটি, \(M_1 = 5\text{ M}\); প্রাথমিক আয়তন, \(V_1 = 500\text{ mL}\); চূড়ান্ত আয়তন, \(V_2 = 1500\text{ mL}\)।

ধাপ ২: অনুমান ও চিহ্ন প্রথা
লঘুকরণের সময় দ্রাবের মোল সংখ্যা অপরিবর্তিত থাকে।

ধাপ ৩: প্রাসঙ্গিক সূত্র ও নীতি
লঘুকরণ সমীকরণ অনুসারে: \[M_1 V_1 = M_2 V_2\]

ধাপ ৪: ধাপে ধাপে গণনা
প্রদত্ত মানগুলো বসিয়ে পাই: \[5\text{ M} \times 500\text{ mL} = M_2 \times 1500\text{ mL}\] \[M_2 = \frac{5 \times 500}{1500} = \frac{5}{3} = 1.66\text{ M}\]

ধাপ ৫: যাচাই ও চূড়ান্ত উত্তর
যেহেতু আয়তন \(3\) গুণ বৃদ্ধি পেয়েছে, তাই মোলারিটি \(3\) গুণ হ্রাস পেয়ে \(1.66\text{ M}\) হবে। সুতরাং, লঘুকৃত দ্রবণের মোলারিটি হলো \(1.66\text{ M}\)।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_Q05 - Element containing the greatest number of atoms

questiontext.text:
The number of atoms present in one mole of an element is equal to Avogadro number. Which of the following element contains the greatest number of atoms?

একটি মৌলের এক মোলে উপস্থিত পরমাণুর সংখ্যা অ্যাভোগাড্রো সংখ্যার সমান। নিচের কোন মৌলটিতে সর্বাধিক সংখ্যক পরমাণু রয়েছে?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given samples: \(4\text{ g He}\), \(46\text{ g Na}\), \(0.40\text{ g Ca}\), and \(12\text{ g He}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Molar masses: \(\text{He} = 4\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\text{Na} = 23\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\text{Ca} = 40\text{ g mol}^{-1}\). Avogadro's number is denoted by \(N_A\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Number of atoms} = \text{Number of moles} \times N_A = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Molar mass}} \times N_A\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
For \(4\text{ g He}\): \(\frac{4}{4} = 1\text{ mol} = 1 N_A\) atoms.
For \(46\text{ g Na}\): \(\frac{46}{23} = 2\text{ mol} = 2 N_A\) atoms.
For \(0.40\text{ g Ca}\): \(\frac{0.40}{40} = 0.01\text{ mol} = 0.01 N_A\) atoms.
For \(12\text{ g He}\): \(\frac{12}{4} = 3\text{ mol} = 3 N_A\) atoms.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Comparing the number of moles, \(3\text{ mol}\) is the largest. Therefore, \(12\text{ g He}\) contains the greatest number of atoms.

ধাপ ১: প্রদত্ত তথ্য ও শর্তাবলি
প্রদত্ত নমুনাগুলো হলো: \(4\text{ g He}\), \(46\text{ g Na}\), \(0.40\text{ g Ca}\) এবং \(12\text{ g He}\)।

ধাপ ২: অনুমান ও চিহ্ন প্রথা
মোলার ভরসমূহ: \(\text{He} = 4\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\text{Na} = 23\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\text{Ca} = 40\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)। অ্যাভোগাড্রো সংখ্যাকে \(N_A\) দ্বারা প্রকাশ করা হলো।

ধাপ ৩: প্রাসঙ্গিক সূত্র ও নীতি
\[\text{পরমাণুর সংখ্যা} = \text{মোল সংখ্যা} \times N_A = \frac{\text{ভর}}{\text{মোলার ভর}} \times N_A\]

ধাপ ৪: ধাপে ধাপে গণনা
\(4\text{ g He}\)-এর জন্য: \(\frac{4}{4} = 1\text{ mol} = 1 N_A\) পরমাণু।
\(46\text{ g Na}\)-এর জন্য: \(\frac{46}{23} = 2\text{ mol} = 2 N_A\) পরমাণু।
\(0.40\text{ g Ca}\)-এর জন্য: \(\frac{0.40}{40} = 0.01\text{ mol} = 0.01 N_A\) পরমাণু।
\(12\text{ g He}\)-এর জন্য: \(\frac{12}{4} = 3\text{ mol} = 3 N_A\) পরমাণু।

ধাপ ৫: যাচাই ও চূড়ান্ত উত্তর
মোল সংখ্যা তুলনা করে দেখা যায় \(3\text{ mol}\) সর্বাধিক। অতএব, \(12\text{ g He}\)-এ সর্বাধিক সংখ্যক পরমাণু রয়েছে।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_Q06 - Molarity of glucose in blood

questiontext.text:
If the concentration of glucose (\(\text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_{6}\)) in blood is \(0.9\text{ g L}^{-1}\), what will be the molarity of glucose in blood?

যদি রক্তে গ্লুকোজের (\(\text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_{6}\)) গাঢ়ত্ব \(0.9\text{ g L}^{-1}\) হয়, তবে রক্তে গ্লুকোজের মোলারিটি কত হবে?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass concentration of glucose (\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6\)) = \(0.9\text{ g L}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Atomic masses: \(\text{C} = 12\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\text{H} = 1\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\text{O} = 16\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Molar mass of }\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6 = 6(12) + 12(1) + 6(16) = 180\text{ g mol}^{-1}\] \[\text{Molarity} = \frac{\text{Mass concentration in g L}^{-1}}{\text{Molar mass in g mol}^{-1}}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[\text{Molarity} = \frac{0.9\text{ g L}^{-1}}{180\text{ g mol}^{-1}} = 0.005\text{ mol L}^{-1} = 0.005\text{ M}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
\(0.005 \times 180 = 0.9\text{ g L}^{-1}\), which matches the given concentration. Thus, the molarity of glucose in blood is \(0.005\text{ M}\).

ধাপ ১: প্রদত্ত তথ্য ও শর্তাবলি
গ্লুকোজের (\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6\)) ভর-গাঢ়ত্ব = \(0.9\text{ g L}^{-1}\)।

ধাপ ২: অনুমান ও চিহ্ন প্রথা
পারমাণবিক ভরসমূহ: \(\text{C} = 12\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\text{H} = 1\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), \(\text{O} = 16\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)।

ধাপ ৩: প্রাসঙ্গিক সূত্র ও নীতি
