Ionic radii vary in inverse proportion to the effective nuclear charge and in direct proportion to the screening effect.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
आयनिक त्रिज्या नाभिक और बाह्यतम इलेक्ट्रॉनों के बीच स्थिरवैद्युत आकर्षण के साथ-साथ आंतरिक कोश के इलेक्ट्रॉनों द्वारा बाह्य इलेक्ट्रॉनों पर लगाए जाने वाले प्रतिकर्षण (परिरक्षण प्रभाव) पर निर्भर करती है।

चरण 2: प्रभावी नाभिकीय आवेश का मूल्यांकन
प्रभावी नाभिकीय आवेश \(Z_{\text{eff}}\), परमाणु क्रमांक \(Z\) और परिरक्षण स्थिरांक \(\sigma\) से \(Z_{\text{eff}} = Z - \sigma\) द्वारा संबंधित होता है। अधिक प्रभावी नाभिकीय आवेश संयोजकता इलेक्ट्रॉन अभ्र को नाभिक के अधिक निकट खींचता है, इसलिए आयनिक त्रिज्या प्रभावी नाभिकीय आवेश के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होती है।

चरण 3: परिरक्षण प्रभाव का मूल्यांकन
परिरक्षण प्रभाव में वृद्धि से आंतरिक-इलेक्ट्रॉन प्रतिकर्षण बढ़ता है और संयोजकता इलेक्ट्रॉनों पर नाभिक का शुद्ध आकर्षण कम हो जाता है, जिससे इलेक्ट्रॉन अभ्र का विस्तार होता है। इस प्रकार, आयनिक त्रिज्या परिरक्षण प्रभाव के अनुक्रमानुपाती होती है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
आयनिक त्रिज्या प्रभावी नाभिकीय आवेश के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती तथा परिरक्षण प्रभाव के अनुक्रमानुपाती रूप से परिवर्तित होती है।

answer.text: inverse proportion to the effective nuclear charge.
inverse proportion to the square of effective nuclear charge.
direct proportion to the square of screening effect.

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q23 - Properties of element in 3rd period group 13

questiontext.text:
An element belongs to 3rd period and group-13 of the periodic table. Which of the following properties will be shown by the element?

एक तत्व आवर्त सारणी के तीसरे आवर्त और वर्ग-13 से संबंधित है। तत्व द्वारा निम्नलिखित में से कौन-से गुण प्रदर्शित किए जाएंगे?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identification of the Element
An element located in the 3rd period has principal quantum number \(n = 3\) for its valence shell, and belonging to group 13 gives it a valence configuration of \(3s^2 3p^1\). This element is aluminium (\(\text{Al}\), atomic number \(13\)).

Step 2: Evaluation of Physical State and Metallic Character
Except for boron, all group 13 elements are metals. Aluminium is a solid metal at room temperature, not a liquid or a non-metal.

Step 3: Evaluation of Electrical Conductivity
Being a metal with delocalised valence electrons, aluminium is a good conductor of electricity.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The element is solid, metallic, and a good conductor of electricity.

चरण 1: तत्व की पहचान
तीसरे आवर्त में स्थित तत्व के संयोजकता कोश की मुख्य क्वांटम संख्या \(n = 3\) होती है, तथा वर्ग 13 से संबंधित होने के कारण इसका संयोजकता इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास \(3s^2 3p^1\) होता है। यह तत्व एल्युमीनियम (\(\text{Al}\), परमाणु क्रमांक \(13\)) है।

चरण 2: भौतिक अवस्था और धात्विक लक्षण का मूल्यांकन
बोरॉन को छोड़कर वर्ग 13 के सभी तत्व धातु हैं। एल्युमीनियम कमरे के ताप पर एक ठोस धातु है, न कि द्रव या अधातु।

चरण 3: विद्युत चालकता का मूल्यांकन
विस्थानीकृत संयोजकता इलेक्ट्रॉनों वाली धातु होने के कारण, एल्युमीनियम विद्युत का सुचालक होता है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
यह तत्व ठोस, धात्विक तथा विद्युत का सुचालक है।

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q43 - Matching atomic radii of second period elements

questiontext.text:
Match the correct atomic radius (in \(\text{pm}\)) with the element.

तत्व के साथ सही परमाणु त्रिज्या (\(\text{pm}\) में) का मिलान कीजिए।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Across a period from left to right in the periodic table, electrons are added to the same valence shell while the nuclear charge increases. This increases the effective nuclear charge and pulls the valence electrons closer to the nucleus, causing atomic radius to decrease.

Step 2: Ordering the Given Elements
The given elements belong to the second period in the order of increasing atomic number: \(\text{Be}\,(Z=4)\), \(\text{B}\,(Z=5)\), \(\text{C}\,(Z=6)\), \(\text{N}\,(Z=7)\), and \(\text{O}\,(Z=8)\). Therefore, their atomic radii decrease in the order \(\text{Be} > \text{B} > \text{C} > \text{N} > \text{O}\).

Step 3: Matching Values
Arranging the given radii in decreasing order gives \(111\,\text{pm} > 88\,\text{pm} > 77\,\text{pm} > 74\,\text{pm} > 66\,\text{pm}\). Assigning them in order yields \(\text{Be} = 111\,\text{pm}\), \(\text{B} = 88\,\text{pm}\), \(\text{C} = 77\,\text{pm}\), \(\text{N} = 74\,\text{pm}\), and \(\text{O} = 66\,\text{pm}\).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct matches are \(\text{Be} \rightarrow 111\,\text{pm}\), \(\text{C} \rightarrow 77\,\text{pm}\), \(\text{O} \rightarrow 66\,\text{pm}\), \(\text{B} \rightarrow 88\,\text{pm}\), and \(\text{N} \rightarrow 74\,\text{pm}\).

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
आवर्त सारणी में किसी आवर्त में बाएँ से दाएँ जाने पर इलेक्ट्रॉन उसी संयोजकता कोश में जुड़ते हैं जबकि नाभिकीय आवेश बढ़ता है। इससे प्रभावी नाभिकीय आवेश बढ़ता है और संयोजकता इलेक्ट्रॉन नाभिक के अधिक निकट खिंचते हैं, जिसके कारण परमाणु त्रिज्या घटती है।

चरण 2: दिए गए तत्वों का क्रम
दिए गए तत्व दूसरे आवर्त से संबंधित हैं और बढ़ते परमाणु क्रमांक के क्रम में हैं: \(\text{Be}\,(Z=4)\), \(\text{B}\,(Z=5)\), \(\text{C}\,(Z=6)\), \(\text{N}\,(Z=7)\), और \(\text{O}\,(Z=8)\)। अतः उनकी परमाणु त्रिज्याएँ \(\text{Be} > \text{B} > \text{C} > \text{N} > \text{O}\) के क्रम में घटती हैं।

चरण 3: मानों का मिलान
दी गई त्रिज्याओं को घटते क्रम में रखने पर \(111\,\text{pm} > 88\,\text{pm} > 77\,\text{pm} > 74\,\text{pm} > 66\,\text{pm}\) प्राप्त होता है। इस क्रम में मान निर्धारित करने पर \(\text{Be} = 111\,\text{pm}\), \(\text{B} = 88\,\text{pm}\), \(\text{C} = 77\,\text{pm}\), \(\text{N} = 74\,\text{pm}\), तथा \(\text{O} = 66\,\text{pm}\) प्राप्त होता है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
सही मिलान \(\text{Be} \rightarrow 111\,\text{pm}\), \(\text{C} \rightarrow 77\,\text{pm}\), \(\text{O} \rightarrow 66\,\text{pm}\), \(\text{B} \rightarrow 88\,\text{pm}\), और \(\text{N} \rightarrow 74\,\text{pm}\) हैं।

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q44 - Matching ionisation and electron gain enthalpies

questiontext.text:
Match the correct ionisation enthalpies (\(\Delta_i H_1, \Delta_i H_2\) in \(\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\)) and electron gain enthalpies (\(\Delta_{eg} H\) in \(\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\)) of the following elements.

निम्नलिखित तत्वों की सही आयनन एन्थैल्पी (\(\Delta_i H_1, \Delta_i H_2\), \(\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\) में) और इलेक्ट्रॉन लब्धि एन्थैल्पी (\(\Delta_{eg} H\), \(\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\) में) का मिलान कीजिए।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Most Reactive Non-Metal
The most reactive non-metal (such as a halogen) has a high first ionisation enthalpy and a very large negative electron gain enthalpy because it readily gains an electron to attain a noble gas configuration. Thus, it corresponds to \(\Delta_i H_1 = 1681\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\), \(\Delta_i H_2 = 3374\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\), \(\Delta_{eg} H = -328\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Most Reactive Metal
The most reactive metal (an alkali metal) has a very low first ionisation enthalpy and a very large jump to the second ionisation enthalpy because removing the second electron disrupts a stable noble gas core. Thus, it corresponds to \(\Delta_i H_1 = 419\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\), \(\Delta_i H_2 = 3051\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\), \(\Delta_{eg} H = -48\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\).

Step 3: Least Reactive Element
The least reactive element (a noble gas) has a completely filled valence shell, resulting in the highest ionisation enthalpies and a positive electron gain enthalpy. Thus, it corresponds to \(\Delta_i H_1 = 2372\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\), \(\Delta_i H_2 = 5251\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\), \(\Delta_{eg} H = +48\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\).

Step 4: Metal Forming Binary Halide
An alkaline earth metal forms a binary halide \(\text{MX}_2\) by losing two valence electrons; hence its first and second ionisation enthalpies are both moderate without an abrupt noble-gas-core jump between \(\Delta_i H_1\) and \(\Delta_i H_2\). Thus, it corresponds to \(\Delta_i H_1 = 738\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\), \(\Delta_i H_2 = 1451\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\), \(\Delta_{eg} H = -40\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\).

चरण 1: सबसे अधिक अभिक्रियाशील अधातु
सबसे अधिक अभिक्रियाशील अधातु (जैसे हैलोजन) की प्रथम आयनन एन्थैल्पी उच्च होती है और इलेक्ट्रॉन लब्धि एन्थैल्पी अत्यधिक ऋणात्मक होती है क्योंकि यह उत्कृष्ट गैस विन्यास प्राप्त करने के लिए सरलता से इलेक्ट्रॉन ग्रहण करता है। अतः यह \(\Delta_i H_1 = 1681\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\), \(\Delta_i H_2 = 3374\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\), \(\Delta_{eg} H = -328\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\) से मेल खाता है।

चरण 2: सबसे अधिक अभिक्रियाशील धातु
सबसे अधिक अभिक्रियाशील धातु (क्षार धातु) की प्रथम आयनन एन्थैल्पी बहुत कम होती है और द्वितीय आयनन एन्थैल्पी में बहुत बड़ा उछाल होता है क्योंकि दूसरा इलेक्ट्रॉन निकालने से स्थायी उत्कृष्ट गैस क्रोड भंग होता है। अतः यह \(\Delta_i H_1 = 419\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\), \(\Delta_i H_2 = 3051\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\), \(\Delta_{eg} H = -48\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\) से मेल खाता है।

चरण 3: सबसे कम अभिक्रियाशील तत्व
सबसे कम अभिक्रियाशील तत्व (उत्कृष्ट गैस) का संयोजकता कोश पूर्णतः भरा होता है, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप इसकी आयनन एन्थैल्पी सर्वाधिक तथा इलेक्ट्रॉन लब्धि एन्थैल्पी धनात्मक होती है। अतः यह \(\Delta_i H_1 = 2372\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\), \(\Delta_i H_2 = 5251\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\), \(\Delta_{eg} H = +48\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\) से मेल खाता है।

चरण 4: द्विअंगी हैलाइड बनाने वाली धातु
क्षारीय मृदा धातु दो संयोजकता इलेक्ट्रॉन त्यागकर द्विअंगी हैलाइड \(\text{MX}_2\) बनाती है; इसलिए इसकी प्रथम और द्वितीय आयनन एन्थैल्पी दोनों मध्यम होती हैं और \(\Delta_i H_1\) तथा \(\Delta_i H_2\) के बीच कोई अचानक बड़ा उछाल नहीं होता। अतः यह \(\Delta_i H_1 = 738\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\), \(\Delta_i H_2 = 1451\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\), \(\Delta_{eg} H = -40\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\) से मेल खाता है।

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q45 - Matching electronic configurations with electron gain enthalpy

questiontext.text:
Electronic configuration of some elements is given below. Match the electronic configuration with its electron gain enthalpy (in \(\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\)).

कुछ तत्वों के इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास नीचे दिए गए हैं। इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास का उसकी इलेक्ट्रॉन लब्धि एन्थैल्पी (\(\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\) में) से मिलान कीजिए।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Noble Gas Configuration \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6\)
This configuration corresponds to neon, which has completely filled orbitals. Adding an extra electron requires placing it in the next higher principal quantum level, so energy must be supplied, giving a positive electron gain enthalpy of \(+48\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Alkali Metal Configuration \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^1\)
This configuration corresponds to sodium. It has a low tendency to gain an electron (since it prefers to lose one electron to achieve a noble gas core), resulting in a small negative electron gain enthalpy of \(-53\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\).

Step 3: Halogen Configuration \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^5\)
This configuration corresponds to fluorine, which needs only one electron to complete its octet and attain a stable noble gas configuration. Thus, it releases a large amount of energy on gaining an electron, giving \(-328\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\).

Step 4: Chalcogen Configuration \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^4\)
This configuration corresponds to oxygen. It has a moderately high tendency to gain an electron (greater than sodium, less than fluorine), giving an electron gain enthalpy of \(-141\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\).

चरण 1: उत्कृष्ट गैस विन्यास \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6\)
यह विन्यास निऑन का है, जिसके कक्षक पूर्णतः भरे होते हैं। एक अतिरिक्त इलेक्ट्रॉन जोड़ने के लिए उसे अगले उच्च मुख्य क्वांटम स्तर में रखना पड़ता है, इसलिए ऊर्जा देनी पड़ती है, जिससे धनात्मक इलेक्ट्रॉन लब्धि एन्थैल्पी \(+48\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\) प्राप्त होती है।

चरण 2: क्षार धातु विन्यास \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^1\)
यह विन्यास सोडियम का है। इसमें इलेक्ट्रॉन ग्रहण करने की प्रवृत्ति कम होती है (क्योंकि यह उत्कृष्ट गैस क्रोड प्राप्त करने के लिए एक इलेक्ट्रॉन त्यागना पसंद करता है), जिसके परिणामस्वरूप कम ऋणात्मक इलेक्ट्रॉन लब्धि एन्थैल्पी \(-53\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\) होती है।

चरण 3: हैलोजन विन्यास \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^5\)
यह विन्यास फ्लुओरीन का है, जिसे अपना अष्टक पूरा करने और स्थायी उत्कृष्ट गैस विन्यास प्राप्त करने के लिए केवल एक इलेक्ट्रॉन की आवश्यकता होती है। अतः इलेक्ट्रॉन ग्रहण करने पर यह अत्यधिक ऊर्जा मुक्त करता है, जिससे \(-328\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\) प्राप्त होता है।

चरण 4: चाल्कोजन विन्यास \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^4\)
यह विन्यास ऑक्सीजन का है। इसमें इलेक्ट्रॉन ग्रहण करने की प्रवृत्ति मध्यम रूप से उच्च होती है (सोडियम से अधिक, फ्लुओरीन से कम), जिससे इलेक्ट्रॉन लब्धि एन्थैल्पी \(-141\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\) प्राप्त होती है।

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_ASSERTIONREASON_Q46 - Periodic trend of ionisation enthalpy across period

questiontext.text:
In the following question a statement of Assertion (A) followed by a statement of Reason (R) is given. Choose the correct option out of the choices given below.

Assertion (A): Generally, ionisation enthalpy increases from left to right in a period.

Reason (R): When successive electrons are added to the orbitals in the same principal quantum level, the shielding effect of inner core of electrons does not increase very much to compensate for the increased attraction of the electron to the nucleus.

निम्नलिखित प्रश्न में अभिकथन (A) के बाद कारण (R) का कथन दिया गया है। नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही विकल्प चुनिए।

अभिकथन (A): सामान्यतः आवर्त में बाएँ से दाएँ जाने पर आयनन एन्थैल्पी बढ़ती है।

कारण (R): जब एक ही मुख्य क्वांटम स्तर के कक्षकों में क्रमिक रूप से इलेक्ट्रॉन जोड़े जाते हैं, तो आंतरिक क्रोड के इलेक्ट्रॉनों का परिरक्षण प्रभाव इतना अधिक नहीं बढ़ता कि वह नाभिक के प्रति इलेक्ट्रॉन के बढ़े हुए आकर्षण की क्षतिपूर्ति कर सके।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the Assertion
Across a period from left to right, the atomic number increases and the atomic size generally decreases, making it harder to remove the outermost electron. Hence, ionisation enthalpy generally increases from left to right in a period, so the assertion is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Reason
As electrons are added successively to the same principal quantum shell, the shielding by the inner-core electrons remains nearly constant and does not offset the increase in nuclear charge. Consequently, the effective nuclear charge increases, so the reason is also correct.

Step 3: Connection and Final Conclusion
Because the increased nuclear attraction is not compensated by shielding, more energy is required to remove a valence electron across a period. Therefore, both the assertion and the reason are correct statements, and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.

चरण 1: अभिकथन का मूल्यांकन
आवर्त में बाएँ से दाएँ जाने पर परमाणु क्रमांक बढ़ता है और परमाणु आकार सामान्यतः घटता है, जिससे बाह्यतम इलेक्ट्रॉन को निकालना अधिक कठिन हो जाता है। अतः आवर्त में बाएँ से दाएँ आयनन एन्थैल्पी सामान्यतः बढ़ती है, इसलिए अभिकथन सही है।

चरण 2: कारण का मूल्यांकन
जब इलेक्ट्रॉन क्रमिक रूप से एक ही मुख्य क्वांटम कोश में जोड़े जाते हैं, तो आंतरिक क्रोड के इलेक्ट्रॉनों द्वारा परिरक्षण लगभग स्थिर रहता है और बढ़े हुए नाभिकीय आवेश की क्षतिपूर्ति नहीं कर पाता। परिणामस्वरूप प्रभावी नाभिकीय आवेश बढ़ता है, इसलिए कारण भी सही है।

चरण 3: संबंध और अंतिम निष्कर्ष
चूँकि बढ़ा हुआ नाभिकीय आकर्षण परिरक्षण द्वारा संतुलित नहीं होता, इसलिए आवर्त में संयोजकता इलेक्ट्रॉन को निकालने के लिए अधिक ऊर्जा की आवश्यकता होती है। अतः अभिकथन और कारण दोनों सही कथन हैं तथा कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या है।

answer.text: Assertion is correct statement and reason is wrong statement.
Assertion and reason both are correct statements and reason is correct explanation of assertion.
Assertion and reason both are wrong statements.
Assertion is wrong statement and reason is correct statement.

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_ASSERTIONREASON_Q47 - First ionisation enthalpy of boron vs beryllium

questiontext.text:
In the following question a statement of Assertion (A) followed by a statement of Reason (R) is given. Choose the correct option out of the choices given below.

Assertion (A): Boron has a smaller first ionisation enthalpy than beryllium.

Reason (R): The penetration of a \(2s\) electron to the nucleus is more than the \(2p\) electron hence \(2p\) electron is more shielded by the inner core of electrons than the \(2s\) electrons.

निम्नलिखित प्रश्न में अभिकथन (A) के बाद कारण (R) का कथन दिया गया है। नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही विकल्प चुनिए।

अभिकथन (A): बोरॉन की प्रथम आयनन एन्थैल्पी बेरिलियम से कम होती है।

कारण (R): नाभिक के प्रति \(2s\) इलेक्ट्रॉन की वेधन क्षमता \(2p\) इलेक्ट्रॉन की तुलना में अधिक होती है, इसलिए \(2p\) इलेक्ट्रॉन \(2s\) इलेक्ट्रॉनों की अपेक्षा आंतरिक क्रोड के इलेक्ट्रॉनों द्वारा अधिक परिरक्षित होता है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the Assertion
Beryllium has the electronic configuration \(1s^2 2s^2\), whereas boron has \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^1\). Experimentally and theoretically, the first ionisation enthalpy of boron (\(801\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\)) is smaller than that of beryllium (\(899\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\)), so the assertion is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Reason
Within the same principal shell, an \(s\) orbital has greater penetration power toward the nucleus than a \(p\) orbital. Therefore, the \(2p\) electron in boron is farther on average and more strongly shielded by the inner \(1s^2\) and \(2s^2\) electrons than a \(2s\) electron in beryllium is shielded by the \(1s^2\) core. Thus, the reason is correct.

Step 3: Connection and Final Conclusion
Because the \(2p\) electron is more shielded and experiences less nuclear attraction, it requires less energy to remove than a \(2s\) electron from beryllium. Therefore, both the assertion and the reason are correct statements, and the reason is the correct explanation for the assertion.

चरण 1: अभिकथन का मूल्यांकन
बेरिलियम का इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास \(1s^2 2s^2\) होता है, जबकि बोरॉन का विन्यास \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^1\) होता है। प्रायोगिक और सैद्धांतिक रूप से, बोरॉन की प्रथम आयनन एन्थैल्पी (\(801\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\)) बेरिलियम (\(899\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\)) से कम होती है, इसलिए अभिकथन सही है।

चरण 2: कारण का मूल्यांकन
एक ही मुख्य कोश में, \(s\) कक्षक की नाभिक के प्रति वेधन क्षमता \(p\) कक्षक से अधिक होती है। अतः बोरॉन में \(2p\) इलेक्ट्रॉन, बेरिलियम में \(2s\) इलेक्ट्रॉन की तुलना में आंतरिक इलेक्ट्रॉनों द्वारा अधिक परिरक्षित होता है। इस प्रकार, कारण भी सही है।

चरण 3: संबंध और अंतिम निष्कर्ष
चूँकि \(2p\) इलेक्ट्रॉन अधिक परिरक्षित होता है और कम नाभिकीय आकर्षण अनुभव करता है, इसलिए इसे निकालने के लिए बेरिलियम के \(2s\) इलेक्ट्रॉन की तुलना में कम ऊर्जा की आवश्यकता होती है। अतः अभिकथन और कारण दोनों सही कथन हैं तथा कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या है।

answer.text: Assertion and reason both are correct statements but reason is not correct explanation for assertion.
Assertion is correct statement but reason is wrong statement.
Assertion and reason both are correct statements and reason is correct explanation for assertion.
Assertion and reason both are wrong statements.

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_ASSERTIONREASON_Q48 - Electron gain enthalpy trend down a group

questiontext.text:
In the following question a statement of Assertion (A) followed by a statement of Reason (R) is given. Choose the correct option out of the choices given below.

Assertion (A): Electron gain enthalpy becomes less negative as we go down a group.

Reason (R): Size of the atom increases on going down the group and the added electron would be farther from the nucleus.

निम्नलिखित प्रश्न में अभिकथन (A) के बाद कारण (R) का कथन दिया गया है। नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही विकल्प चुनिए।

अभिकथन (A): वर्ग में नीचे जाने पर इलेक्ट्रॉन लब्धि एन्थैल्पी कम ऋणात्मक होती जाती है।

कारण (R): वर्ग में नीचे जाने पर परमाणु का आकार बढ़ता है और जोड़ा गया इलेक्ट्रॉन नाभिक से अधिक दूर होगा।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the Assertion
Electron gain enthalpy does not uniformly become less negative down every group. For example, in group 16 and group 17, the electron gain enthalpy of oxygen (\(-141\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\)) is less negative than that of sulphur (\(-200\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\)), and that of fluorine (\(-328\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\)) is less negative than that of chlorine (\(-349\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\)) because of strong interelectronic repulsion in the compact \(2p\) orbitals. Therefore, the assertion is wrong as an unqualified statement.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Reason
As we move down a group, new electron shells are added, so the atomic size increases and the incoming electron enters a shell farther from the nucleus. Therefore, the reason is a correct statement.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The assertion is a wrong statement, whereas the reason is a correct statement.

चरण 1: अभिकथन का मूल्यांकन
प्रत्येक वर्ग में नीचे जाने पर इलेक्ट्रॉन लब्धि एन्थैल्पी एकसमान रूप से कम ऋणात्मक नहीं होती। उदाहरण के लिए, वर्ग 16 और वर्ग 17 में, ऑक्सीजन (\(-141\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\)) की इलेक्ट्रॉन लब्धि एन्थैल्पी सल्फर (\(-200\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\)) की तुलना में कम ऋणात्मक होती है, तथा फ्लुओरीन (\(-328\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\)) की इलेक्ट्रॉन लब्धि एन्थैल्पी क्लोरीन (\(-349\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\)) की तुलना में कम ऋणात्मक होती है क्योंकि छोटे \(2p\) कक्षकों में अंतरा-इलेक्ट्रॉनिक प्रतिकर्षण अधिक होता है। अतः बिना अपवाद के कथन के रूप में अभिकथन गलत है।

चरण 2: कारण का मूल्यांकन
वर्ग में नीचे जाने पर नए इलेक्ट्रॉन कोश जुड़ते हैं, जिससे परमाणु का आकार बढ़ता है और आने वाला इलेक्ट्रॉन नाभिक से अधिक दूर स्थित कोश में प्रवेश करता है। अतः कारण एक सही कथन है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अभिकथन गलत कथन है, जबकि कारण सही कथन है।

answer.text: Assertion and reason both are correct statements but reason is not correct explanation for assertion.
Assertion and reason both are correct statements and reason is correct explanation for assertion.
Assertion and reason both are wrong statements.
Assertion is wrong statement but reason is correct statement.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQI_Q01 - Isostructural species having same shape and hybridisation

questiontext.text: 1. Isostructural species are those which have the same shape and hybridisation. Among the given species identify the isostructural pairs.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Isostructural species possess the same hybridisation of the central atom and the same molecular geometry (shape), which is determined by the number of bond pairs and lone pairs around the central atom according to VSEPR theory.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pair
In \(\mathrm{NF}_3\), nitrogen has 3 bond pairs and 1 lone pair (\(sp^3\) hybridisation, trigonal pyramidal shape), whereas in \(\mathrm{BF}_3\), boron has 3 bond pairs and 0 lone pairs (\(sp^2\) hybridisation, trigonal planar shape).
In \(\mathrm{BF}_4^-\), boron has 4 bond pairs and 0 lone pairs (\(sp^3\) hybridisation, tetrahedral shape). Similarly, in \(\mathrm{NH}_4^+\), nitrogen has 4 bond pairs and 0 lone pairs (\(sp^3\) hybridisation, tetrahedral shape).
In \(\mathrm{BCl}_3\), boron is \(sp^2\) hybridised (trigonal planar), while in \(\mathrm{BrCl}_3\), bromine has 3 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs (\(sp^3d\) hybridisation, T-shaped).
In \(\mathrm{NH}_3\), nitrogen is \(sp^3\) hybridised (trigonal pyramidal), while in \(\mathrm{NO}_3^-\), nitrogen is \(sp^2\) hybridised (trigonal planar).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Only the pair \(\mathrm{BF}_4^-\) and \(\mathrm{NH}_4^+\) shares both \(sp^3\) hybridisation and tetrahedral geometry, making them isostructural.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQI_Q02 - Molecule with the highest dipole moment

questiontext.text: 2. Polarity in a molecule and hence the dipole moment depends primarily on electronegativity of the constituent atoms and shape of a molecule. Which of the following has the highest dipole moment?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The net dipole moment of a polyatomic molecule is the vector sum of all individual bond dipole moments and lone-pair contributions. Both electronegativity difference and molecular symmetry determine the resultant dipole moment.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Species
Carbon dioxide (\(\mathrm{CO}_2\)) is a linear, symmetrical molecule in which the two equal and opposite \(\mathrm{C=O}\) bond dipoles cancel each other out, giving a zero dipole moment (\(\mu = 0\text{ D}\)).
Hydrogen iodide (\(\mathrm{HI}\)) has a very small electronegativity difference between hydrogen and iodine, resulting in a low dipole moment (\(\approx 0.44\text{ D}\)).
Sulfur dioxide (\(\mathrm{SO}_2\)) has a bent shape, but the electronegativity difference between sulfur and oxygen is smaller than that between oxygen and hydrogen, and its bond angle is larger (\(\approx 119^\circ\)), giving \(\mu \approx 1.62\text{ D}\).
Water (\(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)) has a bent structure (bond angle \(\approx 104.5^\circ\)) with a large electronegativity difference between oxygen and hydrogen, and both bond dipoles and the two lone pairs reinforce in the same direction, yielding a high dipole moment (\(\approx 1.85\text{ D}\)).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) has the highest dipole moment among the given molecules.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQI_Q03 - Hybrid orbitals of nitrogen in NO2+ NO3- NH4+

questiontext.text: 3. The types of hybrid orbitals of nitrogen in \(\mathrm{NO}_2^+\), \(\mathrm{NO}_3^-\) and \(\mathrm{NH}_4^+\) respectively are expected to be

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The three nitrogen-containing ions are \(\mathrm{NO}_2^+\), \(\mathrm{NO}_3^-\), and \(\mathrm{NH}_4^+\). Nitrogen has 5 valence electrons.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Using the steric number formula \(H = \frac{1}{2}(V + M - C + A)\), where \(V\) is the number of valence electrons of the central atom, \(M\) is the number of monovalent atoms attached, \(C\) is the cationic charge, and \(A\) is the anionic charge (oxygen is divalent, so \(M = 0\) for oxygen).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
A steric number of \(2\) corresponds to \(sp\) hybridisation, \(3\) corresponds to \(sp^2\) hybridisation, and \(4\) corresponds to \(sp^3\) hybridisation.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
For \(\mathrm{NO}_2^+\): \(H = \frac{1}{2}(5 + 0 - 1 + 0) = 2 \implies sp\) hybridisation.
For \(\mathrm{NO}_3^-\): \(H = \frac{1}{2}(5 + 0 - 0 + 1) = 3 \implies sp^2\) hybridisation.
For \(\mathrm{NH}_4^+\): \(H = \frac{1}{2}(5 + 4 - 1 + 0) = 4 \implies sp^3\) hybridisation.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
All three ions have zero lone pairs on nitrogen and 2, 3, and 4 \(\sigma\)-bond regions respectively, confirming the hybridisations \(sp\), \(sp^2\), and \(sp^3\).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQI_Q04 - Decreasing order of boiling points of H2O HF NH3

questiontext.text: 4. Hydrogen bonds are formed in many compounds e.g., \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\), \(\mathrm{HF}\), \(\mathrm{NH}_3\). The boiling point of such compounds depends to a large extent on the strength of hydrogen bond and the number of hydrogen bonds. The correct decreasing order of the boiling points of above compounds is :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The boiling point of a hydrogen-bonded molecular liquid depends on both the strength of individual hydrogen bonds (governed by electronegativity) and the average number of hydrogen bonds formed per molecule.

Step 2: Evaluation
Although the \(\mathrm{H-F}\) hydrogen bond is stronger than the \(\mathrm{O-H}\) hydrogen bond due to fluorine's higher electronegativity, each \(\mathrm{HF}\) molecule can form only two hydrogen bonds (one via \(\mathrm{H}\) and one via \(\mathrm{F}\)), leading to zig-zag chains. In contrast, each \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) molecule has two hydrogen atoms and two lone pairs on oxygen, allowing it to form four hydrogen bonds in a three-dimensional network. Ammonia (\(\mathrm{NH}_3\)) has weaker hydrogen bonds because nitrogen is less electronegative than both oxygen and fluorine, and it has only one lone pair per molecule.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Consequently, the decreasing order of boiling points is \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} > \mathrm{HF} > \mathrm{NH}_3\).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQI_Q05 - Formal charge on oxygen atom in PO43- ion

questiontext.text: 5. In \(\mathrm{PO}_4^{3-}\) ion the formal charge on the oxygen atom of \(\mathrm{P–O}\) bond is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The phosphate ion \(\mathrm{PO}_4^{3-}\) has a total charge of \(-3\) distributed over 4 equivalent oxygen atoms bonded to a central phosphorus atom.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Due to resonance among four equivalent canonical structures (each having three \(\mathrm{P-O^-}\) single bonds and one \(\mathrm{P=O}\) double bond), all four \(\mathrm{P-O}\) bonds are equivalent and share the negative charge equally.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The average formal charge on each oxygen atom in a symmetrical resonance hybrid is given by:
\[\text{Average formal charge} = \frac{\text{Total charge on the oxygen atoms}}{\text{Total number of equivalent oxygen atoms}}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
In each canonical structure, three oxygen atoms carry a formal charge of \(-1\) and one oxygen atom carries \(0\), giving a total charge of \(-3\) across 4 oxygen atoms:
\[\text{Average formal charge on each O atom} = \frac{-3}{4} = -0.75\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Summing \(-0.75\) over the 4 oxygen atoms gives \(-3\), matching the overall charge of \(\mathrm{PO}_4^{3-}\). Thus, the formal charge on each oxygen atom of the \(\mathrm{P-O}\) bond is \(-0.75\).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQI_Q06 - Bond pairs and lone pairs on nitrogen in NO3-

questiontext.text: 6. In \(\mathrm{NO}_3^-\) ion, the number of bond pairs and lone pairs of electrons on nitrogen atom are

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
We consider the nitrate ion \(\mathrm{NO}_3^-\), where nitrogen (\(\mathrm{N}\), atomic number 7) is the central atom bonded to three oxygen atoms, with an overall charge of \(-1\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Nitrogen belongs to Group 15 and has 5 valence electrons. Since it is a second-period element, it cannot expand its octet beyond 8 valence electrons (4 electron pairs).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Total valence electrons in \(\mathrm{NO}_3^- = 5 + 3(6) + 1 = 24\) electrons (12 pairs). In the Lewis structure, nitrogen forms one \(\mathrm{N=O}\) double bond, one \(\mathrm{N-O^-}\) single bond, and one coordinate (dative) \(\mathrm{N\rightarrow O}\) bond.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Each single bond accounts for 1 shared pair of electrons and the double bond accounts for 2 shared pairs of electrons around nitrogen. Thus, the total number of bond pairs shared by nitrogen is \(1 + 1 + 2 = 4\). Since all 8 electrons around nitrogen are involved in bonding, the number of lone pairs on the nitrogen atom is \(0\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Nitrogen has 4 bond pairs and 0 lone pairs of electrons, satisfying the octet rule.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQI_Q07 - Species having tetrahedral geometry

questiontext.text: 7. Which of the following species has tetrahedral geometry?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
According to VSEPR theory, a species adopts a tetrahedral molecular geometry when its central atom has 4 bond pairs and 0 lone pairs (\(sp^3\) hybridisation).

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Species
In \(\mathrm{BH}_4^-\), boron (3 valence electrons) gains 1 electron from the negative charge to form 4 \(\mathrm{B-H}\) single bonds with 0 lone pairs, resulting in \(sp^3\) hybridisation and tetrahedral geometry.
In \(\mathrm{NH}_2^-\), nitrogen has 2 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs, giving a bent (V-shaped) geometry.
In \(\mathrm{CO}_3^{2-}\), carbon has 3 \(\sigma\)-bond pairs and 0 lone pairs (\(sp^2\) hybridisation), giving a trigonal planar geometry.
In \(\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{O}^+\), oxygen has 3 bond pairs and 1 lone pair, giving a trigonal pyramidal geometry.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, \(\mathrm{BH}_4^-\) has tetrahedral geometry.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQI_Q08 - Number of pi and sigma bonds in naphthalene

questiontext.text: 8. Number of \(\pi\) bonds and \(\sigma\) bonds in the following structure is—

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The given diagram represents the molecular structure of naphthalene (\(\mathrm{C}_{10}\mathrm{H}_8\)), consisting of two fused six-membered carbon rings with 8 attached hydrogen atoms and alternating double bonds.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Every single covalent bond consists of \(1\,\sigma\) bond, and every double covalent bond consists of \(1\,\sigma\) bond and \(1\,\pi\) bond.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Total \(\pi\) bonds = number of double bonds.
Total \(\sigma\) bonds = (number of \(\mathrm{C-C}\) linkages) + (number of \(\mathrm{C-H}\) bonds).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Counting the double bonds in the two fused rings gives 5 double bonds, so there are \(5\,\pi\) bonds.
Counting the \(\sigma\) bonds: there are 11 \(\mathrm{C-C}\) \(\sigma\) bonds forming the bicyclic framework (6 in the first ring + 5 additional bonds in the fused second ring) and 8 \(\mathrm{C-H}\) \(\sigma\) bonds.
Total \(\sigma\) bonds = \(11 + 8 = 19\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The structure contains \(5\,\pi\) bonds and \(19\,\sigma\) bonds.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQI_Q09 - Molecule or ion without unpaired electrons

questiontext.text: 9. Which molecule/ion out of the following does not contain unpaired electrons?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
According to Molecular Orbital Theory (MOT), a species has no unpaired electrons (diamagnetic) if all its molecular orbitals are completely filled with paired electrons.

Step 2: Evaluation of Molecular Orbital Configurations
\(\mathrm{N}_2^+\) has \(14 - 1 = 13\) electrons, an odd number, so it must contain 1 unpaired electron in \(\sigma 2p_z\).
\(\mathrm{O}_2^-\) has \(16 + 1 = 17\) electrons, an odd number, so it contains 1 unpaired electron in \(\pi^* 2p\).
\(\mathrm{O}_2^{2-}\) has \(16 + 2 = 18\) electrons. Its molecular orbital configuration is \(\sigma 1s^2 \sigma^* 1s^2 \sigma 2s^2 \sigma^* 2s^2 \sigma 2p_z^2 (\pi 2p_x^2 = \pi 2p_y^2) (\pi^* 2p_x^2 = \pi^* 2p_y^2)\). Every orbital is fully occupied, so there are 0 unpaired electrons.
\(\mathrm{B}_2\) has 10 electrons, with the last two electrons occupying the degenerate \(\pi 2p_x\) and \(\pi 2p_y\) orbitals singly (by Hund's rule), giving 2 unpaired electrons.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, \(\mathrm{O}_2^{2-}\) does not contain any unpaired electrons.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQI_Q10 - Molecule or ion where all bonds are not equal

questiontext.text: 10. In which of the following molecule/ion all the bonds are not equal?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
All bonds in a molecule or ion are equal if they connect identical pairs of atoms with the same bond order and equivalent hybrid orbital character in a symmetrical geometry.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Species
In \(\mathrm{XeF}_4\) (square planar), \(\mathrm{BF}_4^-\) (tetrahedral), and \(\mathrm{SiF}_4\) (tetrahedral), all bonds are equivalent single bonds between the central atom and identical fluorine atoms.
In ethene (\(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_4\)), there is one \(\mathrm{C=C}\) double bond (bond length \(\approx 134\text{ pm}\)) and four \(\mathrm{C-H}\) single bonds (bond length \(\approx 109\text{ pm}\)).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, all the bonds in \(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_4\) are not equal.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQI_Q11 - Substance with strongest hydrogen bond

questiontext.text: 11. In which of the following substances will hydrogen bond be strongest?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Hydrogen bonding is significant when hydrogen is covalently bonded to a small, highly electronegative atom such as fluorine (\(\mathrm{F}\)), oxygen (\(\mathrm{O}\)), or nitrogen (\(\mathrm{N}\)).

Step 2: Evaluation
Among \(\mathrm{HCl}\), \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\), \(\mathrm{HI}\), and \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S}\), chlorine, iodine, and sulfur have much larger atomic radii and lower electronegativities than oxygen, so they do not form appreciable hydrogen bonds. Oxygen is small and highly electronegative, enabling \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) to form strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, hydrogen bonding is strongest in \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQI_Q12 - Electrons involved in chemical bond formation

questiontext.text: 12. If the electronic configuration of an element is \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 3d^2 4s^2\), the four electrons involved in chemical bond formation will be ____.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
For transition elements (\(d\)-block elements), both the outermost \(ns\) electrons and the penultimate \((n-1)d\) electrons participate in chemical bond formation because their energies are very close.

Step 2: Evaluation
The given electronic configuration \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 3d^2 4s^2\) corresponds to titanium (\(Z = 22\)). Its inner \(1s\) through \(3p\) shells form the stable argon core and do not participate in bonding. The valence electrons available for chemical bonding are the two \(3d\) electrons and two \(4s\) electrons.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Hence, the four electrons involved in chemical bond formation are \(3d^2, 4s^2\).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQI_Q13 - Bond angle corresponding to sp2 hybridisation

questiontext.text: 13. Which of the following angle corresponds to \(sp^2\) hybridisation?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
When one \(s\) orbital and two \(p\) orbitals mix, three equivalent \(sp^2\) hybrid orbitals are formed, oriented in a trigonal planar arrangement to minimize electron-pair repulsion.

Step 2: Evaluation
In a trigonal planar arrangement, the three hybrid orbitals lie in the same plane and are directed toward the corners of an equilateral triangle, resulting in a bond angle of \(360^\circ / 3 = 120^\circ\). (By comparison, \(180^\circ\) corresponds to \(sp\) hybridisation, \(109.5^\circ\) to \(sp^3\), and \(90^\circ\) to octahedral/square planar arrangements.)

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The angle corresponding to \(sp^2\) hybridisation is \(120^\circ\).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQI_Q14 - Stable form of element A from configuration

questiontext.text:
The electronic configurations of three elements, A, B and C are given below.

A\(1s^2\)\(2s^2\)\(2p^6\)
B\(1s^2\)\(2s^2\)\(2p^6\)\(3s^2\)\(3p^3\)
C\(1s^2\)\(2s^2\)\(2p^6\)\(3s^2\)\(3p^5\)

14. Stable form of A may be represented by the formula :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
An element with a completely filled valence shell (an octet in the outermost shell, \(ns^2 np^6\)) is chemically inert and exists as monoatomic species.

Step 2: Evaluation
Element A has the electronic configuration \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6\), which has 8 electrons in its valence shell (corresponding to neon). Because its octet is complete, it has no tendency to gain, lose, or share electrons to form molecules.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the stable form of A is monoatomic, represented by the formula \(\mathrm{A}\).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQI_Q15 - Stable form of element C from configuration

questiontext.text:
The electronic configurations of three elements, A, B and C are given below.

A\(1s^2\)\(2s^2\)\(2p^6\)
B\(1s^2\)\(2s^2\)\(2p^6\)\(3s^2\)\(3p^3\)
C\(1s^2\)\(2s^2\)\(2p^6\)\(3s^2\)\(3p^5\)

15. Stable form of C may be represented by the formula :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Atoms with 7 valence electrons (\(ns^2 np^5\), halogens) require 1 more electron to complete their octet, which they achieve by sharing one pair of electrons with another identical atom to form a covalent diatomic molecule.

Step 2: Evaluation
Element C has the electronic configuration \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^5\) (chlorine). Each atom of C shares one electron with another atom of C to form a single covalent bond (\(\mathrm{C-C}\)), completing the octet of both atoms.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the stable form of C is diatomic, represented by the formula \(\mathrm{C}_2\).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQI_Q16 - Molecular formula of compound formed from B and C

questiontext.text:
The electronic configurations of three elements, A, B and C are given below.

A\(1s^2\)\(2s^2\)\(2p^6\)
B\(1s^2\)\(2s^2\)\(2p^6\)\(3s^2\)\(3p^3\)
C\(1s^2\)\(2s^2\)\(2p^6\)\(3s^2\)\(3p^5\)

16. The molecular formula of the compound formed from B and C will be

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The molecular formula of a simple covalent compound formed between two non-metallic elements is determined by the number of electrons each atom needs to share to complete its octet (its covalency).

Step 2: Evaluation
Element B (\(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^3\), phosphorus) has 5 valence electrons and needs 3 electrons to complete its octet, giving it a valency of 3. Element C (\(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^5\), chlorine) has 7 valence electrons and needs 1 electron to complete its octet, giving it a valency of 1. Therefore, one atom of B shares one electron each with three atoms of C.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The molecular formula of the compound formed from B and C is \(\mathrm{BC}_3\).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQI_Q17 - Nature of bond between elements B and C

questiontext.text:
The electronic configurations of three elements, A, B and C are given below.

A\(1s^2\)\(2s^2\)\(2p^6\)
B\(1s^2\)\(2s^2\)\(2p^6\)\(3s^2\)\(3p^3\)
C\(1s^2\)\(2s^2\)\(2p^6\)\(3s^2\)\(3p^5\)

17. The bond between B and C will be

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A covalent bond is formed by the mutual sharing of electrons between two non-metallic elements that have relatively high ionisation enthalpies and small electronegativity differences.

Step 2: Evaluation
Element B (\(3s^2 3p^3\), phosphorus) and element C (\(3s^2 3p^5\), chlorine) are both \(p\)-block non-metals. Neither element readily loses electrons to form a cation; instead, B shares its three unpaired \(3p\) electrons with three atoms of C to complete the octets of all atoms.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Hence, the bond formed between B and C will be covalent.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQI_Q18 - Correct order of energies of molecular orbitals of N2

questiontext.text: 18. Which of the following order of energies of molecular orbitals of \(\mathrm{N}_2\) is correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
For homonuclear diatomic molecules up to \(\mathrm{N}_2\) (total electrons \(\le 14\)), \(s\text{–}p\) mixing raises the energy of the \(\sigma 2p_z\) molecular orbital above that of the degenerate \(\pi 2p_x\) and \(\pi 2p_y\) bonding molecular orbitals.

Step 2: Evaluation
The complete increasing order of molecular orbital energies for \(\mathrm{N}_2\) is:
\[\sigma 1s < \sigma^* 1s < \sigma 2s < \sigma^* 2s < (\pi 2p_x = \pi 2p_y) < \sigma 2p_z < (\pi^* 2p_x = \pi^* 2p_y) < \sigma^* 2p_z\]
Thus, \((\pi 2p_y)\) is lower in energy than \((\sigma 2p_z)\), which in turn is lower in energy than the degenerate antibonding orbitals \((\pi^* 2p_x) = (\pi^* 2p_y)\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct energy order is \((\pi 2p_y) < (\sigma 2p_z) < (\pi^* 2p_x) = (\pi^* 2p_y)\).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQI_Q19 - Incorrect statement from molecular orbital theory

questiontext.text: 19. Which of the following statement is not correct from the view point of molecular orbital theory?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
According to Molecular Orbital Theory, bond order is \(\frac{1}{2}(N_b - N_a)\), where a zero bond order indicates an unstable molecule, and for diatomic molecules with \(\le 14\) electrons (\(\mathrm{B}_2, \mathrm{C}_2, \mathrm{N}_2\)), \(s\text{–}p\) mixing places \((\pi 2p_x = \pi 2p_y)\) below \(\sigma 2p_z\).

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
\(\mathrm{Be}_2\) has 8 electrons (\(\sigma 1s^2 \sigma^* 1s^2 \sigma 2s^2 \sigma^* 2s^2\)), giving a bond order of \(0\), so it is not stable.
\(\mathrm{He}_2\) has a bond order of \(0\) and is unstable, whereas \(\mathrm{He}_2^+\) has 3 electrons (\(\sigma 1s^2 \sigma^* 1s^1\)) and a bond order of \(0.5\), so it is expected to exist.
\(\mathrm{N}_2\) has a bond order of \(3\), the highest among second-period homonuclear diatomic molecules, giving it maximum bond strength.
However, the energy order \(\sigma 2s < \sigma^* 2s < \sigma 2p_z < (\pi 2p_x = \pi 2p_y) < (\pi^* 2p_x = \pi^* 2p_y) < \sigma^* 2p_z\) applies to \(\mathrm{O}_2\) and \(\mathrm{F}_2\), not \(\mathrm{N}_2\), where \((\pi 2p_x = \pi 2p_y)\) is lower in energy than \(\sigma 2p_z\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the statement placing \(\sigma 2p_z\) below \((\pi 2p_x = \pi 2p_y)\) for \(\mathrm{N}_2\) is not correct.

answer.text: \(\mathrm{He}_2\) is not stable but \(\mathrm{He}_2^+\) is expected to exist.
Bond strength of \(\mathrm{N}_2\) is maximum amongst the homonuclear diatomic molecules belonging to the second period.

The order of energies of molecular orbitals in \(\mathrm{N}_2\) molecule is
\(\sigma 2s < \sigma^* 2s < \sigma 2p_z < (\pi 2p_x = \pi 2p_y) < (\pi^* 2p_x = \pi^* 2p_y) < \sigma^* 2p_z\)

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQI_Q20 - Correct bond order among O2- O2 and O2+

questiontext.text: 20. Which of the following options represents the correct bond order :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The three oxygen species are \(\mathrm{O}_2^-\) (17 electrons), \(\mathrm{O}_2\) (16 electrons), and \(\mathrm{O}_2^+\) (15 electrons).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
All three species follow the molecular orbital energy order for \(\mathrm{O}_2\), where electrons beyond 14 occupy the antibonding \(\pi^* 2p_x\) and \(\pi^* 2p_y\) orbitals.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Bond Order} = \frac{1}{2}(N_b - N_a)\]
where \(N_b\) is the number of bonding electrons and \(N_a\) is the number of antibonding electrons.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
For \(\mathrm{O}_2^-\) (17 electrons): \(N_b = 10\), \(N_a = 7 \implies \text{Bond Order} = \frac{10 - 7}{2} = 1.5\).
For \(\mathrm{O}_2\) (16 electrons): \(N_b = 10\), \(N_a = 6 \implies \text{Bond Order} = \frac{10 - 6}{2} = 2.0\).
For \(\mathrm{O}_2^+\) (15 electrons): \(N_b = 10\), \(N_a = 5 \implies \text{Bond Order} = \frac{10 - 5}{2} = 2.5\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Comparing the values \(1.5 < 2.0 < 2.5\), the correct bond order relationship is \(\mathrm{O}_2^- < \mathrm{O}_2 < \mathrm{O}_2^+\).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQI_Q21 - Outermost electronic configuration of most electronegative element

questiontext.text: 21. The electronic configuration of the outer most shell of the most electronegative element is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Electronegativity increases across a period from left to right and decreases down a group. The most electronegative element in the periodic table is fluorine (\(\mathrm{F}\), atomic number 9).

Step 2: Evaluation
Fluorine has the ground-state electronic configuration \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^5\). Therefore, the electronic configuration of its outermost (valence) shell is \(2s^2 2p^5\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The outermost shell configuration of the most electronegative element is \(2s^2 2p^5\).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQI_Q22 - Element with highest ionisation enthalpy from configuration

questiontext.text: 22. Amongst the following elements whose electronic configurations are given below, the one having the highest ionisation enthalpy is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Ionisation enthalpy generally increases across a period due to increasing effective nuclear charge and decreases down a group due to increasing atomic size. Additionally, elements with exactly half-filled \(p\)-subshells (\(np^3\)) possess extra stability and higher ionisation enthalpies.

Step 2: Evaluation
Comparing the third-period elements: \([\mathrm{Ne}]3s^2 3p^1\) (Al), \([\mathrm{Ne}]3s^2 3p^2\) (Si), and \([\mathrm{Ne}]3s^2 3p^3\) (P), ionisation enthalpy increases from \(3p^1\) to \(3p^3\), with \([\mathrm{Ne}]3s^2 3p^3\) further stabilised by a half-filled \(3p\) subshell. Comparing \([\mathrm{Ne}]3s^2 3p^3\) (P) with \([\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{10} 4s^2 4p^3\) (As), both have half-filled \(p\)-subshells, but phosphorus is smaller (period 3 vs. period 4), so its valence electrons are held more tightly.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the element with electronic configuration \([\mathrm{Ne}]3s^2 3p^3\) has the highest ionisation enthalpy.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQII_Q23 - Species having identical bond order

questiontext.text: 23. Which of the following have identical bond order?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
We are given four diatomic ions: \(\mathrm{CN}^-\), \(\mathrm{NO}^+\), \(\mathrm{O}_2^-\), and \(\mathrm{O}_2^{2-}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Isoelectronic diatomic species have the same molecular orbital electron configuration and therefore the same bond order.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\(\text{Bond Order} = \frac{1}{2}(N_b - N_a)\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\(\mathrm{CN}^-\): \(6 + 7 + 1 = 14\) electrons \(\implies N_b = 10, N_a = 4 \implies \text{Bond Order} = \frac{10 - 4}{2} = 3\).
\(\mathrm{NO}^+\): \(7 + 8 - 1 = 14\) electrons \(\implies N_b = 10, N_a = 4 \implies \text{Bond Order} = \frac{10 - 4}{2} = 3\).
\(\mathrm{O}_2^-\): \(16 + 1 = 17\) electrons \(\implies N_b = 10, N_a = 7 \implies \text{Bond Order} = \frac{10 - 7}{2} = 1.5\).
\(\mathrm{O}_2^{2-}\): \(16 + 2 = 18\) electrons \(\implies N_b = 10, N_a = 8 \implies \text{Bond Order} = \frac{10 - 8}{2} = 1.0\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Both \(\mathrm{CN}^-\) and \(\mathrm{NO}^+\) are 14-electron species with a bond order of \(3\), so they have identical bond order.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQII_Q24 - Molecules attaining linear structure

questiontext.text: 24. Which of the following attain the linear structure:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A triatomic molecule or ion attains a linear structure when the central atom is \(sp\) hybridised with 2 \(\sigma\)-bond pairs and 0 lone pairs, giving a bond angle of \(180^\circ\).

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Species
In \(\mathrm{BeCl}_2\), beryllium has 2 valence electrons and forms 2 \(\mathrm{Be-Cl}\) single bonds with 0 lone pairs (\(sp\) hybridisation), resulting in a linear structure.
In \(\mathrm{CS}_2\), carbon has 4 valence electrons and forms two \(\mathrm{C=S}\) double bonds with 0 lone pairs (\(sp\) hybridisation), resulting in a linear structure.
In \(\mathrm{NO}_2\), nitrogen has an odd electron (17 valence electrons total) and adopts an angular (bent) structure with a bond angle of \(\approx 134^\circ\).
\(\mathrm{NCO}^+\) is not a standard linear species in this context (unlike \(\mathrm{NCO}^-\) which is isoelectronic with \(\mathrm{CO}_2\)).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, \(\mathrm{BeCl}_2\) and \(\mathrm{CS}_2\) attain linear structures.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQII_Q25 - Species isoelectronic with carbon monoxide CO

questiontext.text: 25. \(\mathrm{CO}\) is isoelectronic with

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
We need to identify which species have the same total number of electrons as \(\mathrm{CO}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Isoelectronic species have identical total electron counts (and identical valence electron counts for diatomic species).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Total electrons = sum of atomic numbers of constituent atoms minus positive charge (or plus negative charge).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
For \(\mathrm{CO}\): \(6 + 8 = 14\) electrons.
For \(\mathrm{NO}^+\): \(7 + 8 - 1 = 14\) electrons.
For \(\mathrm{N}_2\): \(7 + 7 = 14\) electrons.
For \(\mathrm{SnCl}_2\): \(50 + 2(17) = 84\) electrons.
For \(\mathrm{NO}_2^-\): \(7 + 2(8) + 1 = 24\) electrons.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Both \(\mathrm{NO}^+\) and \(\mathrm{N}_2\) have 14 electrons and are therefore isoelectronic with \(\mathrm{CO}\).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQII_Q26 - Species having the same molecular shape

questiontext.text: 26. Which of the following species have the same shape?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The shape of a molecule or ion is determined by the arrangement of its bonded atoms around the central atom, which depends on the number of \(\sigma\)-bond pairs and lone pairs (VSEPR theory).

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Species
\(\mathrm{CO}_2\) has 2 \(\sigma\)-bond pairs and 0 lone pairs on carbon (\(sp\) hybridisation), giving a linear shape.
\(\mathrm{CCl}_4\) has 4 \(\sigma\)-bond pairs and 0 lone pairs on carbon (\(sp^3\) hybridisation), giving a tetrahedral shape.
\(\mathrm{O}_3\) has 2 \(\sigma\)-bond pairs and 1 lone pair on the central oxygen atom (\(sp^2\) hybridisation), giving a bent (angular) shape.
\(\mathrm{NO}_2^-\) has 2 \(\sigma\)-bond pairs and 1 lone pair on nitrogen (\(sp^2\) hybridisation), also giving a bent (angular) shape.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, \(\mathrm{O}_3\) and \(\mathrm{NO}_2^-\) have the same (bent) shape.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQII_Q27 - Correct statements about carbonate ion CO32-

questiontext.text: 27. Which of the following statements are correct about \(\mathrm{CO}_3^{2-}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The carbonate ion (\(\mathrm{CO}_3^{2-}\)) is a resonance hybrid of three equivalent canonical structures, each featuring a central carbon atom bonded to three oxygen atoms.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Statement
In \(\mathrm{CO}_3^{2-}\), carbon forms 3 \(\sigma\) bonds and 1 \(\pi\) bond with 0 lone pairs, so the hybridisation of the central carbon atom is \(sp^2\) (not \(sp^3\)).
Each canonical resonance structure has two \(\mathrm{C-O}\) single bonds and one \(\mathrm{C=O}\) double bond (not one single bond and two double bonds).
Because the total \(-2\) charge is distributed equally over three equivalent oxygen atoms across the resonance hybrid, the average formal charge on each oxygen atom has a magnitude of \(\frac{2}{3} \approx 0.67\) units (specifically \(-0.67\)).
Due to resonance averaging, all three \(\mathrm{C-O}\) bonds have identical bond order (\(\frac{4}{3} = 1.33\)) and hence equal bond lengths.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct statements are that the average formal charge on each oxygen atom is \(0.67\) units and that all \(\mathrm{C–O}\) bond lengths are equal.

answer.text: Its resonance structure has one \(\mathrm{C–O}\) single bond and two \(\mathrm{C=O}\) double bonds.
The average formal charge on each oxygen atom is \(0.67\) units.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQII_Q28 - Diamagnetic species among N2 N22- O2 O22-

questiontext.text: 28. Diamagnetic species are those which contain no unpaired electrons. Which among the following are diamagnetic?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
According to Molecular Orbital Theory, a species is diamagnetic when all electrons in its molecular orbitals are paired (zero unpaired electrons).

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Species
\(\mathrm{N}_2\) has 14 electrons: \(\sigma 1s^2 \sigma^* 1s^2 \sigma 2s^2 \sigma^* 2s^2 (\pi 2p_x^2 = \pi 2p_y^2) \sigma 2p_z^2\). All electrons are paired, so \(\mathrm{N}_2\) is diamagnetic.
\(\mathrm{N}_2^{2-}\) has 16 electrons, with the last two electrons occupying the degenerate \(\pi^* 2p_x\) and \(\pi^* 2p_y\) orbitals singly (by Hund's rule), giving 2 unpaired electrons (paramagnetic).
\(\mathrm{O}_2\) has 16 electrons, also with 2 unpaired electrons in \(\pi^* 2p_x^1\) and \(\pi^* 2p_y^1\) (paramagnetic).
\(\mathrm{O}_2^{2-}\) has 18 electrons: \(\sigma 1s^2 \sigma^* 1s^2 \sigma 2s^2 \sigma^* 2s^2 \sigma 2p_z^2 (\pi 2p_x^2 = \pi 2p_y^2) (\pi^* 2p_x^2 = \pi^* 2p_y^2)\). All electrons are paired, so \(\mathrm{O}_2^{2-}\) is diamagnetic.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The diamagnetic species are \(\mathrm{N}_2\) and \(\mathrm{O}_2^{2-}\).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQII_Q29 - Species having same bond order

questiontext.text: 29. Species having same bond order are :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The four diatomic species are \(\mathrm{N}_2\) (14 electrons), \(\mathrm{N}_2^-\) (15 electrons), \(\mathrm{F}_2^+\) (17 electrons), and \(\mathrm{O}_2^-\) (17 electrons).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Isoelectronic diatomic species have identical molecular orbital configurations and therefore identical bond orders.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Bond Order} = \frac{1}{2}(N_b - N_a)\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
For \(\mathrm{N}_2\) (14 electrons): \(N_b = 10, N_a = 4 \implies \text{Bond Order} = \frac{10 - 4}{2} = 3.0\).
For \(\mathrm{N}_2^-\) (15 electrons): \(N_b = 10, N_a = 5 \implies \text{Bond Order} = \frac{10 - 5}{2} = 2.5\).
For \(\mathrm{F}_2^+\) (17 electrons): \(N_b = 10, N_a = 7 \implies \text{Bond Order} = \frac{10 - 7}{2} = 1.5\).
For \(\mathrm{O}_2^-\) (17 electrons): \(N_b = 10, N_a = 7 \implies \text{Bond Order} = \frac{10 - 7}{2} = 1.5\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Both \(\mathrm{F}_2^+\) and \(\mathrm{O}_2^-\) have 17 electrons and a bond order of \(1.5\).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MCQII_Q30 - Incorrect statements about bonding and structure

questiontext.text: 30. Which of the following statements are not correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Electrical conductivity in ionic solids requires mobile ions; resonance canonical structures differ only in electron distribution; hybrid orbitals have greater directional character; and VSEPR theory predicts shapes from bond pairs and lone pairs.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Statement
Solid \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) is a poor conductor of electricity because its \(\mathrm{Na}^+\) and \(\mathrm{Cl}^-\) ions are held rigidly in the crystal lattice and are not free to move (it conducts only in the molten or aqueous state). Hence, calling solid \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) a good conductor is incorrect.
In resonance, canonical structures have the exact same arrangement of atoms (nuclei) and differ only in the arrangement of electrons. Hence, claiming a difference in the arrangement of atoms is incorrect.
Hybrid orbitals overlap more effectively due to directional concentration of electron density, forming stronger bonds than pure atomic orbitals (correct).
VSEPR theory predicts that \(\mathrm{XeF}_4\) has 4 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs on xenon, resulting in a square planar geometry (correct).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The incorrect statements are that \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) is a good conductor of electricity in the solid state and that canonical structures differ in the arrangement of atoms.

answer.text: \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) being an ionic compound is a good conductor of electricity in the solid state.
In canonical structures there is a difference in the arrangement of atoms.
Hybrid orbitals form stronger bonds than pure orbitals.
VSEPR Theory can explain the square planar geometry of \(\mathrm{XeF}_4\).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MATCHING_Q52 - Match species with type of hybrid orbitals

questiontext.text: 52. Match the species in Column I with the type of hybrid orbitals in Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The hybridisation of the central atom is determined by its steric number \(H = \frac{1}{2}(V + M - C + A)\), which equals the sum of \(\sigma\)-bond pairs and lone pairs.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Species
For \(\mathrm{SF}_4\): \(H = \frac{1}{2}(6 + 4) = 5 \implies sp^3d\) hybridisation (4 bond pairs, 1 lone pair).
For \(\mathrm{IF}_5\): \(H = \frac{1}{2}(7 + 5) = 6 \implies sp^3d^2\) hybridisation (5 bond pairs, 1 lone pair, outer \(d\)-orbital).
For \(\mathrm{NO}_2^+\): \(H = \frac{1}{2}(5 + 0 - 1) = 2 \implies sp\) hybridisation (2 \(\sigma\)-bond pairs, 0 lone pairs).
For \(\mathrm{NH}_4^+\): \(H = \frac{1}{2}(5 + 4 - 1) = 4 \implies sp^3\) hybridisation (4 bond pairs, 0 lone pairs).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, \(\mathrm{SF}_4\) matches \(sp^3d\), \(\mathrm{IF}_5\) matches \(sp^3d^2\), \(\mathrm{NO}_2^+\) matches \(sp\), and \(\mathrm{NH}_4^+\) matches \(sp^3\).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MATCHING_Q53 - Match species with geometry or shape

questiontext.text: 53. Match the species in Column I with the geometry/shape in Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Molecular geometry (shape) is determined by the spatial arrangement of bonded atoms around the central atom, accounting for lone-pair repulsions via VSEPR theory.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Species
\(\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{O}^+\) has 3 bond pairs and 1 lone pair on oxygen (\(sp^3\) hybridisation), giving a pyramidal shape.
\(\mathrm{HC \equiv CH}\) (ethyne) has \(sp\) hybridised carbon atoms with 2 \(\sigma\)-bond pairs and 0 lone pairs, giving a linear shape.
\(\mathrm{ClO}_2^-\) has 2 \(\sigma\)-bond pairs and 2 lone pairs on chlorine (\(sp^3\) hybridisation), giving an angular (bent) shape.
\(\mathrm{NH}_4^+\) has 4 bond pairs and 0 lone pairs on nitrogen (\(sp^3\) hybridisation), giving a tetrahedral shape.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, \(\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{O}^+\) is pyramidal, \(\mathrm{HC \equiv CH}\) is linear, \(\mathrm{ClO}_2^-\) is angular, and \(\mathrm{NH}_4^+\) is tetrahedral.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MATCHING_Q54 - Match species with bond order

questiontext.text: 54. Match the species in Column I with the bond order in Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The four diatomic species are \(\mathrm{NO}\) (15 electrons), \(\mathrm{CO}\) (14 electrons), \(\mathrm{O}_2^-\) (17 electrons), and \(\mathrm{O}_2\) (16 electrons).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Bond order is calculated from the molecular orbital electron configuration using \(\text{Bond Order} = \frac{1}{2}(N_b - N_a)\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\(\text{Bond Order} = \frac{1}{2}(N_b - N_a)\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
For \(\mathrm{NO}\) (15 electrons): \(N_b = 10, N_a = 5 \implies \text{Bond Order} = \frac{10 - 5}{2} = 2.5\).
For \(\mathrm{CO}\) (14 electrons): \(N_b = 10, N_a = 4 \implies \text{Bond Order} = \frac{10 - 4}{2} = 3.0\).
For \(\mathrm{O}_2^-\) (17 electrons): \(N_b = 10, N_a = 7 \implies \text{Bond Order} = \frac{10 - 7}{2} = 1.5\).
For \(\mathrm{O}_2\) (16 electrons): \(N_b = 10, N_a = 6 \implies \text{Bond Order} = \frac{10 - 6}{2} = 2.0\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The bond orders are \(\mathrm{NO} \to 2.5\), \(\mathrm{CO} \to 3.0\), \(\mathrm{O}_2^- \to 1.5\), and \(\mathrm{O}_2 \to 2.0\).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MATCHING_Q55 - Match bonding or solid types with examples

questiontext.text: 55. Match the items given in Column I with examples given in Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Different chemical substances exhibit characteristic bonding or crystal lattice types based on their constituent atoms and electronegativities.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Item
Hydrogen bond: \(\mathrm{HF}\) forms strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds due to the high electronegativity of fluorine.
Resonance: Ozone (\(\mathrm{O}_3\)) is a classic resonance hybrid of two equivalent canonical structures.
Ionic solid: \(\mathrm{LiF}\) consists of \(\mathrm{Li}^+\) and \(\mathrm{F}^-\) ions held together by electrostatic attraction in an ionic crystal lattice.
Covalent solid: Carbon (\(\mathrm{C}\), as diamond or graphite) forms an extended three-dimensional or layered covalent network solid.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matches are Hydrogen bond \(\to \mathrm{HF}\), Resonance \(\to \mathrm{O}_3\), Ionic solid \(\to \mathrm{LiF}\), and Covalent solid \(\to \mathrm{C}\).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_MATCHING_Q56 - Match shape of molecules with hybridisation

questiontext.text: 56. Match the shape of molecules in Column I with the type of hybridisation in Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
When there are no lone pairs on the central atom, the molecular shape directly corresponds to the spatial orientation of its hybrid orbitals.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Shape
A tetrahedral shape (bond angle \(109.5^\circ\)) arises from four \(sp^3\) hybrid orbitals.
A trigonal planar shape (bond angle \(120^\circ\)) arises from three \(sp^2\) hybrid orbitals.
A linear shape (bond angle \(180^\circ\)) arises from two \(sp\) hybrid orbitals.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, Tetrahedral matches \(sp^3\), Trigonal matches \(sp^2\), and Linear matches \(sp\).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_AR_Q57 - Stability of sodium chloride and octet acquisition

questiontext.text:
57. Assertion (A) : Sodium chloride formed by the action of chlorine gas on sodium metal is a stable compound.

Reason (R) : This is because sodium and chloride ions acquire octet in sodium chloride formation.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
During ionic bond formation, metal atoms lose valence electrons and non-metal atoms gain electrons so that both ions achieve stable noble-gas (octet) electronic configurations, followed by strong electrostatic attraction in the crystal lattice.

Step 2: Evaluation of Assertion and Reason
Sodium (\([\mathrm{Ne}]3s^1\)) loses one electron to form \(\mathrm{Na}^+\) (\([\mathrm{Ne}]\)), and chlorine (\([\mathrm{Ne}]3s^2 3p^5\)) gains one electron to form \(\mathrm{Cl}^-\) (\([\mathrm{Ar}]\)). Both ions acquire stable octets, and the resulting electrostatic attraction makes sodium chloride a very stable ionic compound. Thus, both the assertion and the reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both A and R are correct, and R is the correct explanation of A.

answer.text: A and R both are correct, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A and R both are correct, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_AR_Q58 - Bond angle comparison between NH3 and H2O

questiontext.text:
58. Assertion (A) : Though the central atom of both \(\mathrm{NH}_3\) and \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) molecules are \(sp^3\) hybridised, yet \(\mathrm{H–N–H}\) bond angle is greater than that of \(\mathrm{H–O–H}\).

Reason (R) : This is because nitrogen atom has one lone pair and oxygen atom has two lone pairs.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
According to VSEPR theory, the magnitude of electron-pair repulsion follows the order: lone pair–lone pair (\(\mathrm{lp–lp}\)) > lone pair–bond pair (\(\mathrm{lp–bp}\)) > bond pair–bond pair (\(\mathrm{bp–bp}\)).

Step 2: Evaluation of Assertion and Reason
Both \(\mathrm{NH}_3\) and \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) have \(sp^3\) hybridised central atoms. However, nitrogen in \(\mathrm{NH}_3\) has 3 bond pairs and 1 lone pair, whereas oxygen in \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) has 2 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs. The stronger \(\mathrm{lp–lp}\) and \(\mathrm{lp–bp}\) repulsions caused by two lone pairs in \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) compress the \(\mathrm{H–O–H}\) bond angle to \(104.5^\circ\), compared to \(107^\circ\) for \(\mathrm{H–N–H}\) in \(\mathrm{NH}_3\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both A and R are correct, and R is the correct explanation of A.

answer.text: A and R both are correct, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A and R both are correct, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_AR_Q59 - Bond dissociation enthalpies of O-H bonds in H2O

questiontext.text:
59. Assertion (A): Among the two \(\mathrm{O–H}\) bonds in \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) molecule, the energy required to break the first \(\mathrm{O–H}\) bond and the other \(\mathrm{O–H}\) bond is the same.

Reason (R) : This is because the electronic environment around oxygen is the same even after breakage of one \(\mathrm{O–H}\) bond.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In a polyatomic molecule, successive bond dissociation enthalpies for identical bonds are not equal because the electronic environment around the central atom changes after the first bond is cleaved.

Step 2: Evaluation of Assertion and Reason
Breaking the first \(\mathrm{O–H}\) bond in \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) produces \(\mathrm{H}^\bullet\) and an \(\mathrm{OH}^\bullet\) radical (\(\Delta H_1^\circ = 502\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\)). The electronic environment around oxygen in the \(\mathrm{OH}^\bullet\) radical differs from that in the intact \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) molecule, so breaking the second \(\mathrm{O–H}\) bond requires a different amount of energy (\(\Delta H_2^\circ = 427\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\)). Therefore, both the assertion and the reason are false.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both A and R are false.

answer.text: A and R both are correct, and R is correct explanation of A.
A and R both are correct, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_COMPREHENSION_Q65 - Formation of molecular orbitals in dioxygen

questiontext.text:
Passage: Molecular orbitals are formed by the overlap of atomic orbitals. Two atomic orbitals combine to form two molecular orbitals called bonding molecular orbital (BMO) and anti bonding molecular orbital (ABMO). Energy of anti bonding orbital is raised above the parent atomic orbitals that have combined and the energy of the bonding orbital is lowered than the parent atomic orbitals. Energies of various molecular orbitals for elements hydrogen to nitrogen increase in the order : \(\sigma 1s < \sigma^* 1s < \sigma 2s < \sigma^* 2s < (\pi 2p_x \simeq \pi 2p_y) < \sigma 2p_z < (\pi^* 2p_x \simeq \pi^* 2p_y) < \sigma^* 2p_z\) and for oxygen and fluorine order of energy of molecular orbitals is given below : \(\sigma 1s < \sigma^* 1s < \sigma 2s < \sigma^* 2s < \sigma 2p_z < (\pi 2p_x \simeq \pi 2p_y) < (\pi^* 2p_x \simeq \pi^* 2p_y) < \sigma^* 2p_z\). Different atomic orbitals of one atom combine with those atomic orbitals of the second atom which have comparable energies and proper orientation. Further, if the overlapping is head on, the molecular orbital is called 'Sigma' (\(\sigma\)) and if the overlap is lateral, the molecular orbital is called 'pi' (\(\pi\)). The molecular orbitals are filled with electrons according to the same rules as followed for filling of atomic orbitals. However, the order for filling is not the same for all molecules or their ions. Bond order is one of the most important parameters to compare the strength of bonds.

65. Which of the following statements is correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
According to Molecular Orbital Theory, the total number of molecular orbitals formed is always equal to the total number of combining atomic orbitals, and half of these are bonding molecular orbitals while the other half are antibonding molecular orbitals.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
Each oxygen atom has 5 atomic orbitals (\(1s, 2s, 2p_x, 2p_y, 2p_z\)) involved in forming \(\mathrm{O}_2\). Combining \(5 + 5 = 10\) atomic orbitals produces 10 molecular orbitals (5 bonding and 5 antibonding).
In \(\mathrm{O}_2\) (16 electrons), the \(\pi^* 2p_x\) and \(\pi^* 2p_y\) orbitals are half-filled and \(\sigma^* 2p_z\) is empty, so not all molecular orbitals are completely filled.
The total number of bonding molecular orbitals (5) is equal to the total number of antibonding molecular orbitals (5).
There are 5 filled bonding orbitals (10 electrons) and 3 occupied antibonding orbitals (6 electrons), so the numbers of filled bonding and antibonding orbitals are not equal.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the only correct statement is that in the formation of dioxygen from oxygen atoms, 10 molecular orbitals will be formed.

answer.text: In the formation of dioxygen from oxygen atoms 10 molecular orbitals will be formed.
All the molecular orbitals in the dioxygen will be completely filled.
Total number of bonding molecular orbitals will not be same as total number of anti bonding orbitals in dioxygen.
Number of filled bonding orbitals will be same as number of filled anti bonding orbitals.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_COMPREHENSION_Q66 - Molecular orbital with maximum nodal planes

questiontext.text:
Passage: Molecular orbitals are formed by the overlap of atomic orbitals. Two atomic orbitals combine to form two molecular orbitals called bonding molecular orbital (BMO) and anti bonding molecular orbital (ABMO). Energy of anti bonding orbital is raised above the parent atomic orbitals that have combined and the energy of the bonding orbital is lowered than the parent atomic orbitals. Energies of various molecular orbitals for elements hydrogen to nitrogen increase in the order : \(\sigma 1s < \sigma^* 1s < \sigma 2s < \sigma^* 2s < (\pi 2p_x \simeq \pi 2p_y) < \sigma 2p_z < (\pi^* 2p_x \simeq \pi^* 2p_y) < \sigma^* 2p_z\) and for oxygen and fluorine order of energy of molecular orbitals is given below : \(\sigma 1s < \sigma^* 1s < \sigma 2s < \sigma^* 2s < \sigma 2p_z < (\pi 2p_x \simeq \pi 2p_y) < (\pi^* 2p_x \simeq \pi^* 2p_y) < \sigma^* 2p_z\). Different atomic orbitals of one atom combine with those atomic orbitals of the second atom which have comparable energies and proper orientation. Further, if the overlapping is head on, the molecular orbital is called 'Sigma' (\(\sigma\)) and if the overlap is lateral, the molecular orbital is called 'pi' (\(\pi\)). The molecular orbitals are filled with electrons according to the same rules as followed for filling of atomic orbitals. However, the order for filling is not the same for all molecules or their ions. Bond order is one of the most important parameters to compare the strength of bonds.

66. Which of the following molecular orbitals has maximum number of nodal planes?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A nodal plane (or nodal surface) is a plane where the electron wave function \(\psi\) changes sign and the probability density \(\psi^2\) is zero. Antibonding molecular orbitals possess an additional nodal plane perpendicular to the internuclear axis between the two nuclei, in addition to the nodal planes inherent to the combining atomic orbitals.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Molecular Orbital
\(\sigma^* 1s\) is formed from two \(1s\) orbitals (0 atomic nodal planes each) combining out of phase, giving 1 nodal plane between the nuclei.
\(\pi 2p_x\) is formed from two \(2p_x\) orbitals combining in phase, giving 1 nodal plane containing the internuclear axis.
\(\pi^* 2p_y\) is formed from two \(2p_y\) orbitals combining out of phase, giving 2 nodal planes (one containing the internuclear axis and one perpendicular to it between the nuclei).
\(\sigma^* 2p_z\) is formed from two \(2p_z\) orbitals combining out of phase along the \(z\)-axis; it retains the two nodal planes passing through each nucleus (from the two \(2p_z\) orbitals) plus the central antibonding nodal plane between the nuclei, giving 3 nodal planes in total.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, \(\sigma^* 2p_z\) has the maximum number of nodal planes (3).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_COMPREHENSION_Q67 - Pair of species having the same bond order

questiontext.text:
Passage: Molecular orbitals are formed by the overlap of atomic orbitals. Two atomic orbitals combine to form two molecular orbitals called bonding molecular orbital (BMO) and anti bonding molecular orbital (ABMO). Energy of anti bonding orbital is raised above the parent atomic orbitals that have combined and the energy of the bonding orbital is lowered than the parent atomic orbitals. Energies of various molecular orbitals for elements hydrogen to nitrogen increase in the order : \(\sigma 1s < \sigma^* 1s < \sigma 2s < \sigma^* 2s < (\pi 2p_x \simeq \pi 2p_y) < \sigma 2p_z < (\pi^* 2p_x \simeq \pi^* 2p_y) < \sigma^* 2p_z\) and for oxygen and fluorine order of energy of molecular orbitals is given below : \(\sigma 1s < \sigma^* 1s < \sigma 2s < \sigma^* 2s < \sigma 2p_z < (\pi 2p_x \simeq \pi 2p_y) < (\pi^* 2p_x \simeq \pi^* 2p_y) < \sigma^* 2p_z\). Different atomic orbitals of one atom combine with those atomic orbitals of the second atom which have comparable energies and proper orientation. Further, if the overlapping is head on, the molecular orbital is called 'Sigma' (\(\sigma\)) and if the overlap is lateral, the molecular orbital is called 'pi' (\(\pi\)). The molecular orbitals are filled with electrons according to the same rules as followed for filling of atomic orbitals. However, the order for filling is not the same for all molecules or their ions. Bond order is one of the most important parameters to compare the strength of bonds.

67. Which of the following pair is expected to have the same bond order?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
We need to compare the bond orders of the pairs: \(\mathrm{O}_2, \mathrm{N}_2\); \(\mathrm{O}_2^+, \mathrm{N}_2^-\); \(\mathrm{O}_2^-, \mathrm{N}_2^+\); and \(\mathrm{O}_2^-, \mathrm{N}_2^-\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Isoelectronic diatomic species have the same total number of electrons and therefore the same bond order.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Bond Order} = \frac{1}{2}(N_b - N_a)\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
For \(\mathrm{O}_2\) (16 electrons): \(\text{BO} = 2.0\); for \(\mathrm{N}_2\) (14 electrons): \(\text{BO} = 3.0\) (different).
For \(\mathrm{O}_2^+\) (\(16 - 1 = 15\) electrons): \(N_b = 10, N_a = 5 \implies \text{BO} = \frac{10 - 5}{2} = 2.5\).
For \(\mathrm{N}_2^-\) (\(14 + 1 = 15\) electrons): \(N_b = 10, N_a = 5 \implies \text{BO} = \frac{10 - 5}{2} = 2.5\).
For \(\mathrm{O}_2^-\) (17 electrons): \(\text{BO} = 1.5\); for \(\mathrm{N}_2^+\) (13 electrons): \(\text{BO} = 2.5\) (different).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Both \(\mathrm{O}_2^+\) and \(\mathrm{N}_2^-\) have 15 electrons and a bond order of \(2.5\), so they are expected to have the same bond order.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_COMPREHENSION_Q68 - Molecule where sigma 2pz is filled after pi 2px and pi 2py

questiontext.text:
Passage: Molecular orbitals are formed by the overlap of atomic orbitals. Two atomic orbitals combine to form two molecular orbitals called bonding molecular orbital (BMO) and anti bonding molecular orbital (ABMO). Energy of anti bonding orbital is raised above the parent atomic orbitals that have combined and the energy of the bonding orbital is lowered than the parent atomic orbitals. Energies of various molecular orbitals for elements hydrogen to nitrogen increase in the order : \(\sigma 1s < \sigma^* 1s < \sigma 2s < \sigma^* 2s < (\pi 2p_x \simeq \pi 2p_y) < \sigma 2p_z < (\pi^* 2p_x \simeq \pi^* 2p_y) < \sigma^* 2p_z\) and for oxygen and fluorine order of energy of molecular orbitals is given below : \(\sigma 1s < \sigma^* 1s < \sigma 2s < \sigma^* 2s < \sigma 2p_z < (\pi 2p_x \simeq \pi 2p_y) < (\pi^* 2p_x \simeq \pi^* 2p_y) < \sigma^* 2p_z\). Different atomic orbitals of one atom combine with those atomic orbitals of the second atom which have comparable energies and proper orientation. Further, if the overlapping is head on, the molecular orbital is called 'Sigma' (\(\sigma\)) and if the overlap is lateral, the molecular orbital is called 'pi' (\(\pi\)). The molecular orbitals are filled with electrons according to the same rules as followed for filling of atomic orbitals. However, the order for filling is not the same for all molecules or their ions. Bond order is one of the most important parameters to compare the strength of bonds.

68. In which of the following molecules, \(\sigma 2p_z\) molecular orbital is filled after \(\pi 2p_x\) and \(\pi 2p_y\) molecular orbitals?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
