दिए गए यौगिकों के क्वथनांक का क्रम \(\text{ईथर} < \text{ऐसीटोन} < \text{जल}\) है (जल में प्रबल हाइड्रोजन आबंधन, ऐसीटोन में द्विध्रुव-द्विध्रुव अन्योन्यक्रिया और ईथर में दुर्बल द्विध्रुव अन्योन्यक्रिया होती है)।

चरण 3: अनुप्रयोग
क्वथनांक के क्रम को उलटने पर \(30^\circ\text{C}\) पर वाष्प दाब का क्रम प्राप्त होता है:
\(\text{जल} < \text{ऐसीटोन} < \text{ईथर}\)।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
\(30^\circ\text{C}\) पर वाष्प दाब का सही क्रम जल < ऐसीटोन < ईथर है।

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_EQUILIBRIUM_MCQ_Q18 - Equilibrium constant for reversed and doubled HI reaction

questiontext.text:
At \(500\text{ K}\), equilibrium constant, \(K_c\), for the following reaction is \(5\).

\[\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{H_2(g)} + \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{I_2(g)} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{HI(g)}\]

What would be the equilibrium constant \(K_c\) for the reaction

\[\mathrm{2HI(g) \rightleftharpoons H_2(g) + I_2(g)}\]

\(500\text{ K}\) पर निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया के लिए साम्य स्थिरांक \(K_c\) का मान \(5\) है।

\[\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{H_2(g)} + \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{I_2(g)} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{HI(g)}\]

अभिक्रिया \(\mathrm{2HI(g) \rightleftharpoons H_2(g) + I_2(g)}\) के लिए साम्य स्थिरांक \(K_c\) क्या होगा?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
At \(T = 500\text{ K}\), for \(\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{H_2(g)} + \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{I_2(g)} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{HI(g)}\), the equilibrium constant is \(K_c = 5\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Temperature remains constant at \(500\text{ K}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
If a reaction is reversed, its equilibrium constant becomes \(\frac{1}{K_c}\). If the stoichiometric coefficients are multiplied by a factor \(n\), the equilibrium constant is raised to the power \(n\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Reversing the given reaction gives:
\[\mathrm{HI(g)} \rightleftharpoons \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{H_2(g)} + \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{I_2(g)}, \quad K_c' = \frac{1}{K_c} = \frac{1}{5}\]
Multiplying the reversed equation by \(2\) gives the target reaction \(\mathrm{2HI(g) \rightleftharpoons H_2(g) + I_2(g)}\):
\[K_c'' = (K_c')^2 = \left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{25} = 0.04\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Since \(K_c > 1\) for formation of \(\mathrm{HI}\), its dissociation constant must be less than \(1\), and \(0.04 < 1\). Thus, \(K_c = 0.04\).

चरण 1: दिए गए आँकड़े और शर्तें
\(T = 500\text{ K}\) पर, \(\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{H_2(g)} + \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{I_2(g)} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{HI(g)}\) के लिए साम्य स्थिरांक \(K_c = 5\) है।

चरण 2: मान्यताएँ और चिह्न परिपाटी
ताप \(500\text{ K}\) पर स्थिर रहता है।

चरण 3: संबंधित सूत्र और सिद्धांत
यदि किसी अभिक्रिया को उलट दिया जाए, तो उसका साम्य स्थिरांक \(\frac{1}{K_c}\) हो जाता है। यदि रससमीकरणमितीय गुणांकों को किसी संख्या \(n\) से गुणा किया जाए, तो साम्य स्थिरांक की घात \(n\) हो जाती है।

चरण 4: चरण-दर-चरण गणना
दी गई अभिक्रिया को उलटने पर:
\[\mathrm{HI(g)} \rightleftharpoons \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{H_2(g)} + \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{I_2(g)}, \quad K_c' = \frac{1}{K_c} = \frac{1}{5}\]
उलटी गई समीकरण को \(2\) से गुणा करने पर अभीष्ट अभिक्रिया \(\mathrm{2HI(g) \rightleftharpoons H_2(g) + I_2(g)}\) प्राप्त होती है:
\[K_c'' = (K_c')^2 = \left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{25} = 0.04\]

चरण 5: जाँच और अंतिम उत्तर
चूँकि \(\mathrm{HI}\) के निर्माण के लिए \(K_c > 1\) है, इसलिए इसके वियोजन के लिए स्थिरांक \(1\) से कम होना चाहिए, और \(0.04 < 1\) है। अतः \(K_c = 0.04\) है।

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_EQUILIBRIUM_MCQ_Q19 - Effect of adding argon at constant volume

questiontext.text:
In which of the following reactions, the equilibrium remains unaffected on addition of small amount of argon at constant volume?

स्थिर आयतन पर थोड़ी मात्रा में आर्गन मिलाने पर निम्नलिखित में से किस अभिक्रिया में साम्यावस्था अप्रभावित रहती है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
According to Le Chatelier's principle, when an inert gas (such as argon) is added to a gaseous equilibrium mixture at constant volume and constant temperature, the total pressure increases, but the molar concentrations and partial pressures of all reacting gases remain unchanged.

Step 2: Evaluation
Since the reaction quotient \(Q_c\) (and \(Q_p\)) depends only on the concentrations (or partial pressures) of the reactants and products, neither \(Q\) nor \(K\) changes when argon is added at constant volume, regardless of whether \(\Delta n_g = 0\) or \(\Delta n_g \neq 0\).

Step 3: Application
For \(\mathrm{H_2(g) + I_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2HI(g)}\), \(\mathrm{PCl_5(g) \rightleftharpoons PCl_3(g) + Cl_2(g)}\), and \(\mathrm{N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3(g)}\), adding argon at constant volume does not disturb the equilibrium in any of them.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The equilibrium will remain unaffected in all three reactions.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
ला शातेलिए के सिद्धांत के अनुसार, स्थिर आयतन और स्थिर ताप पर किसी गैसीय साम्य मिश्रण में अक्रिय गैस (जैसे आर्गन) मिलाने पर कुल दाब तो बढ़ता है, परंतु सभी अभिक्रियाशील गैसों की मोलर सांद्रताएँ और आंशिक दाब अपरिवर्तित रहते हैं।

चरण 2: मूल्यांकन
चूँकि अभिक्रिया भागफल \(Q_c\) (और \(Q_p\)) केवल अभिकारकों और उत्पादों की सांद्रताओं (या आंशिक दाबों) पर निर्भर करता है, इसलिए स्थिर आयतन पर आर्गन मिलाने से न तो \(Q\) बदलता है और न ही \(K\), चाहे \(\Delta n_g = 0\) हो या \(\Delta n_g \neq 0\)।

चरण 3: अनुप्रयोग
\(\mathrm{H_2(g) + I_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2HI(g)}\), \(\mathrm{PCl_5(g) \rightleftharpoons PCl_3(g) + Cl_2(g)}\), और \(\mathrm{N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3(g)}\) — इनमें से किसी भी अभिक्रिया में स्थिर आयतन पर आर्गन मिलाने से साम्य प्रभावित नहीं होता।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
तीनों ही स्थितियों में साम्यावस्था अप्रभावित रहेगी।

answer.text: The equilibrium will remain unaffected in all the three cases.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_MCQII_EQUILIBRIUM_MCQ_Q20 - N2O4 dissociation equilibrium properties

questiontext.text:
For the reaction \(\mathrm{N_2O_4(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NO_2(g)}\), the value of \(K\) is \(50\) at \(400\text{ K}\) and \(1700\) at \(500\text{ K}\). Which of the following options is correct?

अभिक्रिया \(\mathrm{N_2O_4(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NO_2(g)}\) के लिए \(K\) का मान \(400\text{ K}\) पर \(50\) तथा \(500\text{ K}\) पर \(1700\) है। निम्नलिखित में से कौन-से विकल्प सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Reaction: \(\mathrm{N_2O_4(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NO_2(g)}\).
At \(T_1 = 400\text{ K}\), \(K = 50\); at \(T_2 = 500\text{ K}\), \(K = 1700\).
Partial pressures mixed at \(400\text{ K}\): \(p_{\mathrm{NO_2}} = 20\text{ bar}\) and \(p_{\mathrm{N_2O_4}} = 2\text{ bar}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
\(K\) given for the gas-phase equilibrium corresponds to \(K_p\) in bar units.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
1. Van't Hoff principle: an increase in \(K\) with increasing temperature indicates an endothermic reaction (\(\Delta H > 0\)).
2. Reaction quotient: \(Q_p = \frac{p_{\mathrm{NO_2}}^2}{p_{\mathrm{N_2O_4}}}\). If \(Q_p > K_p\), the reaction proceeds backward.
3. Entropy change: \(\Delta n_g = 2 - 1 = +1 > 0\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
- Since \(K\) increases from \(50\) to \(1700\) as \(T\) increases from \(400\text{ K}\) to \(500\text{ K}\), the reaction is endothermic (and not exothermic).
- Calculating \(Q_p\) at \(400\text{ K}\):
\[Q_p = \frac{(20)^2}{2} = \frac{400}{2} = 200\]
Since \(Q_p = 200 > K = 50\), the reaction proceeds in the reverse direction, so more \(\mathrm{N_2O_4(g)}\) will be formed.
- Because \(1\text{ mol}\) of gaseous reactant forms \(2\text{ mol}\) of gaseous product (\(\Delta n_g = +1\)), disorder increases and the entropy of the system increases.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
All three conclusions hold: the reaction is endothermic, more \(\mathrm{N_2O_4(g)}\) will be formed under the given partial pressures at \(400\text{ K}\), and the entropy of the system increases.

चरण 1: दिए गए आँकड़े और शर्तें
अभिक्रिया: \(\mathrm{N_2O_4(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NO_2(g)}\)।
\(T_1 = 400\text{ K}\) पर \(K = 50\); \(T_2 = 500\text{ K}\) पर \(K = 1700\)।
\(400\text{ K}\) पर मिश्रित आंशिक दाब: \(p_{\mathrm{NO_2}} = 20\text{ bar}\) तथा \(p_{\mathrm{N_2O_4}} = 2\text{ bar}\)।

चरण 2: मान्यताएँ और चिह्न परिपाटी
गैसीय प्रावस्था साम्य के लिए दिया गया \(K\) बार (bar) मात्रक में \(K_p\) के संगत है।

चरण 3: संबंधित सूत्र और सिद्धांत
1. वान्ट हॉफ सिद्धांत: ताप बढ़ने पर \(K\) का बढ़ना ऊष्माशोषी अभिक्रिया (\(\Delta H > 0\)) को दर्शाता है।
2. अभिक्रिया भागफल: \(Q_p = \frac{p_{\mathrm{NO_2}}^2}{p_{\mathrm{N_2O_4}}}\)। यदि \(Q_p > K_p\) हो, तो अभिक्रिया प्रतीप दिशा में जाती है।
3. एन्ट्रॉपी परिवर्तन: \(\Delta n_g = 2 - 1 = +1 > 0\)।

चरण 4: चरण-दर-चरण गणना
- चूँकि \(T\) के \(400\text{ K}\) से \(500\text{ K}\) बढ़ने पर \(K\) का मान \(50\) से बढ़कर \(1700\) हो जाता है, अतः अभिक्रिया ऊष्माशोषी है (ऊष्माक्षेपी नहीं)।
- \(400\text{ K}\) पर \(Q_p\) की गणना:
\[Q_p = \frac{(20)^2}{2} = \frac{400}{2} = 200\]
चूँकि \(Q_p = 200 > K = 50\) है, इसलिए अभिक्रिया प्रतीप दिशा में अग्रसर होगी और अधिक \(\mathrm{N_2O_4(g)}\) बनेगी।
- चूँकि \(1\text{ mol}\) गैसीय अभिकारक से \(2\text{ mol}\) गैसीय उत्पाद बनता है (\(\Delta n_g = +1\)), अतः अव्यवस्था बढ़ती है और निकाय की एन्ट्रॉपी बढ़ती है।

चरण 5: जाँच और अंतिम उत्तर
तीनों निष्कर्ष सत्य हैं: अभिक्रिया ऊष्माशोषी है, \(400\text{ K}\) पर दिए गए आंशिक दाबों पर अधिक \(\mathrm{N_2O_4(g)}\) बनेगी, तथा निकाय की एन्ट्रॉपी बढ़ती है।

answer.text: If \(\mathrm{NO_2(g)}\) and \(\mathrm{N_2O_4(g)}\) are mixed at \(400\text{ K}\) at partial pressures \(20\text{ bar}\) and \(2\text{ bar}\) respectively, more \(\mathrm{N_2O_4(g)}\) will be formed.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_MCQII_EQUILIBRIUM_MCQ_Q21 - Temperature of solid-liquid equilibrium at atmospheric pressure

questiontext.text:
At a particular temperature and atmospheric pressure, the solid and liquid phases of a pure substance can exist in equilibrium. Which of the following term defines this temperature?

एक विशेष ताप और वायुमंडलीय दाब पर, किसी शुद्ध पदार्थ की ठोस और द्रव प्रावस्थाएँ साम्यावस्था में रह सकती हैं। निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा पद इस ताप को परिभाषित करता है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
For any pure substance at atmospheric pressure (\(1\text{ atm}\)), the solid and liquid phases coexist in dynamic equilibrium at a characteristic fixed temperature.

Step 2: Evaluation
- Normal melting point: The temperature at which the solid phase melts into the liquid phase at atmospheric pressure.
- Freezing point: The temperature at which the liquid phase freezes into the solid phase at atmospheric pressure; for a pure substance, this is identical to the normal melting point.
- Boiling point refers to liquid-vapour equilibrium, and "equilibrium temperature" is a general term not specific to the solid-liquid phase transition.

Step 3: Application
Both normal melting point and freezing point correctly define the temperature at which solid and liquid phases of a pure substance exist in equilibrium at atmospheric pressure.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The terms that define this temperature are normal melting point and freezing point.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
वायुमंडलीय दाब (\(1\text{ atm}\)) पर किसी शुद्ध पदार्थ की ठोस और द्रव प्रावस्थाएँ एक विशिष्ट निश्चित ताप पर गतिक साम्यावस्था में सह-अस्तित्व में रहती हैं।

चरण 2: मूल्यांकन
- सामान्य गलनांक: वह ताप जिस पर वायुमंडलीय दाब पर ठोस प्रावस्था द्रव प्रावस्था में पिघलती है।
- हिमांक: वह ताप जिस पर वायुमंडलीय दाब पर द्रव प्रावस्था ठोस प्रावस्था में जमती है; शुद्ध पदार्थ के लिए यह सामान्य गलनांक के समान होता है।
- क्वथनांक द्रव-वाष्प साम्य से संबंधित है, तथा "साम्य ताप" एक सामान्य शब्द है जो केवल ठोस-द्रव संक्रमण के लिए विशिष्ट नहीं है।

चरण 3: अनुप्रयोग
सामान्य गलनांक और हिमांक दोनों ही उस ताप को सही ढंग से परिभाषित करते हैं जिस पर वायुमंडलीय दाब पर किसी शुद्ध पदार्थ की ठोस और द्रव प्रावस्थाएँ साम्यावस्था में होती हैं।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
इस ताप को परिभाषित करने वाले पद सामान्य गलनांक और हिमांक हैं।

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_MATCH_EQUILIBRIUM_MCQ_Q38 - Matching physical and solution equilibria with conditions

questiontext.text:
Match the following equilibria with the corresponding condition:

Column IColumn II
(i) Liquid \(\rightleftharpoons\) Vapour(a) Saturated solution
(ii) Solid \(\rightleftharpoons\) Liquid(b) Boiling point
(iii) Solid \(\rightleftharpoons\) Vapour(c) Sublimation point
(iv) Solute (s) \(\rightleftharpoons\) Solute (solution)(d) Melting point
(e) Unsaturated solution

निम्नलिखित साम्यावस्थाओं को संगत अवस्थाओं से सुमेलित कीजिए:

स्तंभ Iस्तंभ II
(i) द्रव \(\rightleftharpoons\) वाष्प(a) संतृप्त विलयन
(ii) ठोस \(\rightleftharpoons\) द्रव(b) क्वथनांक
(iii) ठोस \(\rightleftharpoons\) वाष्प(c) ऊर्ध्वपातन बिंदु
(iv) विलेय (s) \(\rightleftharpoons\) विलेय (विलयन)(d) गलनांक
(e) असंतृप्त विलयन

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Phase and dissolution equilibria occur at characteristic transition points or saturation conditions at a given pressure and temperature.

Step 2: Evaluation
- Liquid \(\rightleftharpoons\) Vapour equilibrium at atmospheric pressure defines the boiling point.
- Solid \(\rightleftharpoons\) Liquid equilibrium at atmospheric pressure defines the melting point.
- Solid \(\rightleftharpoons\) Vapour equilibrium defines the sublimation point.
- Solute (s) \(\rightleftharpoons\) Solute (solution) equilibrium occurs when no more solute can dissolve at that temperature, which defines a saturated solution.

Step 3: Application
Pairing each equilibrium with its condition gives: (i)-(b), (ii)-(d), (iii)-(c), (iv)-(a).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct match is (i)-(b), (ii)-(d), (iii)-(c), (iv)-(a).

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
प्रावस्था और विलयन साम्य किसी निश्चित दाब और ताप पर विशिष्ट संक्रमण बिंदुओं या संतृप्ति अवस्थाओं पर स्थापित होते हैं।

चरण 2: मूल्यांकन
- वायुमंडलीय दाब पर द्रव \(\rightleftharpoons\) वाष्प साम्य क्वथनांक को परिभाषित करता है।
- वायुमंडलीय दाब पर ठोस \(\rightleftharpoons\) द्रव साम्य गलनांक को परिभाषित करता है।
- ठोस \(\rightleftharpoons\) वाष्प साम्य ऊर्ध्वपातन बिंदु को परिभाषित करता है।
- विलेय (s) \(\rightleftharpoons\) विलेय (विलयन) साम्य तब स्थापित होता है जब उस ताप पर और अधिक विलेय न घुल सके, जो संतृप्त विलयन को परिभाषित करता है।

चरण 3: अनुप्रयोग
प्रत्येक साम्य को उसकी अवस्था से मिलाने पर (i)-(b), (ii)-(d), (iii)-(c), (iv)-(a) प्राप्त होता है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
सही सुमेलन (i)-(b), (ii)-(d), (iii)-(c), (iv)-(a) है।

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_MATCH_EQUILIBRIUM_MCQ_Q39 - Matching modified ammonia synthesis reactions with Kc

questiontext.text:
For the reaction: \(\mathrm{N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3(g)}\)

Equilibrium constant \(K_c = \frac{[\mathrm{NH_3}]^2}{[\mathrm{N_2}][\mathrm{H_2}]^3}\)

Some reactions are written below in Column I and their equilibrium constants in terms of \(K_c\) are written in Column II. Match the following reactions with the corresponding equilibrium constant:

Column I (Reaction)Column II (Equilibrium constant)
(i) \(\mathrm{2N_2(g) + 6H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 4NH_3(g)}\)(a) \(2K_c\)
(ii) \(\mathrm{2NH_3(g) \rightleftharpoons N_2(g) + 3H_2(g)}\)(b) \(K_c^{\frac{1}{2}}\)
(iii) \(\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{N_2(g)} + \frac{3}{2}\mathrm{H_2(g)} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{NH_3(g)}\)(c) \(\frac{1}{K_c}\)
(d) \(K_c^2\)

अभिक्रिया \(\mathrm{N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3(g)}\) के लिए साम्य स्थिरांक \(K_c = \frac{[\mathrm{NH_3}]^2}{[\mathrm{N_2}][\mathrm{H_2}]^3}\) है।

स्तंभ I में कुछ अभिक्रियाएँ दी गई हैं तथा स्तंभ II में \(K_c\) के पदों में उनके साम्य स्थिरांक दिए गए हैं। निम्नलिखित अभिक्रियाओं को संगत साम्य स्थिरांक से सुमेलित कीजिए:

स्तंभ I (अभिक्रिया)स्तंभ II (साम्य स्थिरांक)
(i) \(\mathrm{2N_2(g) + 6H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 4NH_3(g)}\)(a) \(2K_c\)
(ii) \(\mathrm{2NH_3(g) \rightleftharpoons N_2(g) + 3H_2(g)}\)(b) \(K_c^{\frac{1}{2}}\)
(iii) \(\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{N_2(g)} + \frac{3}{2}\mathrm{H_2(g)} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{NH_3(g)}\)(c) \(\frac{1}{K_c}\)
(d) \(K_c^2\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Base reaction: \(\mathrm{N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3(g)}\) with equilibrium constant \(K_c\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
All reactions are considered at the same temperature.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Multiplying a chemical equation by \(n\) raises \(K_c\) to the power \(n\) (\(K_c^n\)), and reversing an equation inverts \(K_c\) to \(\frac{1}{K_c}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
- Reaction (i) is obtained by multiplying the base equation by \(2\), so its equilibrium constant is \(K_c^2\) (matches d).
- Reaction (ii) is the reverse of the base equation, so its equilibrium constant is \(\frac{1}{K_c}\) (matches c).
- Reaction (iii) is obtained by multiplying the base equation by \(\frac{1}{2}\), so its equilibrium constant is \(K_c^{\frac{1}{2}}\) (matches b).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The correct match is (i)-(d), (ii)-(c), (iii)-(b).

चरण 1: दिए गए आँकड़े और शर्तें
मूल अभिक्रिया: \(\mathrm{N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3(g)}\), जिसका साम्य स्थिरांक \(K_c\) है।

चरण 2: मान्यताएँ और चिह्न परिपाटी
सभी अभिक्रियाएँ समान ताप पर मानी गई हैं।

चरण 3: संबंधित सूत्र और सिद्धांत
किसी रासायनिक समीकरण को \(n\) से गुणा करने पर साम्य स्थिरांक की घात \(n\) हो जाती है (\(K_c^n\)), और समीकरण को उलटने पर साम्य स्थिरांक \(\frac{1}{K_c}\) हो जाता है।

चरण 4: चरण-दर-चरण गणना
- अभिक्रिया (i) मूल समीकरण को \(2\) से गुणा करने पर प्राप्त होती है, अतः इसका साम्य स्थिरांक \(K_c^2\) है (d से सुमेलित)।
- अभिक्रिया (ii) मूल समीकरण का व्युत्क्रम है, अतः इसका साम्य स्थिरांक \(\frac{1}{K_c}\) है (c से सुमेलित)।
- अभिक्रिया (iii) मूल समीकरण को \(\frac{1}{2}\) से गुणा करने पर प्राप्त होती है, अतः इसका साम्य स्थिरांक \(K_c^{\frac{1}{2}}\) है (b से सुमेलित)।

चरण 5: जाँच और अंतिम उत्तर
सही सुमेलन (i)-(d), (ii)-(c), (iii)-(b) है।

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_MATCH_EQUILIBRIUM_MCQ_Q40 - Matching standard free energy with equilibrium constant

questiontext.text:
Match standard free energy of the reaction with the corresponding equilibrium constant:

Column IColumn II
(i) \(\Delta G^\circ > 0\)(a) \(K > 1\)
(ii) \(\Delta G^\circ < 0\)(b) \(K = 1\)
(iii) \(\Delta G^\circ = 0\)(c) \(K = 0\)
(d) \(K < 1\)

अभिक्रिया की मानक मुक्त ऊर्जा को संगत साम्य स्थिरांक से सुमेलित कीजिए:

स्तंभ Iस्तंभ II
(i) \(\Delta G^\circ > 0\)(a) \(K > 1\)
(ii) \(\Delta G^\circ < 0\)(b) \(K = 1\)
(iii) \(\Delta G^\circ = 0\)(c) \(K = 0\)
(d) \(K < 1\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Three sign/value cases for \(\Delta G^\circ\) are given: \(\Delta G^\circ > 0\), \(\Delta G^\circ < 0\), and \(\Delta G^\circ = 0\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
\(R > 0\) and absolute temperature \(T > 0\), so \(RT > 0\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\(\Delta G^\circ = -RT \ln K\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
- When \(\Delta G^\circ > 0\), \(-RT \ln K > 0 \implies \ln K < 0 \implies K < 1\) (matches d).
- When \(\Delta G^\circ < 0\), \(-RT \ln K < 0 \implies \ln K > 0 \implies K > 1\) (matches a).
- When \(\Delta G^\circ = 0\), \(-RT \ln K = 0 \implies \ln K = 0 \implies K = 1\) (matches b).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The correct matching is (i)-(d), (ii)-(a), (iii)-(b).

चरण 1: दिए गए आँकड़े और शर्तें
\(\Delta G^\circ\) के तीन मान/चिह्न दिए गए हैं: \(\Delta G^\circ > 0\), \(\Delta G^\circ < 0\), और \(\Delta G^\circ = 0\)।

चरण 2: मान्यताएँ और चिह्न परिपाटी
\(R > 0\) और परम ताप \(T > 0\) होता है, अतः \(RT > 0\)।

चरण 3: संबंधित सूत्र और सिद्धांत
\(\Delta G^\circ = -RT \ln K\)।

चरण 4: चरण-दर-चरण गणना
- जब \(\Delta G^\circ > 0\), तब \(-RT \ln K > 0 \implies \ln K < 0 \implies K < 1\) (d से सुमेलित)।
- जब \(\Delta G^\circ < 0\), तब \(-RT \ln K < 0 \implies \ln K > 0 \implies K > 1\) (a से सुमेलित)।
- जब \(\Delta G^\circ = 0\), तब \(-RT \ln K = 0 \implies \ln K = 0 \implies K = 1\) (b से सुमेलित)।

चरण 5: जाँच और अंतिम उत्तर
सही सुमेलन (i)-(d), (ii)-(a), (iii)-(b) है।

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_MATCH_EQUILIBRIUM_MCQ_Q41 - Matching species with conjugate acids

questiontext.text:
Match the following species with the corresponding conjugate acid:

SpeciesConjugate acid
(i) \(\mathrm{NH_3}\)(a) \(\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}}\)
(ii) \(\mathrm{HCO_3^-}\)(b) \(\mathrm{NH_4^+}\)
(iii) \(\mathrm{H_2O}\)(c) \(\mathrm{H_3O^+}\)
(iv) \(\mathrm{HSO_4^-}\)(d) \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\)
(e) \(\mathrm{H_2CO_3}\)

निम्नलिखित स्पीशीज़ को उनके संगत संयुग्मी अम्ल से सुमेलित कीजिए:

स्पीशीज़संयुग्मी अम्ल
(i) \(\mathrm{NH_3}\)(a) \(\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}}\)
(ii) \(\mathrm{HCO_3^-}\)(b) \(\mathrm{NH_4^+}\)
(iii) \(\mathrm{H_2O}\)(c) \(\mathrm{H_3O^+}\)
(iv) \(\mathrm{HSO_4^-}\)(d) \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\)
(e) \(\mathrm{H_2CO_3}\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
According to the Bronsted-Lowry concept, the conjugate acid of a species is formed by adding one proton (\(\mathrm{H^+}\)) to that species.

Step 2: Evaluation
- \(\mathrm{NH_3 + H^+ \rightarrow NH_4^+}\) (matches b)
- \(\mathrm{HCO_3^- + H^+ \rightarrow H_2CO_3}\) (matches e; note \(\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}}\) is the conjugate base, not the conjugate acid)
- \(\mathrm{H_2O + H^+ \rightarrow H_3O^+}\) (matches c)
- \(\mathrm{HSO_4^- + H^+ \rightarrow H_2SO_4}\) (matches d)

Step 3: Application
Thus, the correct pairings are (i)-(b), (ii)-(e), (iii)-(c), (iv)-(d).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct match is (i)-(b), (ii)-(e), (iii)-(c), (iv)-(d).

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
ब्रॉन्स्टेड-लौरी संकल्पना के अनुसार, किसी स्पीशीज़ में एक प्रोटॉन (\(\mathrm{H^+}\)) जोड़ने पर उसका संयुग्मी अम्ल प्राप्त होता है।

चरण 2: मूल्यांकन
- \(\mathrm{NH_3 + H^+ \rightarrow NH_4^+}\) (b से सुमेलित)
- \(\mathrm{HCO_3^- + H^+ \rightarrow H_2CO_3}\) (e से सुमेलित; ध्यान दें कि \(\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}}\) संयुग्मी क्षारक है, संयुग्मी अम्ल नहीं)
- \(\mathrm{H_2O + H^+ \rightarrow H_3O^+}\) (c से सुमेलित)
- \(\mathrm{HSO_4^- + H^+ \rightarrow H_2SO_4}\) (d से सुमेलित)

चरण 3: अनुप्रयोग
अतः सही युग्मन (i)-(b), (ii)-(e), (iii)-(c), (iv)-(d) है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
सही सुमेलन (i)-(b), (ii)-(e), (iii)-(c), (iv)-(d) है।

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_MATCH_EQUILIBRIUM_MCQ_Q43 - Matching reaction spontaneity with Gibbs energy and K

questiontext.text:
Match Column (I) with Column (II):

Column IColumn II
(i) Equilibrium(a) \(\Delta G > 0, K < 1\)
(ii) Spontaneous reaction(b) \(\Delta G = 0\)
(iii) Non spontaneous reaction(c) \(\Delta G^\circ = 0\)
(d) \(\Delta G < 0, K > 1\)

स्तंभ (I) को स्तंभ (II) से सुमेलित कीजिए:

स्तंभ Iस्तंभ II
(i) साम्यावस्था(a) \(\Delta G > 0, K < 1\)
(ii) स्वतः प्रवर्तित अभिक्रिया(b) \(\Delta G = 0\)
(iii) अ-स्वत: प्रवर्तित अभिक्रिया(c) \(\Delta G^\circ = 0\)
(d) \(\Delta G < 0, K > 1\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
At constant temperature and pressure, the Gibbs free energy change \(\Delta G\) governs the spontaneity and equilibrium of a process, while \(\Delta G^\circ = -RT \ln K\) relates standard free energy to the equilibrium constant \(K\).

Step 2: Evaluation
- At equilibrium, \(\Delta G = 0\) (matches b). Note that \(\Delta G^\circ = 0\) only holds for the special case \(K = 1\), not for equilibrium in general.
- For a spontaneous reaction, \(\Delta G < 0\), and product-favoured spontaneity corresponds to \(K > 1\) (matches d).
- For a non-spontaneous reaction, \(\Delta G > 0\), and reactant-favoured behaviour corresponds to \(K < 1\) (matches a).

Step 3: Application
Matching Column I with Column II gives: (i)-(b), (ii)-(d), (iii)-(a).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct match is (i)-(b), (ii)-(d), (iii)-(a).

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
स्थिर ताप और दाब पर, गिब्स मुक्त ऊर्जा परिवर्तन \(\Delta G\) किसी प्रक्रम की स्वतःप्रवर्तिता और साम्य को निर्धारित करता है, जबकि \(\Delta G^\circ = -RT \ln K\) मानक मुक्त ऊर्जा को साम्य स्थिरांक \(K\) से जोड़ता है।

चरण 2: मूल्यांकन
- साम्यावस्था पर \(\Delta G = 0\) होता है (b से सुमेलित)। ध्यान दें कि \(\Delta G^\circ = 0\) केवल \(K = 1\) की विशेष स्थिति के लिए होता है, सामान्य साम्यावस्था के लिए नहीं।
- स्वतः प्रवर्तित अभिक्रिया के लिए \(\Delta G < 0\) तथा \(K > 1\) होता है (d से सुमेलित)।
- अ-स्वतः प्रवर्तित अभिक्रिया के लिए \(\Delta G > 0\) तथा \(K < 1\) होता है (a से सुमेलित)।

चरण 3: अनुप्रयोग
स्तंभ I को स्तंभ II से मिलाने पर (i)-(b), (ii)-(d), (iii)-(a) प्राप्त होता है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
सही सुमेलन (i)-(b), (ii)-(d), (iii)-(a) है।

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_AR_EQUILIBRIUM_MCQ_Q44 - Acidity order of hydrogen halides

questiontext.text:
In the following question a statement of Assertion (A) followed by a statement of Reason (R) is given. Choose the correct option out of the choices given below.

Assertion (A) : Increasing order of acidity of hydrogen halides is \(\mathrm{HF < HCl < HBr < HI}\)

Reason (R) : While comparing acids formed by the elements belonging to the same group of periodic table, H-A bond strength is a more important factor in determining acidity of an acid than the polar nature of the bond.

निम्नलिखित प्रश्न में अभिकथन (A) के पश्चात कारण (R) का कथन दिया गया है। नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही विकल्प चुनिए।

अभिकथन (A) : हाइड्रोजन हैलाइडों की अम्लीयता का बढ़ता क्रम \(\mathrm{HF < HCl < HBr < HI}\) है।

कारण (R) : आवर्त सारणी के एक ही समूह के तत्वों द्वारा बनाए गए अम्लों की तुलना करते समय, किसी अम्ल की अम्लीयता निर्धारित करने में बंध की ध्रुवीय प्रकृति की अपेक्षा H-A आबंध प्रबलता एक अधिक महत्वपूर्ण कारक है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
For binary acids \(\mathrm{H-A}\) formed by elements in the same group (group 17: \(\mathrm{F, Cl, Br, I}\)), atomic size increases rapidly down the group, causing the \(\mathrm{H-A}\) bond length to increase and the \(\mathrm{H-A}\) bond dissociation enthalpy to decrease sharply.

Step 2: Evaluation
Although electronegativity decreases from \(\mathrm{F}\) to \(\mathrm{I}\) (making \(\mathrm{H-F}\) the most polar bond), the decrease in \(\mathrm{H-A}\) bond strength from \(\mathrm{HF}\) to \(\mathrm{HI}\) dominates, making proton release easiest for \(\mathrm{HI}\) and hardest for \(\mathrm{HF}\).

Step 3: Application
Thus, the acidity order \(\mathrm{HF < HCl < HBr < HI}\) is true, and the dominance of \(\mathrm{H-A}\) bond strength over bond polarity down a group is also true and directly explains the acidity trend.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
एक ही समूह (समूह 17: \(\mathrm{F, Cl, Br, I}\)) के तत्वों द्वारा निर्मित द्विअंगी अम्लों \(\mathrm{H-A}\) के लिए, समूह में नीचे जाने पर परमाणु आकार तेजी से बढ़ता है, जिससे \(\mathrm{H-A}\) आबंध लंबाई बढ़ती है और \(\mathrm{H-A}\) आबंध वियोजन एन्थैल्पी तेजी से घटती है।

चरण 2: मूल्यांकन
यद्यपि \(\mathrm{F}\) से \(\mathrm{I}\) तक विद्युतऋणात्मकता घटती है (जिससे \(\mathrm{H-F}\) सर्वाधिक ध्रुवीय आबंध है), तथापि \(\mathrm{HF}\) से \(\mathrm{HI}\) तक \(\mathrm{H-A}\) आबंध प्रबलता में कमी अधिक प्रभावी होती है, जिससे \(\mathrm{HI}\) से प्रोटॉन का त्याग सबसे सरल और \(\mathrm{HF}\) से सबसे कठिन होता है।

चरण 3: अनुप्रयोग
अतः अम्लीयता का क्रम \(\mathrm{HF < HCl < HBr < HI}\) सत्य है, तथा समूह में नीचे जाने पर आबंध ध्रुवीयता की तुलना में \(\mathrm{H-A}\) आबंध प्रबलता का अधिक महत्वपूर्ण होना भी सत्य है और यह अम्लीयता क्रम की सही व्याख्या करता है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
A और R दोनों सत्य हैं तथा R, A की सही व्याख्या है।

answer.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_AR_EQUILIBRIUM_MCQ_Q45 - Buffer action of acetic acid and sodium acetate

questiontext.text:
In the following question a statement of Assertion (A) followed by a statement of Reason (R) is given. Choose the correct option out of the choices given below.

Assertion (A) : A solution containing a mixture of acetic acid and sodium acetate maintains a constant value of pH on addition of small amounts of acid or alkali.

Reason (R) : A solution containing a mixture of acetic acid and sodium acetate acts as a buffer solution around pH \(4.75\).

निम्नलिखित प्रश्न में अभिकथन (A) के पश्चात कारण (R) का कथन दिया गया है। नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही विकल्प चुनिए।

अभिकथन (A) : ऐसीटिक अम्ल और सोडियम ऐसीटेट के मिश्रण वाला विलयन, अम्ल या क्षार की थोड़ी मात्रा मिलाने पर pH का मान स्थिर बनाए रखता है।

कारण (R) : ऐसीटिक अम्ल और सोडियम ऐसीटेट के मिश्रण वाला विलयन लगभग pH \(4.75\) के आसपास एक बफर विलयन की तरह कार्य करता है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
An acidic buffer solution consists of a weak acid and its salt with a strong base; it resists changes in pH upon addition of small quantities of strong acid or strong base.

Step 2: Evaluation
A mixture of acetic acid (\(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\), \(\text{p}K_a \approx 4.75\)) and sodium acetate (\(\mathrm{CH_3COONa}\)) forms a classic acidic buffer with \(\text{pH} = \text{p}K_a + \log\frac{[\mathrm{CH_3COO^-}]}{[\mathrm{CH_3COOH}]} \approx 4.75\) when concentrations are equal. Added \(\mathrm{H^+}\) is consumed by \(\mathrm{CH_3COO^-}\), and added \(\mathrm{OH^-}\) is neutralised by \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\).

Step 3: Application
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and the fact that the mixture acts as a buffer solution around pH \(4.75\) explains why it maintains a constant pH on adding small amounts of acid or alkali.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
एक अम्लीय बफर विलयन में एक दुर्बल अम्ल और प्रबल क्षारक के साथ उसका लवण होता है; यह प्रबल अम्ल या प्रबल क्षारक की थोड़ी मात्रा मिलाने पर pH में होने वाले परिवर्तन का विरोध करता है।

चरण 2: मूल्यांकन
ऐसीटिक अम्ल (\(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\), \(\text{p}K_a \approx 4.75\)) और सोडियम ऐसीटेट (\(\mathrm{CH_3COONa}\)) का मिश्रण एक प्रमुख अम्लीय बफर बनाता है, जिसकी समान सांद्रता पर \(\text{pH} \approx 4.75\) होती है। बाहर से मिलाए गए \(\mathrm{H^+}\) को \(\mathrm{CH_3COO^-}\) द्वारा तथा \(\mathrm{OH^-}\) को \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\) द्वारा उदासीन कर दिया जाता है।

चरण 3: अनुप्रयोग
अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं, और इस मिश्रण का लगभग pH \(4.75\) पर बफर विलयन की तरह कार्य करना ही यह स्पष्ट करता है कि यह अम्ल या क्षार की थोड़ी मात्रा मिलाने पर pH को स्थिर क्यों बनाए रखता है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
A और R दोनों सत्य हैं तथा R, A की सही व्याख्या है।

answer.text: Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_AR_EQUILIBRIUM_MCQ_Q46 - Ionisation of H2S in presence of HCl

questiontext.text:
In the following question a statement of Assertion (A) followed by a statement of Reason (R) is given. Choose the correct option out of the choices given below.

Assertion (A) : The ionisation of hydrogen sulphide in water is low in the presence of hydrochloric acid.

Reason (R) : Hydrogen sulphide is a weak acid.

निम्नलिखित प्रश्न में अभिकथन (A) के पश्चात कारण (R) का कथन दिया गया है। नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही विकल्प चुनिए।

अभिकथन (A) : हाइड्रोक्लोरिक अम्ल की उपस्थिति में जल में हाइड्रोजन सल्फाइड का आयनन कम होता है।

कारण (R) : हाइड्रोजन सल्फाइड एक दुर्बल अम्ल है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Hydrochloric acid (\(\mathrm{HCl}\)) is a strong electrolyte that dissociates completely to produce \(\mathrm{H^+}\) ions, whereas hydrogen sulphide (\(\mathrm{H_2S}\)) is a weak diprotic acid: \(\mathrm{H_2S \rightleftharpoons 2H^+ + S^{2-}}\).

Step 2: Evaluation
In the presence of \(\mathrm{HCl}\), the high concentration of common \(\mathrm{H^+}\) ions shifts the \(\mathrm{H_2S}\) ionisation equilibrium in the backward direction (common ion effect), lowering its degree of ionisation. Thus, Assertion (A) is true. Reason (R) is also true because \(\mathrm{H_2S}\) is indeed a weak acid.

Step 3: Application
However, Reason (R) merely states that \(\mathrm{H_2S}\) is a weak acid without mentioning the common ion effect of \(\mathrm{H^+}\) from \(\mathrm{HCl}\), which is the actual reason why its ionisation is suppressed specifically in the presence of \(\mathrm{HCl}\).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation of A.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
हाइड्रोक्लोरिक अम्ल (\(\mathrm{HCl}\)) एक प्रबल विद्युत-अपघट्य है जो पूर्णतः वियोजित होकर \(\mathrm{H^+}\) आयन देता है, जबकि हाइड्रोजन सल्फाइड (\(\mathrm{H_2S}\)) एक दुर्बल द्विक्षारकीय अम्ल है: \(\mathrm{H_2S \rightleftharpoons 2H^+ + S^{2-}}\)।

चरण 2: मूल्यांकन
\(\mathrm{HCl}\) की उपस्थिति में, उभयनिष्ठ \(\mathrm{H^+}\) आयनों की उच्च सांद्रता \(\mathrm{H_2S}\) के आयनन साम्य को प्रतीप दिशा में विस्थापित कर देती है (सम-आयन प्रभाव), जिससे इसका आयनन कम हो जाता है। अतः अभिकथन (A) सत्य है। कारण (R) भी सत्य है क्योंकि \(\mathrm{H_2S}\) वास्तव में एक दुर्बल अम्ल है।

चरण 3: अनुप्रयोग
यद्यपि, कारण (R) केवल यह बताता है कि \(\mathrm{H_2S}\) एक दुर्बल अम्ल है, और इसमें \(\mathrm{HCl}\) से प्राप्त \(\mathrm{H^+}\) के सम-आयन प्रभाव का उल्लेख नहीं है, जो विशेष रूप से \(\mathrm{HCl}\) की उपस्थिति में आयनन कम होने का वास्तविक कारण है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
A और R दोनों सत्य हैं परंतु R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।

answer.text: Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_AR_EQUILIBRIUM_MCQ_Q47 - Dependence of equilibrium constant on temperature

questiontext.text:
In the following question a statement of Assertion (A) followed by a statement of Reason (R) is given. Choose the correct option out of the choices given below.

Assertion (A) : For any chemical reaction at a particular temperature, the equilibrium constant is fixed and is a characteristic property.

Reason (R) : Equilibrium constant is independent of temperature.

निम्नलिखित प्रश्न में अभिकथन (A) के पश्चात कारण (R) का कथन दिया गया है। नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही विकल्प चुनिए।

अभिकथन (A) : किसी निश्चित ताप पर किसी भी रासायनिक अभिक्रिया के लिए साम्य स्थिरांक निश्चित होता है और यह एक अभिलाक्षणिक गुण है।

कारण (R) : साम्य स्थिरांक ताप से स्वतंत्र होता है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The equilibrium constant \(K\) of a reaction is a characteristic constant for a given reaction stoichiometry at a specified temperature.

Step 2: Evaluation
Assertion (A) is true because at a fixed temperature, \(K\) has a unique, constant value independent of initial concentrations, pressure, or catalyst. However, Reason (R) is false because \(K\) depends strongly on temperature according to the van't Hoff equation (\(\ln\frac{K_2}{K_1} = \frac{\Delta H^\circ}{R}\left(\frac{1}{T_1} - \frac{1}{T_2}\right)\)).

Step 3: Application
When temperature changes, \(K\) increases for endothermic reactions and decreases for exothermic reactions.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
A is true but R is false.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
किसी अभिक्रिया का साम्य स्थिरांक \(K\) एक निश्चित ताप पर दी गई अभिक्रिया के लिए एक अभिलाक्षणिक स्थिरांक होता है।

चरण 2: मूल्यांकन
अभिकथन (A) सत्य है क्योंकि एक निश्चित ताप पर \(K\) का मान प्रारंभिक सांद्रताओं, दाब या उत्प्रेरक से स्वतंत्र और नियत होता है। यद्यपि, कारण (R) गलत है क्योंकि वान्ट हॉफ समीकरण (\(\ln\frac{K_2}{K_1} = \frac{\Delta H^\circ}{R}\left(\frac{1}{T_1} - \frac{1}{T_2}\right)\)) के अनुसार \(K\) ताप पर निर्भर करता है।

चरण 3: अनुप्रयोग
ताप बदलने पर ऊष्माशोषी अभिक्रियाओं के लिए \(K\) बढ़ता है तथा ऊष्माक्षेपी अभिक्रियाओं के लिए घटता है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
A सत्य है परंतु R गलत है।

answer.text: Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_AR_EQUILIBRIUM_MCQ_Q48 - Basic nature of aqueous ammonium carbonate

questiontext.text:
In the following question a statement of Assertion (A) followed by a statement of Reason (R) is given. Choose the correct option out of the choices given below.

Assertion (A) : Aqueous solution of ammonium carbonate is basic.

Reason (R) : Acidic/basic nature of a salt solution of a salt of weak acid and weak base depends on \(K_a\) and \(K_b\) value of the acid and the base forming it.

निम्नलिखित प्रश्न में अभिकथन (A) के पश्चात कारण (R) का कथन दिया गया है। नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही विकल्प चुनिए।

अभिकथन (A) : अमोनियम कार्बोनेट का जलीय विलयन क्षारीय होता है।

कारण (R) : दुर्बल अम्ल और दुर्बल क्षारक के लवण के विलयन की अम्लीय/क्षारीय प्रकृति इसे बनाने वाले अम्ल और क्षारक के \(K_a\) और \(K_b\) मानों पर निर्भर करती है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
For a salt of a weak acid and a weak base, both the cation and anion undergo hydrolysis, and the pH of the aqueous solution is governed by \(\text{pH} = 7 + \frac{1}{2}(\text{p}K_a - \text{p}K_b)\).

Step 2: Evaluation
Ammonium carbonate, \(\mathrm{(NH_4)_2CO_3}\), is formed from weak base \(\mathrm{NH_4OH}\) (\(K_b \approx 1.8 \times 10^{-5}\)) and weak acid \(\mathrm{H_2CO_3}\) (\(K_{a_1} \approx 4.3 \times 10^{-7}\), \(K_{a_2} \approx 5.6 \times 10^{-11}\)). Since \(K_b > K_a\), the carbonate ion hydrolyses more strongly than the ammonium ion, producing excess \(\mathrm{OH^-}\) ions and making the solution basic.

Step 3: Application
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and comparing \(K_a\) and \(K_b\) directly explains why the ammonium carbonate solution is basic.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
दुर्बल अम्ल और दुर्बल क्षारक के लवण के लिए धनायन और ऋणायन दोनों का जल-अपघटन होता है, तथा जलीय विलयन की pH सूत्र \(\text{pH} = 7 + \frac{1}{2}(\text{p}K_a - \text{p}K_b)\) द्वारा निर्धारित होती है।

चरण 2: मूल्यांकन
अमोनियम कार्बोनेट, \(\mathrm{(NH_4)_2CO_3}\), दुर्बल क्षारक \(\mathrm{NH_4OH}\) (\(K_b \approx 1.8 \times 10^{-5}\)) और दुर्बल अम्ल \(\mathrm{H_2CO_3}\) (\(K_{a_1} \approx 4.3 \times 10^{-7}\), \(K_{a_2} \approx 5.6 \times 10^{-11}\)) से बनता है। चूँकि \(K_b > K_a\) है, इसलिए कार्बोनेट आयन का जल-अपघटन अमोनियम आयन की तुलना में अधिक होता है, जिससे \(\mathrm{OH^-}\) आयन अधिक बनते हैं और विलयन क्षारीय होता है।

चरण 3: अनुप्रयोग
अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं, और \(K_a\) तथा \(K_b\) की तुलना ही यह स्पष्ट करती है कि अमोनियम कार्बोनेट का विलयन क्षारीय क्यों होता है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
A और R दोनों सत्य हैं तथा R, A की सही व्याख्या है।

answer.text: Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_AR_EQUILIBRIUM_MCQ_Q49 - Buffer behaviour of ammonium acetate solution

questiontext.text:
In the following question a statement of Assertion (A) followed by a statement of Reason (R) is given. Choose the correct option out of the choices given below.

Assertion (A) : An aqueous solution of ammonium acetate can act as a buffer.

Reason (R) : Acetic acid is a weak acid and \(\mathrm{NH_4OH}\) is a weak base.

निम्नलिखित प्रश्न में अभिकथन (A) के पश्चात कारण (R) का कथन दिया गया है। नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही विकल्प चुनिए।

अभिकथन (A) : अमोनियम ऐसीटेट का जलीय विलयन एक बफर के रूप में कार्य कर सकता है।

कारण (R) : ऐसीटिक अम्ल एक दुर्बल अम्ल है और \(\mathrm{NH_4OH}\) एक दुर्बल क्षारक है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A salt formed from a weak acid and a weak base can act as a simple (single-salt) buffer in aqueous solution because it supplies both a weak conjugate base (to neutralise added \(\mathrm{H^+}\)) and a weak conjugate acid (to neutralise added \(\mathrm{OH^-}\)).

Step 2: Evaluation
Ammonium acetate (\(\mathrm{CH_3COONH_4}\)) dissociates into \(\mathrm{CH_3COO^-}\) and \(\mathrm{NH_4^+}\). Because \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\) is a weak acid, \(\mathrm{CH_3COO^-}\) reacts with any added \(\mathrm{H^+}\) to form undissociated \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\); because \(\mathrm{NH_4OH}\) is a weak base, \(\mathrm{NH_4^+}\) reacts with any added \(\mathrm{OH^-}\) to form undissociated \(\mathrm{NH_4OH}\). Thus, the solution resists changes in pH.

Step 3: Application
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and the weak nature of both acetic acid and \(\mathrm{NH_4OH}\) directly explains why ammonium acetate acts as a buffer.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
दुर्बल अम्ल और दुर्बल क्षारक से बना लवण जलीय विलयन में एक सरल (एकल-लवण) बफर के रूप में कार्य कर सकता है, क्योंकि यह दुर्बल संयुग्मी क्षारक (जो मिलाए गए \(\mathrm{H^+}\) को उदासीन करता है) और दुर्बल संयुग्मी अम्ल (जो मिलाए गए \(\mathrm{OH^-}\) को उदासीन करता है) दोनों प्रदान करता है।

चरण 2: मूल्यांकन
अमोनियम ऐसीटेट (\(\mathrm{CH_3COONH_4}\)) वियोजित होकर \(\mathrm{CH_3COO^-}\) और \(\mathrm{NH_4^+}\) देता है। चूँकि \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\) एक दुर्बल अम्ल है, अतः \(\mathrm{CH_3COO^-}\) मिलाए गए \(\mathrm{H^+}\) के साथ अभिक्रिया करके अवियोजित \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\) बनाता है; और चूँकि \(\mathrm{NH_4OH}\) एक दुर्बल क्षारक है, अतः \(\mathrm{NH_4^+}\) मिलाए गए \(\mathrm{OH^-}\) के साथ अभिक्रिया करके अवियोजित \(\mathrm{NH_4OH}\) बनाता है। इस प्रकार विलयन pH परिवर्तन का विरोध करता है।

चरण 3: अनुप्रयोग
अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं, तथा ऐसीटिक अम्ल और \(\mathrm{NH_4OH}\) दोनों की दुर्बल प्रकृति ही यह स्पष्ट करती है कि अमोनियम ऐसीटेट बफर की तरह कार्य क्यों करता है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
A और R दोनों सत्य हैं तथा R, A की सही व्याख्या है।

answer.text: Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation of A.
A is false but R is true.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_AR_EQUILIBRIUM_MCQ_Q50 - Addition of helium at constant pressure to PCl5 dissociation

questiontext.text:
In the following question a statement of Assertion (A) followed by a statement of Reason (R) is given. Choose the correct option out of the choices given below.

Assertion (A) : In the dissociation of \(\mathrm{PCl_5}\) at constant pressure and temperature addition of helium at equilibrium increases the dissociation of \(\mathrm{PCl_5}\).

Reason (R) : Helium removes \(\mathrm{Cl_2}\) from the field of action.

निम्नलिखित प्रश्न में अभिकथन (A) के पश्चात कारण (R) का कथन दिया गया है। नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही विकल्प चुनिए।

अभिकथन (A) : स्थिर दाब और ताप पर \(\mathrm{PCl_5}\) के वियोजन में साम्यावस्था पर हीलियम मिलाने से \(\mathrm{PCl_5}\) का वियोजन बढ़ जाता है।

कारण (R) : हीलियम अभिक्रिया क्षेत्र से \(\mathrm{Cl_2}\) को हटा देता है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
For the dissociation equilibrium \(\mathrm{PCl_5(g) \rightleftharpoons PCl_3(g) + Cl_2(g)}\), \(\Delta n_g = 2 - 1 = +1 > 0\). When an inert gas is added at constant pressure and temperature, the volume of the system must increase to keep total pressure constant.

Step 2: Evaluation
Increasing volume decreases the partial pressures of all gaseous species, so by Le Chatelier's principle the equilibrium shifts toward the side with a larger number of gaseous moles (forward direction), increasing the dissociation of \(\mathrm{PCl_5}\). Thus, Assertion (A) is true. However, helium is a chemically inert noble gas and does not react with or remove \(\mathrm{Cl_2}\), so Reason (R) is false.

Step 3: Application
Since A is true and R is false, the statement attributing the shift to chemical removal of \(\mathrm{Cl_2}\) is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
A is true but R is false.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
वियोजन साम्य \(\mathrm{PCl_5(g) \rightleftharpoons PCl_3(g) + Cl_2(g)}\) के लिए \(\Delta n_g = 2 - 1 = +1 > 0\) है। स्थिर दाब और ताप पर अक्रिय गैस मिलाने पर, कुल दाब स्थिर रखने के लिए निकाय का आयतन बढ़ता है।

चरण 2: मूल्यांकन
आयतन बढ़ने से सभी गैसीय स्पीशीज़ के आंशिक दाब कम हो जाते हैं, अतः ला शातेलिए के सिद्धांत के अनुसार साम्य अधिक गैसीय मोलों वाली दिशा (अग्र दिशा) में विस्थापित होता है, जिससे \(\mathrm{PCl_5}\) का वियोजन बढ़ जाता है। इसलिए अभिकथन (A) सत्य है। यद्यपि, हीलियम एक रासायनिक रूप से अक्रिय उत्कृष्ट गैस है और यह \(\mathrm{Cl_2}\) से अभिक्रिया नहीं करती या उसे हटाती नहीं है, अतः कारण (R) गलत है।

चरण 3: अनुप्रयोग
चूँकि A सत्य है और R गलत है, इसलिए \(\mathrm{Cl_2}\) के रासायनिक निष्कासन वाला कथन असत्य है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
A सत्य है परंतु R गलत है।

answer.text: Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q01 - Reaction that is not a redox reaction

questiontext.text: Which of the following is not an example of redox reaction?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A redox reaction is a chemical reaction in which there is a simultaneous change in oxidation numbers of reacting species, involving both oxidation (increase in oxidation number) and reduction (decrease in oxidation number). A reaction in which no atom undergoes any change in oxidation state is a non-redox reaction.

Step 2: Evaluation
In \(\mathrm{CuO} + \mathrm{H}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cu} + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\), the oxidation number of \(\mathrm{Cu}\) decreases from \(+2\) to \(0\) (reduction) and that of \(\mathrm{H}\) increases from \(0\) to \(+1\) (oxidation).
In \(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3 + 3\mathrm{CO} \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{Fe} + 3\mathrm{CO}_2\), the oxidation number of \(\mathrm{Fe}\) decreases from \(+3\) to \(0\) (reduction) and that of \(\mathrm{C}\) increases from \(+2\) to \(+4\) (oxidation).
In \(2\mathrm{K} + \mathrm{F}_2 \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{KF}\), the oxidation number of \(\mathrm{K}\) increases from \(0\) to \(+1\) (oxidation) and that of \(\mathrm{F}\) decreases from \(0\) to \(-1\) (reduction).
In \(\mathrm{BaCl}_2 + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4 \longrightarrow \mathrm{BaSO}_4 + 2\mathrm{HCl}\), the oxidation numbers of all elements remain unchanged: \(\mathrm{Ba}\) is \(+2\), \(\mathrm{Cl}\) is \(-1\), \(\mathrm{H}\) is \(+1\), \(\mathrm{S}\) is \(+6\), and \(\mathrm{O}\) is \(-2\) on both sides.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Since no element changes its oxidation state in the double displacement reaction \(\mathrm{BaCl}_2 + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4 \longrightarrow \mathrm{BaSO}_4 + 2\mathrm{HCl}\), it is not a redox reaction.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q02 - Strongest oxidising agent from standard potentials

questiontext.text:
The more positive the value of \(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus}\), the greater is the tendency of the species to get reduced. Using the standard electrode potential of redox couples given below find out which of the following is the strongest oxidising agent.

\(\mathbf{E}^{\ominus}\) values: \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}/\mathrm{Fe}^{2+} = +0.77\); \(\mathrm{I}_2(\mathrm{s})/\mathrm{I}^{-} = +0.54\); \(\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}/\mathrm{Cu} = +0.34\); \(\mathrm{Ag}^{+}/\mathrm{Ag} = +0.80\mathrm{V}\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
An oxidising agent is a species that gains electrons and gets reduced. A more positive standard reduction potential \(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus}\) indicates a greater tendency for the oxidised form of the redox couple to accept electrons and undergo reduction, making it a stronger oxidising agent.

Step 2: Evaluation
Comparing the given standard reduction potentials:
\(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus}(\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}/\mathrm{Cu}) = +0.34\ \mathrm{V}\)
\(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus}(\mathrm{I}_2(\mathrm{s})/\mathrm{I}^-) = +0.54\ \mathrm{V}\)
\(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus}(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}/\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}) = +0.77\ \mathrm{V}\)
\(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus}(\mathrm{Ag}^{+}/\mathrm{Ag}) = +0.80\ \mathrm{V}\)
The decreasing order of standard reduction potential is \(\mathrm{Ag}^{+}/\mathrm{Ag} > \mathrm{Fe}^{3+}/\mathrm{Fe}^{2+} > \mathrm{I}_2/\mathrm{I}^- > \mathrm{Cu}^{2+}/\mathrm{Cu}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Because the \(\mathrm{Ag}^{+}/\mathrm{Ag}\) couple has the highest positive \(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus}\) value (\(+0.80\ \mathrm{V}\)), \(\mathrm{Ag}^{+}\) has the greatest tendency to get reduced and is the strongest oxidising agent among the given species.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q03 - Predicting redox feasibility from standard potentials

questiontext.text:
\(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus}\) values of some redox couples are given below. On the basis of these values choose the correct option.

\(\mathbf{E}^{\ominus}\) values: \(\mathrm{Br}_2/\mathrm{Br}^{-} = +1.90\); \(\mathrm{Ag}^{+}/\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{s}) = +0.80\); \(\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}/\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{s}) = +0.34\); \(\mathrm{I}_2(\mathrm{s})/\mathrm{I}^{-} = +0.54\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A species with a lower standard reduction potential \(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus}\) acts as a reducing agent and can reduce the oxidised form of a redox couple that has a higher standard reduction potential \(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus}\).

Step 2: Evaluation
The \(\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}/\mathrm{Cu}\) couple has \(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus} = +0.34\ \mathrm{V}\), which is lower than the \(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus}\) values of \(\mathrm{I}_2/\mathrm{I}^-\) (\(+0.54\ \mathrm{V}\)), \(\mathrm{Ag}^+/\mathrm{Ag}\) (\(+0.80\ \mathrm{V}\)), and \(\mathrm{Br}_2/\mathrm{Br}^-\) (\(+1.90\ \mathrm{V}\)).
Therefore, \(\mathrm{Cu}\) can reduce \(\mathrm{I}_2\) to \(\mathrm{I}^-\), \(\mathrm{Ag}^+\) to \(\mathrm{Ag}\), and \(\mathrm{Br}_2\) to \(\mathrm{Br}^-\).
However, \(\mathrm{Cu}\) cannot reduce \(\mathrm{Br}^-\), \(\mathrm{I}^-\), or \(\mathrm{Ag}\), because those species are already in their reduced forms.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Based on the given \(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus}\) values, \(\mathrm{Cu}\) will reduce \(\mathrm{Br}_2\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q04 - Non-feasible redox reaction pair

questiontext.text:
Using the standard electrode potential, find out the pair between which redox reaction is not feasible.

\(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus}\) values: \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}/\mathrm{Fe}^{2+} = +0.77\); \(\mathrm{I}_2/\mathrm{I}^- = +0.54\); \(\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}/\mathrm{Cu} = +0.34\); \(\mathrm{Ag}^+/\mathrm{Ag} = +0.80\ \mathrm{V}\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
\(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus}(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}/\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}) = +0.77\ \mathrm{V}\)
\(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus}(\mathrm{I}_2/\mathrm{I}^-) = +0.54\ \mathrm{V}\)
\(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus}(\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}/\mathrm{Cu}) = +0.34\ \mathrm{V}\)
\(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus}(\mathrm{Ag}^+/\mathrm{Ag}) = +0.80\ \mathrm{V}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
A redox reaction is spontaneous (feasible) under standard conditions when the standard cell potential \(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus}_{\text{cell}}\) is positive (\(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus}_{\text{cell}} > 0\)).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\mathrm{E}^{\ominus}_{\text{cell}} = \mathrm{E}^{\ominus}_{\text{cathode (reduction)}} - \mathrm{E}^{\ominus}_{\text{anode (oxidation)}}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
For \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\) and \(\mathrm{I}^-\): \(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus}_{\text{cell}} = 0.77 - 0.54 = +0.23\ \mathrm{V} > 0\) (feasible).
For \(\mathrm{Ag}^+\) and \(\mathrm{Cu}\): \(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus}_{\text{cell}} = 0.80 - 0.34 = +0.46\ \mathrm{V} > 0\) (feasible).
For \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\) and \(\mathrm{Cu}\): \(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus}_{\text{cell}} = 0.77 - 0.34 = +0.43\ \mathrm{V} > 0\) (feasible).
For \(\mathrm{Ag}\) and \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\): \(\mathrm{Ag}\) must undergo oxidation and \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\) must undergo reduction, giving \(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus}_{\text{cell}} = 0.77 - 0.80 = -0.03\ \mathrm{V} < 0\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Since \(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus}_{\text{cell}}\) is negative (\(-0.03\ \mathrm{V}\)) for the reaction between \(\mathrm{Ag}\) and \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\), the redox reaction between \(\mathrm{Ag}\) and \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\) is not feasible.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q05 - Dual behaviour of thiosulphate with halogens

questiontext.text:
Thiosulphate reacts differently with iodine and bromine in the reactions given below:

\[2\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_3^{2-} + \mathrm{I}_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{S}_4\mathrm{O}_6^{2-} + 2\mathrm{I}^-\]\[\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_3^{2-} + 2\mathrm{Br}_2 + 5\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-} + 2\mathrm{Br}^- + 10\ \mathrm{H}^+\]

Which of the following statements justifies the above dual behaviour of thiosulphate?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A stronger oxidising agent oxidises a reducing agent to a higher oxidation state than a weaker oxidising agent does.

Step 2: Evaluation
In \(\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_3^{2-}\), the average oxidation state of sulphur is \(+2\).
In the reaction with \(\mathrm{I}_2\), thiosulphate is oxidised to tetrathionate (\(\mathrm{S}_4\mathrm{O}_6^{2-}\)), where the average oxidation state of sulphur increases from \(+2\) to \(+2.5\), while \(\mathrm{I}_2\) is reduced to \(\mathrm{I}^-\).
In the reaction with \(\mathrm{Br}_2\), thiosulphate is oxidised to sulphate (\(\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}\)), where the oxidation state of sulphur increases from \(+2\) to \(+6\), while \(\mathrm{Br}_2\) is reduced to \(\mathrm{Br}^-\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Because bromine oxidises sulphur in thiosulphate to a much higher oxidation state (\(+6\)) than iodine does (\(+2.5\)), bromine is a stronger oxidant than iodine.

answer.text: Bromine is a stronger oxidant than iodine.
Bromine is a weaker oxidant than iodine.
Thiosulphate undergoes oxidation by bromine and reduction by iodine in these reactions.
Bromine undergoes oxidation and iodine undergoes reduction in these reactions.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q06 - Incorrect rule for assigning oxidation number

questiontext.text: The oxidation number of an element in a compound is evaluated on the basis of certain rules. Which of the following rules is not correct in this respect?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Standard rules for assigning oxidation numbers state that an element in its free or uncombined state has an oxidation number of zero, the algebraic sum of oxidation numbers of all atoms in a neutral compound is zero, and fluorine always has an oxidation number of \(-1\) in all its compounds because it is the most electronegative element.

Step 2: Evaluation
Hydrogen generally has an oxidation number of \(+1\) when combined with non-metals. However, when hydrogen is combined with metals in binary metal hydrides (such as \(\mathrm{NaH}\), \(\mathrm{LiH}\), or \(\mathrm{CaH}_2\)), hydrogen is more electronegative than the metal and has an oxidation number of \(-1\). Thus, the statement that the oxidation number of hydrogen is always \(+1\) is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The rule stating that the oxidation number of hydrogen is always \(+1\) is not correct.

answer.text: The oxidation number of hydrogen is always \(+1\).
The algebraic sum of all the oxidation numbers in a compound is zero.
An element in the free or the uncombined state bears oxidation number zero.
In all its compounds, the oxidation number of fluorine is \(-1\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q07 - Compound exhibiting two different oxidation states

questiontext.text: In which of the following compounds, an element exhibits two different oxidation states.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In ionic compounds containing a polyatomic cation and a polyatomic anion made of the same element, the atoms of that element in the two different ions can have distinct oxidation states.

Step 2: Evaluation
Ammonium nitrate (\(\mathrm{NH}_4\mathrm{NO}_3\)) is an ionic compound composed of the ammonium cation (\(\mathrm{NH}_4^+\)) and the nitrate anion (\(\mathrm{NO}_3^-\)).
In \(\mathrm{NH}_4^+\), let the oxidation number of \(\mathrm{N}\) be \(x\): \(x + 4(+1) = +1 \Rightarrow x = -3\).
In \(\mathrm{NO}_3^-\), let the oxidation number of \(\mathrm{N}\) be \(y\): \(y + 3(-2) = -1 \Rightarrow y = +5\).
In \(\mathrm{NH}_2\mathrm{OH}\), \(\mathrm{N}\) has oxidation number \(-1\); in \(\mathrm{N}_2\mathrm{H}_4\), \(\mathrm{N}\) has oxidation number \(-2\); and in \(\mathrm{N}_3\mathrm{H}\), the average oxidation number of \(\mathrm{N}\) is \(-\frac{1}{3}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Nitrogen exhibits two different oxidation states (\(-3\) and \(+5\)) in \(\mathrm{NH}_4\mathrm{NO}_3\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q08 - Increasing oxidation number of central atom

questiontext.text: Which of the following arrangements represent increasing oxidation number of the central atom?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The four oxoanions are \(\mathrm{CrO}_2^-\), \(\mathrm{ClO}_3^-\), \(\mathrm{CrO}_4^{2-}\), and \(\mathrm{MnO}_4^-\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Oxygen is assigned an oxidation number of \(-2\) in each oxoanion, and the sum of the oxidation numbers equals the overall charge on the ion.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Oxidation number of central atom} + n(-2) = \text{Charge on the ion}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
1. In \(\mathrm{CrO}_2^-\): \(x + 2(-2) = -1 \Rightarrow x = +3\).
2. In \(\mathrm{ClO}_3^-\): \(x + 3(-2) = -1 \Rightarrow x = +5\).
3. In \(\mathrm{CrO}_4^{2-}\): \(x + 4(-2) = -2 \Rightarrow x = +6\).
4. In \(\mathrm{MnO}_4^-\): \(x + 4(-2) = -1 \Rightarrow x = +7\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Since \(+3 < +5 < +6 < +7\), the arrangement in increasing order of oxidation number of the central atom is \(\mathrm{CrO}_2^-\), \(\mathrm{ClO}_3^-\), \(\mathrm{CrO}_4^{2-}\), \(\mathrm{MnO}_4^-\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q09 - Largest oxidation number from outer configuration

questiontext.text: The largest oxidation number exhibited by an element depends on its outer electronic configuration. With which of the following outer electronic configurations the element will exhibit largest oxidation number?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
For \(3d\)-series transition elements, the maximum possible oxidation state is equal to the total number of valence electrons in the \(4s\) and \(3d\) orbitals (up to manganese), because both \(4s\) and unpaired \(3d\) electrons can participate in bonding.

Step 2: Evaluation
For \(3d^{1}4s^{2}\), total valence electrons \(= 1 + 2 = 3\) (maximum oxidation state \(+3\)).
For \(3d^{3}4s^{2}\), total valence electrons \(= 3 + 2 = 5\) (maximum oxidation state \(+5\)).
For \(3d^{5}4s^{1}\), total valence electrons \(= 5 + 1 = 6\) (maximum oxidation state \(+6\)).
For \(3d^{5}4s^{2}\), total valence electrons \(= 5 + 2 = 7\) (maximum oxidation state \(+7\)).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
An element with the outer electronic configuration \(3d^{5}4s^{2}\) will exhibit the largest oxidation number (\(+7\)).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q10 - Identifying a disproportionation reaction

questiontext.text: Identify disproportionation reaction

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A disproportionation reaction is a redox reaction in which an element in one intermediate oxidation state is simultaneously oxidised to a higher oxidation state and reduced to a lower oxidation state.

Step 2: Evaluation
In \(\mathrm{CH}_4 + 2\mathrm{O}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{CO}_2 + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\), \(\mathrm{C}\) is oxidised (\(-4\) to \(+4\)) and \(\mathrm{O}\) is reduced (\(0\) to \(-2\)); different elements undergo oxidation and reduction.
In \(\mathrm{CH}_4 + 4\mathrm{Cl}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{CCl}_4 + 4\mathrm{HCl}\), \(\mathrm{C}\) is oxidised (\(-4\) to \(+4\)) and \(\mathrm{Cl}\) is reduced (\(0\) to \(-1\)); different elements undergo oxidation and reduction.
In \(2\mathrm{F}_2 + 2\mathrm{OH}^- \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{F}^- + \mathrm{OF}_2 + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\), \(\mathrm{F}\) is only reduced (\(0\) to \(-1\) in both \(\mathrm{F}^-\) and \(\mathrm{OF}_2\)), while \(\mathrm{O}\) is oxidised (\(-2\) to \(+2\) in \(\mathrm{OF}_2\)).
In \(2\mathrm{NO}_2 + 2\mathrm{OH}^- \longrightarrow \mathrm{NO}_2^- + \mathrm{NO}_3^- + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\), the oxidation number of \(\mathrm{N}\) in \(\mathrm{NO}_2\) is \(+4\). It decreases to \(+3\) in \(\mathrm{NO}_2^-\) (reduction) and increases to \(+5\) in \(\mathrm{NO}_3^-\) (oxidation).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The reaction \(2\mathrm{NO}_2 + 2\mathrm{OH}^- \longrightarrow \mathrm{NO}_2^- + \mathrm{NO}_3^- + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) is a disproportionation reaction.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q11 - Element not showing disproportionation tendency

questiontext.text: Which of the following elements does not show disproportionation tendency?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
To undergo disproportionation, an element must be able to exist in at least three oxidation states so that an intermediate oxidation state can simultaneously increase (oxidation) and decrease (reduction).

Step 2: Evaluation
Chlorine (\(\mathrm{Cl}\)), bromine (\(\mathrm{Br}\)), and iodine (\(\mathrm{I}\)) exhibit multiple oxidation states ranging from \(-1\) to \(+7\), so they readily show disproportionation reactions.
Fluorine (\(\mathrm{F}\)) is the most electronegative element in the periodic table and exhibits only \(-1\) oxidation state in its compounds (besides \(0\) in elemental \(\mathrm{F}_2\)). It cannot be oxidised to any positive oxidation state.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Fluorine (\(\mathrm{F}\)) does not show disproportionation tendency.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQII_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q12 - Decomposition of potassium chlorate redox analysis

questiontext.text:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are not true about the following decomposition reaction.

\[2\mathrm{KClO}_3 \rightarrow 2\mathrm{KCl} + 3\mathrm{O}_2\]

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Determining the oxidation numbers of every element before and after the reaction identifies which species are oxidised, reduced, or unchanged.

Step 2: Evaluation
In \(\mathrm{KClO}_3\), the oxidation numbers are \(\mathrm{K} = +1\), \(\mathrm{Cl} = +5\), and \(\mathrm{O} = -2\).
In \(\mathrm{KCl}\) and \(\mathrm{O}_2\), the oxidation numbers are \(\mathrm{K} = +1\), \(\mathrm{Cl} = -1\), and \(\mathrm{O} = 0\).
Thus, \(\mathrm{K}\) remains in the \(+1\) oxidation state (it undergoes neither oxidation nor reduction), \(\mathrm{Cl}\) is reduced from \(+5\) to \(-1\), and \(\mathrm{O}\) is oxidised from \(-2\) to \(0\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The reaction is a redox reaction in which potassium does not undergo oxidation. Therefore, the statements that potassium is undergoing oxidation and that none of the species are undergoing oxidation or reduction are not true.

answer.text: None of the species are undergoing oxidation or reduction

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQII_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q13 - Oxidant and reductant in zinc hydrochloric acid reaction

questiontext.text:
Identify the correct statement (s) in relation to the following reaction:

\[\mathrm{Zn} + 2\mathrm{HCl} \rightarrow \mathrm{ZnCl}_2 + \mathrm{H}_2\]

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A reductant (reducing agent) donates electrons and gets oxidised (its oxidation number increases). An oxidant (oxidising agent) accepts electrons and gets reduced (its oxidation number decreases).

Step 2: Evaluation
In \(\mathrm{Zn} + 2\mathrm{HCl} \rightarrow \mathrm{ZnCl}_2 + \mathrm{H}_2\):
The oxidation number of \(\mathrm{Zn}\) increases from \(0\) to \(+2\) in \(\mathrm{ZnCl}_2\), so zinc is oxidised and acts as a reductant.
The oxidation number of \(\mathrm{H}^+\) decreases from \(+1\) in \(\mathrm{HCl}\) to \(0\) in \(\mathrm{H}_2\), so hydrogen ion is reduced and acts as an oxidant.
The oxidation number of \(\mathrm{Cl}^-\) remains unchanged at \(-1\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
In this reaction, hydrogen ion is acting as an oxidant and zinc is acting as a reductant.

answer.text: Hydrogen ion is acting as an oxidant

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQII_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q14 - Outer configurations exhibiting multiple oxidation states

questiontext.text: The exhibition of various oxidation states by an element is also related to the outer orbital electronic configuration of its atom. Atom(s) having which of the following outermost electronic configurations will exhibit more than one oxidation state in its compounds.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Elements exhibit variable oxidation states when they can lose or share different numbers of electrons from their valence shells (such as \(ns\) and \((n-1)d\) orbitals in transition metals, or \(ns\) and \(np\) orbitals in \(p\)-block elements).

Step 2: Evaluation
An atom with \(3s^{1}\) configuration (alkali metal, \(\mathrm{Na}\)) only loses its single \(3s\) electron to exhibit a fixed oxidation state of \(+1\).
An atom with \(3d^{1}4s^{2}\) configuration (\(\mathrm{Sc}\)) loses all three outer electrons together to exhibit only the \(+3\) oxidation state in its compounds.
An atom with \(3d^{2}4s^{2}\) configuration (\(\mathrm{Ti}\)) can lose electrons from both \(4s\) and \(3d\) orbitals to exhibit multiple oxidation states such as \(+2\), \(+3\), and \(+4\).
An atom with \(3s^{2}3p^{3}\) configuration (\(\mathrm{P}\)) can gain or share electrons to exhibit multiple oxidation states such as \(-3\), \(+3\), and \(+5\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Atoms having the outermost electronic configurations \(3d^{2}4s^{2}\) and \(3s^{2}3p^{3}\) exhibit more than one oxidation state in their compounds.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQII_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q15 - Disproportionation of phosphorus in alkaline medium

questiontext.text:
Identify the correct statements with reference to the given reaction

\[\mathrm{P}_{4} + 3\mathrm{OH}^{-} + 3\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O} \rightarrow \mathrm{PH}_{3} + 3\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{PO}_{4}^{-}\]

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
By calculating the oxidation numbers of each element on the reactant and product sides, we can determine which species undergo oxidation, reduction, or no change.

Step 2: Evaluation
In \(\mathrm{P}_4\), the oxidation number of phosphorus is \(0\).
In \(\mathrm{PH}_3\), the oxidation number of phosphorus is \(-3\) (since \(\mathrm{H}\) is \(+1\)), indicating reduction.
In the phosphorus oxoanion product (\(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{PO}_4^-\) or \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{PO}_2^-\)), the oxidation number of phosphorus is positive (\(+5\) in \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{PO}_4^-\)), indicating oxidation.
Thus, phosphorus undergoes both oxidation and reduction (disproportionation).
Meanwhile, hydrogen has an oxidation number of \(+1\) in \(\mathrm{OH}^-\), \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\), \(\mathrm{PH}_3\), and \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{PO}_4^-\), so hydrogen undergoes neither oxidation nor reduction.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Phosphorus is undergoing oxidation as well as reduction, and hydrogen is undergoing neither oxidation nor reduction.

answer.text: Phosphorus is undergoing oxidation as well as reduction.
Hydrogen is undergoing neither oxidation nor reduction.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQII_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q16 - Electrodes acting as anodes with SHE

questiontext.text: Which of the following electrodes will act as anodes, when connected to Standard Hydrogen Electrode?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The Standard Hydrogen Electrode (SHE) has a standard electrode potential \(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus} = 0.00\ \mathrm{V}\). When an electrode is connected to SHE, the electrode with the lower (more negative) standard reduction potential undergoes oxidation and acts as the anode, while the electrode with the higher (more positive) standard reduction potential undergoes reduction and acts as the cathode.

Step 2: Evaluation
For \(\mathrm{Al} / \mathrm{Al}^{3+}\), \(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus} = -1.66\ \mathrm{V} < 0.00\ \mathrm{V}\), so it acts as an anode.
For \(\mathrm{Fe} / \mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\), \(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus} = -0.44\ \mathrm{V} < 0.00\ \mathrm{V}\), so it acts as an anode.
For \(\mathrm{Cu} / \mathrm{Cu}^{2+}\), \(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus} = +0.34\ \mathrm{V} > 0.00\ \mathrm{V}\), so it acts as a cathode.
For \(\mathrm{F}_2(\mathrm{g}) / 2\mathrm{F}^-(\mathrm{aq})\), \(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus} = +2.87\ \mathrm{V} > 0.00\ \mathrm{V}\), so it acts as a cathode.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The \(\mathrm{Al} / \mathrm{Al}^{3+}\) (\(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus} = -1.66\)) and \(\mathrm{Fe} / \mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\) (\(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus} = -0.44\)) electrodes will act as anodes when connected to the Standard Hydrogen Electrode.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCHING_REDOXREACTIONS_MATCH_Q27 - Oxidation states of central atoms in ions

questiontext.text: Match Column I with Column II for the oxidation states of the central atoms.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The given species are \(\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}^{2-}\), \(\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-}\), \(\mathrm{VO}_{3}^{-}\), and \(\mathrm{FeF}_{6}^{3-}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Oxygen has an oxidation state of \(-2\) and fluorine has an oxidation state of \(-1\). The algebraic sum of the oxidation states of all atoms in an ion equals the net charge on the ion.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\sum (\text{number of atoms} \times \text{oxidation state}) = \text{charge on the ion}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
1. For \(\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}^{2-}\): \(2x + 7(-2) = -2 \Rightarrow 2x = +12 \Rightarrow x = +6\).
2. For \(\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-}\): \(x + 4(-2) = -1 \Rightarrow x = +7\).
3. For \(\mathrm{VO}_{3}^{-}\): \(x + 3(-2) = -1 \Rightarrow x = +5\).
4. For \(\mathrm{FeF}_{6}^{3-}\): \(x + 6(-1) = -3 \Rightarrow x = +3\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The oxidation states of the central atoms are: \(\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}^{2-} \rightarrow +6\), \(\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-} \rightarrow +7\), \(\mathrm{VO}_{3}^{-} \rightarrow +5\), and \(\mathrm{FeF}_{6}^{3-} \rightarrow +3\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCHING_REDOXREACTIONS_MATCH_Q28 - Matching redox terms and oxidation numbers

questiontext.text: Match the items in Column I with relevant items in Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Basic definitions of ions and standard rules for assigning oxidation numbers allow direct matching of each term or chemical species to its corresponding value or name.

Step 2: Evaluation
1. Ions having a positive charge are called cations.
2. The algebraic sum of the oxidation numbers of all atoms in a neutral molecule is \(0\).
3. The oxidation number of a monoatomic ion equals its charge, so the oxidation number of hydrogen ion (\(\mathrm{H}^{+}\)) is \(+1\).
4. Fluorine always exhibits an oxidation number of \(-1\) in all its compounds, including \(\mathrm{NaF}\).
5. Ions having a negative charge are called anions.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matches are: ions having positive charge \(\rightarrow\) Cation; sum of oxidation numbers in a neutral molecule \(\rightarrow\) \(0\); oxidation number of \(\mathrm{H}^{+}\) \(\rightarrow\) \(+1\); oxidation number of fluorine in \(\mathrm{NaF}\) \(\rightarrow\) \(-1\); ions having negative charge \(\rightarrow\) Anion.

subquestion.text: The sum of oxidation number of all atoms in a neutral molecule

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AR_REDOXREACTIONS_AR_Q29 - Fluorine as best oxidant and electronegativity

questiontext.text:
In the following question a statement of assertion (A) followed by a statement of reason (R) is given. Choose the correct option out of the choices given below.

Assertion (A) : Among halogens fluorine is the best oxidant.

Reason (R) : Fluorine is the most electronegative atom.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The oxidising power of halogens in aqueous solution depends on the overall standard reduction potential (\(\mathrm{E}^{\ominus}\)), which is governed by bond dissociation enthalpy, electron gain enthalpy, and hydration enthalpy of the halide ion.

Step 2: Evaluation
Assertion (A) is true: fluorine has the highest standard reduction potential (\(+2.87\ \mathrm{V}\)) among all halogens, making it the strongest oxidising agent.
Reason (R) is also true: fluorine has the highest electronegativity on the Pauling scale.
However, Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A), because fluorine's superior oxidising ability in aqueous medium arises primarily from the low \(\mathrm{F}-\mathrm{F}\) bond dissociation enthalpy and the very high hydration enthalpy of the small \(\mathrm{F}^-\) ion, rather than electronegativity alone.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

answer.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AR_REDOXREACTIONS_AR_Q30 - Permanganate ion reaction with potassium iodide

questiontext.text:
In the following question a statement of assertion (A) followed by a statement of reason (R) is given. Choose the correct option out of the choices given below.

Assertion (A): In the reaction between potassium permanganate and potassium iodide, permanganate ions act as oxidising agent.

Reason (R) : Oxidation state of manganese changes from \(+2\) to \(+7\) during the reaction.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
An oxidising agent oxidises another species while itself undergoing reduction (a decrease in oxidation state).

Step 2: Evaluation
Assertion (A) is true: in the reaction between \(\mathrm{KMnO}_4\) and \(\mathrm{KI}\), permanganate ions (\(\mathrm{MnO}_4^-\)) oxidise iodide ions (\(\mathrm{I}^-\)) to iodine (\(\mathrm{I}_2\) or \(\mathrm{IO}_3^-\)), so \(\mathrm{MnO}_4^-\) acts as an oxidising agent.
Reason (R) is false: in \(\mathrm{MnO}_4^-\), manganese is in the \(+7\) oxidation state, and during the reaction it is reduced to \(+2\) (in acidic medium as \(\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}\)) or \(+4\) (in neutral/faintly alkaline medium as \(\mathrm{MnO}_2\)). Its oxidation state does not change from \(+2\) to \(+7\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
A is true, but R is false.

answer.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AR_REDOXREACTIONS_AR_Q31 - Decomposition of hydrogen peroxide as disproportionation

questiontext.text:
In the following question a statement of assertion (A) followed by a statement of reason (R) is given. Choose the correct option out of the choices given below.

Assertion (A) : The decomposition of hydrogen peroxide to form water and oxygen is an example of disproportionation reaction.

Reason (R) : The oxygen of peroxide is in \(-1\) oxidation state and it is converted to zero oxidation state in \(\mathrm{O}_2\) and \(-2\) oxidation state in \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A disproportionation reaction is one in which a single element in an intermediate oxidation state is simultaneously oxidised to a higher oxidation state and reduced to a lower oxidation state.

Step 2: Evaluation
In the decomposition reaction \(2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{aq}) \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(l) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g})\), oxygen in \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2\) is in the \(-1\) oxidation state. It is simultaneously oxidised to \(0\) in \(\mathrm{O}_2\) and reduced to \(-2\) in \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\). Thus, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) directly explains why the reaction is a disproportionation reaction.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

answer.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AR_REDOXREACTIONS_AR_Q32 - Definition and examples of redox couple

questiontext.text:
In the following question a statement of assertion (A) followed by a statement of reason (R) is given. Choose the correct option out of the choices given below.

Assertion (A) : Redox couple is the combination of oxidised and reduced form of a substance involved in an oxidation or reduction half cell.

Reason (R) : In the representation \(\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}/\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}}^{\ominus}\) and \(\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}/\mathrm{Cu}}^{\ominus}\), \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}/\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\) and \(\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}/\mathrm{Cu}\) are redox couples.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A redox couple consists of the oxidised and reduced forms of the same substance taking part in an oxidation or reduction half-reaction, conventionally written as \(\text{oxidised form}/\text{reduced form}\).

Step 2: Evaluation
Assertion (A) is true because it accurately defines a redox couple.
Reason (R) is also true because \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}/\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\) and \(\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}/\mathrm{Cu}\) are valid examples of redox couples.
However, Reason (R) only provides specific examples of redox couples and does not explain why a redox couple is defined as the combination of oxidised and reduced forms in a half-cell.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

answer.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q01 - Identifying reaction that is not redox

questiontext.text:
Which of the following is not an example of redox reaction?

নিচের কোনটি জারণ-বিজারণ (রেডক্স) বিক্রিয়ার উদাহরণ নয়?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A redox reaction is a chemical reaction in which there is a simultaneous change in the oxidation numbers of at least two species—one undergoes oxidation (increase in oxidation number) and another undergoes reduction (decrease in oxidation number). If no atom changes its oxidation state during the reaction, it is not a redox reaction.

Step 2: Evaluation
In \(\mathrm{CuO} + \mathrm{H}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cu} + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\), the oxidation number of \(\mathrm{Cu}\) decreases from \(+2\) to \(0\) (reduction) and that of \(\mathrm{H}\) increases from \(0\) to \(+1\) (oxidation).
In \(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3 + 3\mathrm{CO} \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{Fe} + 3\mathrm{CO}_2\), the oxidation number of \(\mathrm{Fe}\) decreases from \(+3\) to \(0\) (reduction) and that of \(\mathrm{C}\) increases from \(+2\) to \(+4\) (oxidation).
In \(2\mathrm{K} + \mathrm{F}_2 \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{KF}\), the oxidation number of \(\mathrm{K}\) increases from \(0\) to \(+1\) (oxidation) and that of \(\mathrm{F}\) decreases from \(0\) to \(-1\) (reduction).
In \(\mathrm{BaCl}_2 + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4 \longrightarrow \mathrm{BaSO}_4 + 2\mathrm{HCl}\), the oxidation numbers of \(\mathrm{Ba}\) (\(+2\)), \(\mathrm{Cl}\) (\(-1\)), \(\mathrm{H}\) (\(+1\)), \(\mathrm{S}\) (\(+6\)), and \(\mathrm{O}\) (\(-2\)) remain unchanged on both sides.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, \(\mathrm{BaCl}_2 + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4 \longrightarrow \mathrm{BaSO}_4 + 2\mathrm{HCl}\) is a double displacement (precipitation) reaction and is not an example of a redox reaction.

ধাপ ১: মূল ধারণা (Conceptual Principle)
রেডক্স বা জারণ-বিজারণ বিক্রিয়া হলো এমন একটি রাসায়নিক বিক্রিয়া যেখানে অন্তত দুটি প্রজাতির জারণ সংখ্যার যুগপৎ পরিবর্তন ঘটে—একটির জারণ (জারণ সংখ্যা বৃদ্ধি) এবং অন্যটির বিজারণ (জারণ সংখ্যা হ্রাস) হয়। বিক্রিয়ার সময় কোনো পরমাণুর জারণ সংখ্যার পরিবর্তন না হলে সেটি রেডক্স বিক্রিয়া নয়।

ধাপ ২: মূল্যায়ন (Evaluation)
\(\mathrm{CuO} + \mathrm{H}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cu} + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) বিক্রিয়ায় \(\mathrm{Cu}\)-এর জারণ সংখ্যা \(+2\) থেকে কমে \(0\) হয় (বিজারণ) এবং \(\mathrm{H}\)-এর জারণ সংখ্যা \(0\) থেকে বেড়ে \(+1\) হয় (জারণ)।
\(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3 + 3\mathrm{CO} \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{Fe} + 3\mathrm{CO}_2\) বিক্রিয়ায় \(\mathrm{Fe}\)-এর জারণ সংখ্যা \(+3\) থেকে কমে \(0\) হয় (বিজারণ) এবং \(\mathrm{C}\)-এর জারণ সংখ্যা \(+2\) থেকে বেড়ে \(+4\) হয় (জারণ)।
\(2\mathrm{K} + \mathrm{F}_2 \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{KF}\) বিক্রিয়ায় \(\mathrm{K}\)-এর জারণ সংখ্যা \(0\) থেকে বেড়ে \(+1\) হয় (জারণ) এবং \(\mathrm{F}\)-এর জারণ সংখ্যা \(0\) থেকে কমে \(-1\) হয় (বিজারণ)।
